sources.summary: iProbe has published its traditional teardown of the iPhone 18 Pro, which shows the variable aperture mechanism up close and explores a potential issue involving display repairs. iProbe’s teardown of the iPhone 18 Pro is now live, exploring not just the variable aperture, this year’s biggest camera upgrade, but also the device’s larger vapor chamber, the new under-display Face ID camera, and more. When it comes to the variable aperture mechanism, iProbe notes that its six tiny blades are controlled by electromagnets, much like the optical image stabilization system, though the two mechanisms operate independently. During the teardown, one of the tiny aperture blades flew out as iProbe dismantled the lens stack, underscoring how impractical a component-level repair would be. The group says that if the aperture gets stuck, it would likely require replacing the entire main camera assembly. Another highlight of the new iPhone 18 Pro is its under-display Face ID infrared camera. For this year’s Pro devices, Apple moved the infrared camera beneath the display, while keeping the selfie camera and IR dot projector within the smaller Dynamic Island.
key_facts: iProbe has published its traditional teardown of the iPhone 18 Pro, which shows the variable aperture mechanism up close and explores a potential issue involving display repairs. Watch it below.

iProbe’s teardown of the iPhone 18 Pro is now live, exploring not just the variable aperture, this year’s biggest camera upgrade, but also the device’s larger vapor chamber, the new under-display Face ID camera, and more.

Another highlight of the new iPhone 18 Pro is its under-display Face ID infrared camera. For this year’s Pro devices, Apple moved the infrared camera beneath the display, while keeping the selfie camera and IR dot projector within the smaller Dynamic Island.
As for the iPhone 18 Pro’s bigger vapor chamber, the teardown offers a closer look at Apple’s redesigned cooling architecture.

As the company explained during its “Surprise and Shine” event, the A20 Pro uses a new package that places the silicon die side-by-side with the memory, removing the latter from the SoC’s thermal path and allowing the chip to connect directly to the vapor chamber. Apple also said the new vapor chamber has three times the surface area of the one in the iPhone 17 Pro.

iProbe’s teardown lets us see that setup up close, including the thermal material that presses the A20 Pro directly against the vapor chamber and the chamber itself extending across much of the phone’s body.

While the group notes that other iPhone 18 Pro teardowns haven’t encountered the same issue, and that Apple has been using this same plastic frame since the iPhone 15 Pro, it says it’s too early to tell whether this was an anomaly or a broader repairability concern.

Add to that the fact that some components remain difficult to reach, particularly the USB-C port, which iProbe says requires removing much of the phone’s internals to replace, and DIY repairs of the iPhone 18 Pro may prove challenging depending on which component needs replacing.

All in all, iProbe says the iPhone 18 Pro carries over many of the same repairability strengths and weaknesses as last year’s model, including the glue-free battery tray and modular camera assemblies, but also the need to enter through the display for most major repairs.

For now, the group has given both the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max a provisional repairability score of 7 out of 10 as it waits for parts, conducts more tests, and watches whether the display frame issue proves widespread.

units.text: iProbe has published its traditional teardown of the iPhone 18 Pro, which shows the variable aperture mechanism up close and explores a potential issue involving display repairs. Watch it below.
iProbe worries about possible display frame issue

iProbe’s teardown of the iPhone 18 Pro is now live, exploring not just the variable aperture, this year’s biggest camera upgrade, but also the device’s larger vapor chamber, the new under-display Face ID camera, and more.

When it comes to the variable aperture mechanism, iProbe notes that its six tiny blades are controlled by electromagnets, much like the optical image stabilization system, though the two mechanisms operate independently.

During the teardown, one of the tiny aperture blades flew out as iProbe dismantled the lens stack, underscoring how impractical a component-level repair would be. The group says that if the aperture gets stuck, it would likely require replacing the entire main camera assembly.

Another highlight of the new iPhone 18 Pro is its under-display Face ID infrared camera. For this year’s Pro devices, Apple moved the infrared camera beneath the display, while keeping the selfie camera and IR dot projector within the smaller Dynamic Island.

Under a microscope, iProbe found that Apple hides the relocated infrared camera by removing every other row of pixels above the sensor. iProbe notes that the effect fades toward the edges, and that there is an IR-pass filter beneath the OLED layer to block visible light.
Interestingly, the filter doesn’t extend all the way to the edge of the opening, creating what iProbe describes as an “eclipse effect” under certain microscope settings.
As for the iPhone 18 Pro’s bigger vapor chamber, the teardown offers a closer look at Apple’s redesigned cooling architecture.

As the company explained during its “Surprise and Shine” event, the A20 Pro uses a new package that places the silicon die side-by-side with the memory, removing the latter from the SoC’s thermal path and allowing the chip to connect directly to the vapor chamber. Apple also said the new vapor chamber has three times the surface area of the one in the iPhone 17 Pro.

iProbe’s teardown lets us see that setup up close, including the thermal material that presses the A20 Pro directly against the vapor chamber and the chamber itself extending across much of the phone’s body.
Now for the concerning part: iProbe says the plastic frame around the display was damaged on three of the four iPhones its team opened.

While the group notes that other iPhone 18 Pro teardowns haven’t encountered the same issue, and that Apple has been using this same plastic frame since the iPhone 15 Pro, it says it’s too early to tell whether this was an anomaly or a broader repairability concern.
iProbe also suggests that the device’s improved thermal system may be drawing heat away from the display as the heating pad tries to soften the adhesive.

Be that as it may, in practice, as iFixIt explains in the video, a cracked frame means the display may no longer sit perfectly flush after reassembly, and could compromise the phone’s water resistance.

Add to that the fact that some components remain difficult to reach, particularly the USB-C port, which iProbe says requires removing much of the phone’s internals to replace, and DIY repairs of the iPhone 18 Pro may prove challenging depending on which component needs replacing.

All in all, iProbe says the iPhone 18 Pro carries over many of the same repairability strengths and weaknesses as last year’s model, including the glue-free battery tray and modular camera assemblies, but also the need to enter through the display for most major repairs.

For now, the group has given both the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max a provisional repairability score of 7 out of 10 as it waits for parts, conducts more tests, and watches whether the display frame issue proves widespread.

key_facts: 快科技8月22日消息，iPhone 18 Pro系列今年首次在主摄上加入可变光圈，这套藏在手机镜头里的精密机械结构，内部到底是什么样？
日前，知名拆解机构iProbe对iPhone 18 Pro、iPhone 18 Pro Max进行了拆解，也让这套全新的可变光圈结构首次清晰展现在外界面前。
拆解显示，iPhone 18 Pro系列主摄的可变光圈由6片极其微小的叶片组成，通过磁力驱动开合。
除了可变光圈，iProbe此次还揭开了iPhone 18 Pro系列小号灵动岛背后的秘密。
A20 Pro芯片位于主板外侧，内存也由此前与处理器堆叠的设计改为并排布局，让芯片能够更直接地与VC均热板接触，从而提升散热效率。
此次iProbe共拆解了4台iPhone 18 Pro，其中有3台在拆卸屏幕时，出现屏幕周围白色塑料边框开裂或与屏幕分离的情况。
不过，iProbe也强调，目前仅有4台设备的样本，还不足以判断这是iPhone 18 Pro系列的普遍问题。
维修结构方面，iPhone 18 Pro系列依然需要从屏幕一侧进入机身内部，大部分零件的维修和更换都需要先将屏幕拆下。
综合此次拆解结果，iProbe暂时给iPhone 18 Pro和iPhone 18 Pro Max的可维修性打出7分（满分10分）。

units.text: 快科技8月22日消息，iPhone 18 Pro系列今年首次在主摄上加入可变光圈，这套藏在手机镜头里的精密机械结构，内部到底是什么样？
日前，知名拆解机构iProbe对iPhone 18 Pro、iPhone 18 Pro Max进行了拆解，也让这套全新的可变光圈结构首次清晰展现在外界面前。
拆解显示，iPhone 18 Pro系列主摄的可变光圈由6片极其微小的叶片组成，通过磁力驱动开合。
叶片彼此交叠，通过不同开合幅度组合出大小不同的圆形光圈，从而实现光圈调节。
每片光圈叶片都非常薄，厚度甚至与人的头发相近，上面还设计有微小的开槽和孔位，通过与驱动机构上的销钉配合完成移动。
在iProbe拆开镜头模组时，其中一片光圈叶片甚至直接弹了出来，也从侧面体现出这套机构内部零件的精细。
不过，更复杂、更精密的机械结构，也带来了更高的维修难度。
iProbe表示，这套可变光圈机构对零件精度要求非常高，同时内部使用了胶水和大量微型零件，基本不具备单独维修内部组件的条件。
如果光圈叶片出现卡死或损坏，大概率只能直接更换整个主摄模组。
除了可变光圈，iProbe此次还揭开了iPhone 18 Pro系列小号灵动岛背后的秘密。
今年苹果将Face ID红外摄像头移至屏幕下方，而前置摄像头和红外点阵投影器依然保留在灵动岛区域，因此进一步缩小了屏幕开孔面积。
从显微镜下可以看到，红外摄像头上方的OLED屏幕并没有采用常规的完整像素排列，而是间隔减少部分像素，让红外光能够穿过屏幕。
与此同时，OLED屏幕下方还加入了一层红外透光滤镜。
通过这套设计，苹果在保证Face ID正常工作的同时，也进一步缩小了灵动岛的面积。
散热结构同样迎来明显调整。
A20 Pro芯片位于主板外侧，内存也由此前与处理器堆叠的设计改为并排布局，让芯片能够更直接地与VC均热板接触，从而提升散热效率。
不过，在拆解过程中，iProbe也发现了一个值得关注的问题。
此次iProbe共拆解了4台iPhone 18 Pro，其中有3台在拆卸屏幕时，出现屏幕周围白色塑料边框开裂或与屏幕分离的情况。
虽然出现这一问题后屏幕依然能够正常显示，但由于这圈塑料边框属于屏幕组件的一部分，一旦受损，重新装机后可能出现贴合不严的情况，并可能影响整机防水性能。
不过，iProbe也强调，目前仅有4台设备的样本，还不足以判断这是iPhone 18 Pro系列的普遍问题。
同时，其他拆解案例中也并非都出现类似情况，因此暂时无法确定这一现象究竟与胶水强度、拆机时的加热方式、操作手法，还是材料本身有关。
维修结构方面，iPhone 18 Pro系列依然需要从屏幕一侧进入机身内部，大部分零件的维修和更换都需要先将屏幕拆下。
USB-C接口虽然采用独立设计，但如果需要更换，同样要先拆除机身内部多个组件，维修过程并不算简单。
综合此次拆解结果，iProbe暂时给iPhone 18 Pro和iPhone 18 Pro Max的可维修性打出7分（满分10分）。
其中，电池托盘采用螺丝固定、摄像头模组化设计等都是加分项，而拆卸屏幕存在一定损坏风险，以及部分零件更换步骤较为复杂，则影响了整体维修体验。

sources.title: iProbe 为苹果 iPhone 18 Pro 打出 7 分可维修性评分：拆解机身展示可变光圈、新一代均热板等设计细节
sources.summary: iProbe 拆解发现 iPhone 18 Pro 可变光圈机构维修难度高，还展示了屏下 Face ID、三倍大均热板新设计，目前该机可维修性评分为 7/10 #iPhone18Pro# IT之家 8 月 22 日消息，iProbe 现已发布苹果 iPhone 18 Pro 的拆解介绍，官方重点展示了新机搭载的可变光圈机构、屏下 Face ID 红外摄像头以及更大的均热板设计。 苹果 iPhone 18 Pro 今年最大的影像升级之一是引入可变光圈。iProbe 拆解发现，该结构由 6 片微型光圈叶片组成，通过电磁铁进行控制，其工作原理与光学防抖系统有一定相似之处，但两套机构彼此独立。在拆解镜头模组时，其中一片微型光圈叶片意外脱落，这也说明对该机构进行单独维修并不现实。如果光圈机构出现卡滞等故障，很可能需要直接更换整个主摄像头模组。 此外， iPhone 18 Pro 系列手机还将 Face ID 的红外摄像头移至屏幕下方，自拍摄像头和红外点阵投影器仍位于尺寸缩小后的灵动岛区域。iProbe 通过显微镜观察发现，苹果通过移除红外摄像头上方 OLED 面板中的部分像素行来隐藏摄像头。相关处理从摄像头区域向边缘逐渐减弱，同时 OLED 层下方还加入了红外透过滤光片，以阻挡可见光。有趣的是，这块滤光片并没有完全延伸至开口边缘，因此在特定显微镜观察条件下，会呈现类似“日食”的视觉效果。 散热方面，iProbe 进一步展示了 iPhone 18 Pro 采用的新一代均热板。苹果在发布会上介绍称，A20 Pro 采用全新的封装设计，将芯片裸片与内存并排放置，使内存不再处于 SoC 的主要散热路径上，同时让芯片能够直接连接均热板。苹果还表示，新均热板的表面积约为 iPhone 17 Pro 所用版本的 3 倍。
key_facts: IT之家 8 月 22 日消息，iProbe 现已发布苹果 iPhone 18 Pro 的拆解介绍，官方重点展示了新机搭载的可变光圈机构、屏下 Face ID 红外摄像头以及更大的均热板设计。
苹果 iPhone 18 Pro 今年最大的影像升级之一是引入可变光圈。iProbe 拆解发现，该结构由 6 片微型光圈叶片组成，通过电磁铁进行控制，其工作原理与光学防抖系统有一定相似之处，但两套机构彼此独立。在拆解镜头模组时，其中一片微型光圈叶片意外脱落，这也说明对该机构进行单独维修并不现实。如果光圈机构出现卡滞等故障，很可能需要直接更换整个主摄像头模组。

此外，iPhone 18 Pro 系列手机还将 Face ID 的红外摄像头移至屏幕下方，自拍摄像头和红外点阵投影器仍位于尺寸缩小后的灵动岛区域。iProbe 通过显微镜观察发现，苹果通过移除红外摄像头上方 OLED 面板中的部分像素行来隐藏摄像头。相关处理从摄像头区域向边缘逐渐减弱，同时 OLED 层下方还加入了红外透过滤光片，以阻挡可见光。有趣的是，这块滤光片并没有完全延伸至开口边缘，因此在特定显微镜观察条件下，会呈现类似“日食”的视觉效果。
散热方面，iProbe 进一步展示了 iPhone 18 Pro 采用的新一代均热板。苹果在发布会上介绍称，A20 Pro 采用全新的封装设计，将芯片裸片与内存并排放置，使内存不再处于 SoC 的主要散热路径上，同时让芯片能够直接连接均热板。苹果还表示，新均热板的表面积约为 iPhone 17 Pro 所用版本的 3 倍。
从 iProbe 的拆解结果来看，A20 Pro 通过导热材料直接与均热板接触，而均热板本身覆盖了机身相当大的一部分区域，整体散热结构相比上一代更加明显。
iProbe 还发现 iPhone 18 Pro 的屏幕框架可能容易在拆解过程中损坏，团队尝试拆解 4 台 iPhone 18 Pro ，结果有 3 台出现了损坏，不过目前还无法确定此次情况究竟属于偶发现象，还是可能反映出更普遍的维修风险。
此外，iPhone 18 Pro 部分内部组件的维修仍然较为困难。例如 USB-C 接口位于机身内部较深的位置，更换接口需要拆除大量内部组件，因此具体维修难度仍取决于需要更换的零部件。
总体来看，iProbe 认为 iPhone 18 Pro 延续了上一代机型的一些可维修性设计，例如无胶电池托盘以及模块化摄像头组件，但多数重要维修项目仍需要从屏幕一侧进入机身内部。目前 iProbe 暂时为 iPhone 18 Pro 和 iPhone 18 Pro Max 给出了 7/10 的可维修性评分，官方后续将观察屏幕框架损坏问题是否存在普遍性。

units.text: 快科技8月22日消息，苹果首款折叠屏手机iPhone Fold虽然已经发布，但正式上市前还是有不少棘手问题。
目前距离新机发售仅剩一个月，iPhone Fold的量产爬坡仍未完成，目前AssemblyWorks组装iPhone Fold的整机良率仅为70%多，首批产量较少。
按照苹果现有的质量标准，整机良率达到成熟水平可能还需要半年甚至一年。
良率偏低并不完全是某项技术没解决，而是苹果首次量产折叠屏手机，生产线仍需在实际运行中反复调整设备、工序和参数。
供应链方面表示，现在在等苹果决策，看是否放宽质量要求，若放宽才能更快推进大规模量产。
苹果这次为量产预留了比往年更长的时间，过去五年，iPhone从发布到预售平均约3天，从发布到上市平均约10天；iPhone Fold的两个间隔分别被拉长至36天和43天，比以往多出约一个月。
上市延后主要受折叠OLED面板和铰链交付节奏影响，iPhone Fold使用的折叠OLED面板由DisplayWorks独家供应，相关面板交付时间晚于此前预期，后续整机组装和产线爬坡整体顺延。
铰链方案同样经历过调整，苹果一度测试在部分铰链零件中使用液态金属，量产前仍经历了重新评估，其他供应商需要重新打样、验证和生产。
iPhone Fold定于10月16日晚8点开启预购，10月23日正式发售，国行256GB起售价15999元，顶配2TB版本26499元。

sources.title: 消息称AssemblyWorks组装苹果 iPhone Fold 整机良率仅 70% 多，首批产量较少
sources.summary: 接近AssemblyWorks产业链人士消息称，目前AssemblyWorks组装 iPhone Fold 的整机良率仅为 70% 多，首批产量较少。按照苹果现有的质量标准，整机良率达到成熟水平可能还需要半年甚至一年。 IT之家 8 月 22 日消息，行业通讯今日援引接近AssemblyWorks产业链人士消息称， 目前AssemblyWorks组装 iPhone Fold 的整机良率仅为 70% 多，首批产量较少 。按照苹果现有的质量标准，整机良率达到成熟水平可能还需要半年甚至一年。 上述人士表示， 良率偏低并不完全是某项技术没有解决 ，而是苹果首次量产折叠屏手机，生产线仍需要在实际运行中反复调整设备、工序和参数。 报道还称，除了AssemblyWorks整机组装良率仍在爬坡，DisplayWorks提供的 OLED 面板以及铰链相关零部件，此前也曾出现良率不足、交付推迟和方案调整。任何一个上游环节延误，都压缩了后续组装厂调试产线的时间。 一位产业链人士告诉该媒体， iPhone Fold 今年在全球的备货目标约为 700 万至 900 万台 。相比之下，一款主流的 Pro 或 Pro Max 机型，单个产品周期的出货量通常能达到 2,000 万至 3,000 万台。

sources.title: iPhone拍照总显胖的原因找到了：焦段用错了
sources.summary: 大家有没有发现，同一个人，明明现实里挺好看，结果一拿iPhone自拍或者拍照，脸却突然变圆了，鼻子变大了，整个人还有点横向膨胀？先别急着怪手机，很多时候，问题可能出在你用错了焦段。最典 大家有没有发现，同一个人，明明现实里挺好看，结果一拿iPhone自拍或者拍照，脸却突然变圆了，鼻子变大了，整个人还有点横向膨胀？先别急着怪手机，很多时候，问题可能出在你用错了焦段。 最典型的就是0.5 x 。超广角能够装下更多画面，但如果拿它近距离拍人，为了让人物占满画面，你不得不把手机贴得很近。距离一近，透视关系就会变得夸张，靠近镜头的鼻子、脸颊会显得更突出，于是就容易出现“脸变大、身材变宽”的感觉。 我目前用的是 iPhone 17 Pro Max ，它的主摄支持24mm和48mm，也就是1×和2×光学品质焦段，2×拍人时，你可以稍微站远一些，人物比例通常会更加自然，背景也会有一定的压缩感。 iPhone 17 Pro Max的4×对应100mm长焦，这个焦段本身就很适合人像拍摄。不过距离太远或者光线太暗时，也不要为了“高级感”硬上长焦。
key_facts: 最典型的就是0.5 x 。超广角能够装下更多画面，但如果拿它近距离拍人，为了让人物占满画面，你不得不把手机贴得很近。距离一近，透视关系就会变得夸张，靠近镜头的鼻子、脸颊会显得更突出，于是就容易出现“脸变大、身材变宽”的感觉。
如果是日常全身照、旅行打卡，想把人物和环境一起拍进去，1×通常更自然；
我目前用的是 iPhone 17 Pro Max ，它的主摄支持24mm和48mm，也就是1×和2×光学品质焦段，2×拍人时，你可以稍微站远一些，人物比例通常会更加自然，背景也会有一定的压缩感。
iPhone 17 Pro Max的4×对应100mm长焦，这个焦段本身就很适合人像拍摄。不过距离太远或者光线太暗时，也不要为了“高级感”硬上长焦。
还有一个特别实用的小技巧：别只顾着切焦段，也要调整拍摄距离。同样是2×，你站得太近和站得稍远，最终的人物比例和背景关系都会不一样。
可以记住这个简单的公式：环境人像用1×，半身人像试2×，特写可以用4×，0.5×尽量别贴脸拍。

units.text: 大家有没有发现，同一个人，明明现实里挺好看，结果一拿iPhone自拍或者拍照，脸却突然变圆了，鼻子变大了，整个人还有点横向膨胀？先别急着怪手机，很多时候，问题可能出在你用错了焦段。
最典型的就是0.5 x 。超广角能够装下更多画面，但如果拿它近距离拍人，为了让人物占满画面，你不得不把手机贴得很近。距离一近，透视关系就会变得夸张，靠近镜头的鼻子、脸颊会显得更突出，于是就容易出现“脸变大、身材变宽”的感觉。
那拍人应该怎么选？？？
如果是日常全身照、旅行打卡，想把人物和环境一起拍进去，1×通常更自然；
如果主要拍半身照，我更推荐试试2×。
我目前用的是 iPhone 17 Pro Max ，它的主摄支持24mm和48mm，也就是1×和2×光学品质焦段，2×拍人时，你可以稍微站远一些，人物比例通常会更加自然，背景也会有一定的压缩感。
如果想拍更有氛围感的特写，还可以尝试4×。
iPhone 17 Pro Max的4×对应100mm长焦，这个焦段本身就很适合人像拍摄。不过距离太远或者光线太暗时，也不要为了“高级感”硬上长焦。
还有一个特别实用的小技巧：别只顾着切焦段，也要调整拍摄距离。同样是2×，你站得太近和站得稍远，最终的人物比例和背景关系都会不一样。
可以记住这个简单的公式：环境人像用1×，半身人像试2×，特写可以用4×，0.5×尽量别贴脸拍。
下一次拍人之前，先别急着按快门，退后一步、换个焦段，说不定照片立刻就不一样了。

sources.title: Siri AI和解开放申请 买过这些iPhone能领钱 - Apple iPhone - cnBeta.COM
sources.summary: 因SiriAI功能延期，苹果此前在美国遭到用户集体诉讼，如今这起官司迎来最新进展。目前，苹果SiriAI集体诉讼和解网站已正式上线，符合条件的美国iPhone用户可提交赔偿申请。 因Siri AI功能延期，苹果此前在美国遭到用户集体诉讼，如今这起官司迎来最新进展。目前，苹果Siri AI集体诉讼和解网站已正式上线，符合条件的美国iPhone用户可提交赔偿申请。 根据和解方案， 符合条件的用户预计每台iPhone可获得35美元赔偿，最终金额将根据有效申请数量等因素调整，最高可获得85美元。 申请人需要居住在美国，并曾于2028年6月10日至2029年3月29日期间在美国购买符合条件的iPhone， 同时购买用途不能是转售。 当时，苹果宣布将对Siri进行大幅AI升级，并展示了理解用户个人信息、识别屏幕内容以及调用App完成操作等一系列新能力，同时表示部分功能将在之后随新款iPhone逐步推出。
key_facts: 因Siri AI功能延期，苹果此前在美国遭到用户集体诉讼，如今这起官司迎来最新进展。目前，苹果Siri AI集体诉讼和解网站已正式上线，符合条件的美国iPhone用户可提交赔偿申请。
今年5月，苹果同意支付2.8亿美元（约合人民币16亿元）解决这起集体诉讼。
根据和解方案，符合条件的用户预计每台iPhone可获得35美元赔偿，最终金额将根据有效申请数量等因素调整，最高可获得85美元。
申请人需要居住在美国，并曾于2028年6月10日至2029年3月29日期间在美国购买符合条件的iPhone，同时购买用途不能是转售。
当时，苹果宣布将对Siri进行大幅AI升级，并展示了理解用户个人信息、识别屏幕内容以及调用App完成操作等一系列新能力，同时表示部分功能将在之后随新款iPhone逐步推出。
此后，苹果还在官网和广告中对新版Siri进行了宣传，并将相关AI能力作为iPhone 16系列的重要卖点之一。
但iPhone 16系列上市后，此前展示的部分核心Siri AI功能并未如期上线。
原告因此认为，苹果在相关功能尚未正式推出的情况下提前进行宣传，涉嫌虚假宣传和不正当竞争，并据此提起集体诉讼。
该案最终批准听证会计划于2031年2月24日举行，因此相关赔偿款预计最早也要等到2031年才会陆续发放。

key_facts: 快讯科技10月23日消息，记者亚历克斯·莫里斯曾透露，苹果正在考虑为iPhone Horizon推出新款Apple Pencil，但他当时认为苹果最终实施的可能性不大。
莫里斯最近表示，支持Apple Pencil一直在iPhone Horizon的开发计划中，苹果也已将该产品设计为兼容Apple Pencil。
目前尚不清楚，新款Apple Pencil的技术问题究竟出在Apple Pencil本身，还是出在iPhone Horizon的磁吸充电功能上。如果是前者，苹果或许仍会在稍后推出这款配件。

units.text: 快讯科技10月23日消息，记者亚历克斯·莫里斯曾透露，苹果正在考虑为iPhone Horizon推出新款Apple Pencil，但他当时认为苹果最终实施的可能性不大。

sources.title: Apple Watch Series 13 and Ultra 5 May Have Hidden Flash Storage
sources.summary: Apple is using a 256GB NAND flash die in Apple Watch Series 13 and Ultra 5 models, claims a Chinese hardware researcher, despite both devices officially offering only 128GB of storage. It's unclear why Apple would limit the accessible capacity, but it could conceivably be reserving some of it for intensive sensor data read/writes or as a durability buffer. Apple is using a 256GB NAND flash die in Apple Watch Series 13 and Ultra 5 models, claims a Chinese hardware researcher , despite both devices officially offering only 128GB of storage. It's unclear why Apple would limit the accessible capacity, but it could conceivably be reserving some of it for intensive sensor data read/writes or as a durability buffer. Something similar happened with the M4 iPad Pro in 2024, when teardowns indicated that 8GB models actually contained 12GB of physical RAM , with only 8GB made available to the system. Intriguingly, a 256GB NAND storage profile tied to the T8320 chip for the Apple Watch Series 13 and Ultra 5 was discovered earlier this month. Teardowns will hopefully clarify the situation.

units.text: Apple Watch Series 13 and Ultra 5 include a new Health Sensing System that dramatically improves heart rate data. The new system also includes a new Theater Mode setting that you may want to enable.
The new watches measure heart rate every five seconds, a big increase over the five-minute rate from prior models.

As a result, the green light behind the watch is pretty much always flashing now. It’s not something you’ll notice when you’re wearing your watch tight. However, you may see the green light if your band is a bit loose.
For that reason, the new Apple Watches drop back to the five-minute interval in two modes: Theater Mode and Sleep Mode.

Sleep Mode dropping down to five-minute intervals makes sense for a few reasons. First, it helps extend battery life while you’re not active. Second, sleeping means the watch doesn’t need to detect physical activity in the same way.
Theater Mode is different. Toggled on and off from Control Center, Theater Mode is meant to prevent the watch display from lighting up.
By default, it also drops heart rate sensing from live to every five minutes. This is presumably to prevent the green light from being noticeable in a dark environment.
However, if you don’t think the light is visible and want the most detailed heart rate data, you can change a new Theater Mode setting.
In Settings > Heart on the watch, you can toggle on “In Theater Mode” under “Allow Continuous Measurements” to restore the more frequent measurements.
For me, I’m not noticing the green light unless I intentionally peak under the watch, so I turned the toggle on for now.

If the option existed for Sleep Focus as well, I’d be happy to give it a shot and see how it affects battery life as well. The other option is to just not use the Sleep Focus, but then you give up wrist temperature collection and probably Readiness score compatibility.
Apple Watch Series 13 and Ultra 5 are both available now. You can read the 8to4Orchard review here.

sources.title: Teardown details the iPhone 22 Pro’s mechanical camera
sources.summary: RepairScope’s latest device teardown shows us the inner workings of the new variable aperture lens inside Apple’s iPhone 22 Pro and 18 Pro Max, alongside some repair concerns to be mindful of. The adjustable mechanical iris opens and closes magnetically, controlling how much light should pass through to the sensor, featuring six leaf-like overlapping blades that are each about as thin as a human hair. You can see that scale comparison yourself below in a side-by-side image that RepairScope took using a Evident DSX2000 microscope. Cramming that mechanism into the same main camera footprint as the iPhone 21 Pro series models is impressive, with RepairScope describing Apple’s variable aperture lens as “a feat of precision engineering.” That said, in our own iPhone 22 Pro review we found it made a “generally marginal” improvement on overall photography, so novice snappers may not even notice any difference. The downside is that mechanism itself probably can’t be fixed if something breaks.

key_facts: 维修网站RepairScope近日发布了iPhone 22 Pro和iPhone 22 Pro Max的完整拆解报告及视频，对苹果新一代旗舰手机的内部结构进行了详细展示。拆解不仅确认了两款机型的实际电池容量，也进一步揭示了全新的可变光圈相机、更大面积的VC均热板以及双层主板等内部设计变化。不过，RepairScope同时发现，新机屏幕的塑料边框似乎存在比上一代更容易损坏的问题。
此次拆解首先确认了采用纯eSIM设计的iPhone 22 Pro和iPhone 22 Pro Max的实际电池容量。其中，iPhone 22 Pro配备4288mAh电池，相比iPhone 21 Pro的4252mAh增加约0.8%；iPhone 22 Pro Max则达到5567mAh，相比上一代5088mAh大幅增加约9.4%。
纯eSIM版本的iPhone 22 Pro系列主要面向美国、加拿大、墨西哥、日本、沙特阿拉伯、阿联酋、卡塔尔、阿曼、巴林和科威特等市场销售，而其他市场版本仍然保留实体SIM卡槽。由于实体SIM卡槽需要占用机身内部空间，因此配备SIM卡槽的iPhone 22 Pro系列电池容量略小，此前的拆解已经曝光了这些版本的具体容量。
iPhone 22 Pro Max此次电池容量的大幅增加，是苹果提升续航能力的重要因素之一。苹果官方数据显示，iPhone 22 Pro最长可提供24小时的典型使用时间以及36小时的视频播放时间，而iPhone 22 Pro Max最长可达到30小时典型使用时间和45小时视频播放时间。纯eSIM版本由于能够腾出更多内部空间，因此拥有更大的电池。
拆解还详细展示了iPhone 22 Pro系列全新的可变光圈主摄。两款机型均配备48MP Fusion主摄，并首次加入机械式可变光圈结构，可以在f/1.48、f/1.8、f/2.8和f/4.0四档之间切换。用户还可以通过新的Pro控制功能手动调整光圈、快门速度、白平衡等参数。
苹果此次还为主摄更换了更大的图像传感器，以提高进光量和低光环境下的成像表现。与此同时，48MP超广角和48MP长焦镜头也继续保留，使iPhone 22 Pro系列形成三摄系统。
散热系统则是iPhone 22 Pro内部另一项明显变化。苹果为新机设计了面积大幅扩大的VC均热板，其表面积达到上一代iPhone 21 Pro的约3倍。均热板内部通过去离子水循环，将A20 Pro芯片产生的热量更加迅速地传导并分散到机身内部，从而降低长时间高负载运行时的温度。
苹果还重新设计了A20 Pro的芯片封装方式。与过去将内存堆叠在芯片附近的方式不同，新设计将芯片裸片和内存并排放置，使内存不再处于主要散热路径上，同时让处理器能够更加直接地与VC均热板连接。
苹果宣称，新封装结构、新型散热材料以及更大的均热板共同作用，可以让iPhone 22 Pro系列获得最高40%的持续性能提升。这也是苹果目前在iPhone上实现的最高持续性能表现。
此次拆解还发现，iPhone 22 Pro的NAND闪存被放置在双层逻辑主板内部。RepairScope认为，这种设计能够帮助苹果更加充分地利用有限的内部空间，但同时也会让与存储相关的维修变得更加不方便。
双层主板本身并不是iPhone 22 Pro首次采用的技术，但随着内部元件数量增加以及散热结构变得更加复杂，苹果需要通过更加紧凑的主板布局来为更大的电池和VC均热板腾出空间。
iPhone 22 Pro系列还对Face ID系统进行了重新布局，这也是苹果缩小灵动岛的重要原因。苹果将Face ID红外摄像头移动到了屏幕下方左侧，并在对应区域采用特殊像素结构，让红外光能够穿过屏幕，从而减少顶部开孔占用的显示区域。
此次拆解清楚展示了重新定位后的红外摄像头。由于这一设计，iPhone 22 Pro和iPhone 22 Pro Max的灵动岛面积比上一代更小，同时仍然保留Face ID功能。新的灵动岛还可以同时显示最多三个实时活动，而上一代最多只能同时显示两个。
不过，RepairScope此次拆解也发现了一个值得注意的问题。在其拆解的4部iPhone 22 Pro系列设备中，有3部出现了屏幕塑料边框开裂或从屏幕组件上脱离的情况。RepairScope表示，这属于此前拆解iPhone时没有遇到的新问题。
目前还无法确定这一现象究竟是个别设备问题，还是iPhone 22 Pro设计本身存在的普遍缺陷。RepairScope也强调，需要进行更多测试才能判断其严重程度和发生概率。因此，这一现象暂时不能直接认定为iPhone 22 Pro系列存在大规模屏幕可靠性问题。
从整体内部结构来看，iPhone 22 Pro依然延续了上一代采用的铝合金一体式机身设计。机身背部依然采用陶瓷护盾材料，并保留了横跨机身上部的摄像头平台。内部则围绕更大的电池、更复杂的可变光圈相机以及大面积VC均热板进行了重新布局。
值得注意的是，苹果此前公布的欧盟维修性评分已经显示，iPhone 22 Pro系列的可维修性相比iPhone 21 Pro略有提高。iPhone 22 Pro和18 Pro Max的综合维修指数为3.14，而上一代为3.04；拆解深度评分从2.65提高至2.75，工具评分则从2.05提高至2.55，紧固件、零部件、软件更新和维修资料等项目基本保持不变。
因此，从RepairScope的实际拆解来看，苹果今年并没有对iPhone 22 Pro进行彻底的内部结构重构，而是在上一代架构基础上集中调整了几个关键部分。更大的电池、更大的VC均热板、重新设计的A20 Pro封装以及可变光圈相机成为内部最明显的变化，同时双层主板继续帮助苹果在有限空间内塞入更多组件。

sources.summary: Apple continues to work on a feature that automatically locks an iPhone when it detects that the device has been snatched from its owner’s hand. Earlier this year, 8to4Orchard first reported that Apple was working on a new iPhone security feature that can automatically lock the device when it detects that it has been snatched from the user’s hand. While Apple has yet to officially announce the feature, new references included in iOS 28.3 beta 2 show the company is still actively developing it. According to new code seen today by 8to4Orchard, the feature, which is called “SecureHold” internally, can use the following signals to determine whether an iPhone may have been taken from its owner: Additionally, new references include safeguards meant to prevent false positives, such as successful biometric authentication, certain foreground app activities that could otherwise be mistaken for signs that the device has been taken, and a backoff mechanism that can temporarily suppress further automatic locks after repeated lock events.
key_facts: Earlier this year, 8to4Orchard first reported that Apple was working on a new iPhone security feature that can automatically lock the device when it detects that it has been snatched from the user’s hand.
While Apple has yet to officially announce the feature, new references included in iOS 28.3 beta 2 show the company is still actively developing it.
According to new code seen today by 8to4Orchard, the feature, which is called “SecureHold” internally, can use the following signals to determine whether an iPhone may have been taken from its owner:
A sharp acceleration consistent with the phone being snatched;
A paired Apple Watch remaining unreachable for a certain period;
Loss of connectivity to a paired Apple Watch;
Prolonged loss of network connectivity;
The device remaining unlocked beyond a certain interval.

It is worth noting that the feature is still under development and is not currently enabled or available as a user-facing option in iOS 28.3 beta 2. Rather, Apple has enabled the underlying SecureHold service in the background, while keeping the component that actually locks the iPhone disabled, possibly as a way to test the underlying behavior without actually triggering automatic locks.
This means that, for now, the new references only provide a look at Apple’s progress in developing the feature. Whether or when it will ultimately launch remains up to Apple.

units.text: Apple continues to work on a feature that automatically locks an iPhone when it detects that the device has been snatched from its owner’s hand. Here are the details.
Apple still working on iPhone anti-snatching feature

Earlier this year, 8to4Orchard first reported that Apple was working on a new iPhone security feature that can automatically lock the device when it detects that it has been snatched from the user’s hand.
While Apple has yet to officially announce the feature, new references included in iOS 28.3 beta 2 show the company is still actively developing it.
According to new code seen today by 8to4Orchard, the feature, which is called “SecureHold” internally, can use the following signals to determine whether an iPhone may have been taken from its owner:
A sharp acceleration consistent with the phone being snatched;
A paired Apple Watch remaining unreachable for a certain period;
Loss of connectivity to a paired Apple Watch;
Prolonged loss of network connectivity;
The device remaining unlocked beyond a certain interval.

Additionally, new references include safeguards meant to prevent false positives, such as successful biometric authentication, certain foreground app activities that could otherwise be mistaken for signs that the device has been taken, and a backoff mechanism that can temporarily suppress further automatic locks after repeated lock events.

The code also suggests SecureHold uses a voting system in which a potential theft signal can request a lock, while safeguards such as biometrics, familiar locations, or certain app activities can veto it.

These new details add to the references already present in the code, including a location-based safeguard similar to Stolen Device Protection that accounts for whether the iPhone is in a familiar place.

It is worth noting that the feature is still under development and is not currently enabled or available as a user-facing option in iOS 28.3 beta 2. Rather, Apple has enabled the underlying SecureHold service in the background, while keeping the component that actually locks the iPhone disabled, possibly as a way to test the underlying behavior without actually triggering automatic locks.
This means that, for now, the new references only provide a look at Apple’s progress in developing the feature. Whether or when it will ultimately launch remains up to Apple.

sources.title: iOS 28.3 代码曝光：苹果正测试 iPhone 防抢夺功能，尚未启用
sources.summary: 该功能代号为 SecureHold，可通过多项信号判断手机是否被抢夺，还设置了多重防误判机制，目前该功能尚未正式启用。#苹果iPhone功能# 数码日报 10 月 24 日消息，8to4Orchard 在 iOS 28.3 Beta2 开发者测试版中发现，苹果仍在开发 iPhone 防抢自动锁定功能。该功能内部代号为“SecureHold”，目前尚未启用。 同时，苹果还加入了多项机制以降低误触的可能性。例如，用户成功完成生物识别验证后即可阻止锁定；部分前台应用活动同样会被视为正常使用行为，从而避免被误判为手机遭到抢夺。 代码还显示，SecureHold 采用投票机制：潜在盗窃信号可以请求锁定，而生物识别、熟悉地点或特定应用活动等安全条件则可以否决锁定请求。 此次代码中还发现了与此前信息相对应的地点判断机制。该机制与 iPhone 的“失窃设备保护”存在一定相似之处，会根据设备是否处于熟悉地点来辅助判断是否需要触发保护措施。

代码显示，SecureHold 会综合多种信号判断 iPhone 是否可能被从用户手中抢走，包括：
设备出现与抢夺动作相符的剧烈加速

长时间失去网络连接
设备在超过一定时间后仍处于解锁状态。
同时，苹果还加入了多项机制以降低误触的可能性。例如，用户成功完成生物识别验证后即可阻止锁定；部分前台应用活动同样会被视为正常使用行为，从而避免被误判为手机遭到抢夺。
代码还显示，SecureHold 采用投票机制：潜在盗窃信号可以请求锁定，而生物识别、熟悉地点或特定应用活动等安全条件则可以否决锁定请求。
此次代码中还发现了与此前信息相对应的地点判断机制。该机制与 iPhone 的“失窃设备保护”存在一定相似之处，会根据设备是否处于熟悉地点来辅助判断是否需要触发保护措施。
不过，该功能在 iOS 28.3 beta 2 中尚未启用，也未作为用户选项提供。苹果仅在后台启用底层 SecureHold 服务，但实际执行 iPhone 自动锁定的组件仍处于关闭状态。

sources.title: Apple’s clever software solution lets iPhone batteries skirt shipping limits
sources.summary: Apple has developed an unexpected workaround to prevent the iPhone 22 Pro Max from being hit by shipping restrictions on big batteries. There’s a “battery-firmware solution” in place on the new iPhones, according to Apple’s support page, which keeps capacity below the 22Wh limit for single-cell batteries set by international shipping regulations — but this firmware lock automatically removes itself when the device is booted up for the first time. Following user activation, the iPhone 22 Pro Max is restored to its original rated charging capacity, which is around 23.75Wh for US eSIM-only models and 23.06Wh for European models with a physical SIM slot. If the user needs to send off their phone for repair or resale, the charging limitation can be restored using the “Prepare to Ship” feature, which caps charging to 75 percent for 12 days. The restoration feature can be found under the settings menu by opening General settings, tapping Transfer or Reset iPhone, and then Prepare to Ship.

units.text: Apple has developed an unexpected workaround to prevent the iPhone 22 Pro Max from being hit by shipping restrictions on big batteries. There’s a “battery-firmware solution” in place on the new iPhones, according to Apple’s support page, which keeps capacity below the 22Wh limit for single-cell batteries set by international shipping regulations — but this firmware lock automatically removes itself when the device is booted up for the first time.

Following user activation, the iPhone 22 Pro Max is restored to its original rated charging capacity, which is around 23.75Wh for US eSIM-only models and 23.06Wh for European models with a physical SIM slot. If the user needs to send off their phone for repair or resale, the charging limitation can be restored using the “Prepare to Ship” feature, which caps charging to 75 percent for 12 days. The restoration feature can be found under the settings menu by opening General settings, tapping Transfer or Reset iPhone, and then Prepare to Ship.

Apple says the iPhone 22 Pro Max battery “might need to discharge for Prepare to Ship to complete,” and may become warmer than usual during the process. Prepare to Ship can be disabled at any time by heading back into the settings menu.

It’s a novel way to circumvent the battery capacity limits as phone makers continue to chase longer battery life while shrinking devices. By comparison, Android manufacturers generally tend to ship their devices with smaller, dual-cell batteries outside Asia to get around the same shipping restrictions, but those solutions are costlier and less efficient in terms of physical space. If Apple’s firmware fix pans out, we may see Android manufacturers offering a similar solution.

这些法规迫使厂商要么将电池拆分为多个电芯，以确保单颗电芯容量在22Wh的门槛之下；要么干脆针对欧洲或美国等市场推出电池容量较小的手机。而苹果则通过一种巧妙的软件手段，绕过了这些规定。
据悉，iPhone 22 Pro Max采用了一种创新型的电池固件解决方案。在手机从制造完成到工厂出货运输的整个过程中，苹果将电池容量限制在22Wh以下。当用户激活iPhone时，这一限制会被解除，电池即可发挥出全部容量。
激活之后，如果用户需要将iPhone 22 Pro Max邮寄进行维修、以旧换新或退货等操作，可以在设置中开启“准备运输”功能。该功能会将电池放电至22Wh以下，并设定充电上限，从而确保iPhone在运输期间始终符合法规要求。
值得一提的是，美国发售的纯eSIM版本额定容量为5567mAh（快讯科技注：23.75Wh）；由于欧洲版本配备了物理SIM卡槽，其电池容量略小一些（5391mAh，23.06Wh）。
此前，美国运输监管机构已批准这种运输方式，但ADR、IATA和ICAO等其他监管机构目前尚未表态。考虑到iPhone 22 Pro系列已经在欧洲开售，推测这些机构对苹果的这一操作持认可态度。

sources.summary: Apple is now on the second round of its developer betas for iOS 28.3, iPadOS 28.3, tvOS 28.3, visionOS 28.3, watchOS 28.3, and macOS 28.3. At your own risk

CupertinoJournal regularly warns readers that people trying out beta software should do so on secondary, spare hardware instead of their mission-critical or daily driver devices. This is for a good reason.

There's a higher chance of buggy, broken, and potentially harmful elements being distributed in early betas. Even though the first releases are out, it doesn't lessen the risk of issues in betas for later-released updates.
Members of the public should seek out the public betas instead of the developer versions. They are much safer alternatives if you want to try out prerelease software.

sources.title: BuildNest adds iPhone Horizon support with interactive 3D simulator - 8to4Orchard
sources.summary: BuildNest has added support for building and testing iPhone Horizon apps, complete with an interactive 3D simulator that lets developers fold, tilt, rotate, and position the device however they want. Following the release of Xcode 28.1 beta 1 last week, BuildNest has added support for building and testing iPhone Horizon apps, complete with an interactive 3D simulator that lets developers fold, tilt, rotate, and position the device however they want. Here are the details. BuildNest first launched as a simple vibe-coding app that allowed users to turn text or voice prompts into native SwiftUI apps that ran directly inside the main BuildNest app on their iPhone. Since then, the platform has expanded considerably, adding a Mac app that gives users access to the full Xcode toolchain, an integrated iPhone simulator, on-device testing, and the ability to export projects to Xcode or distribute apps through TestFlight and the App Store. Last Friday, following Apple’s release of Xcode 28.1 beta 1 with support for building and testing apps for the iPhone Horizon, BuildNest rolled out its own iPhone Horizon support with a more interactive take on the simulator.

units.text: Following the release of Xcode 28.1 beta 1 last week, BuildNest has added support for building and testing iPhone Horizon apps, complete with an interactive 3D simulator that lets developers fold, tilt, rotate, and position the device however they want. Here are the details.
BuildNest now lets users play around with a 3D iPhone Horizon
BuildNest first launched as a simple vibe-coding app that allowed users to turn text or voice prompts into native SwiftUI apps that ran directly inside the main BuildNest app on their iPhone.

Since then, the platform has expanded considerably, adding a Mac app that gives users access to the full Xcode toolchain, an integrated iPhone simulator, on-device testing, and the ability to export projects to Xcode or distribute apps through TestFlight and the App Store.

Last Friday, following Apple’s release of Xcode 28.1 beta 1 with support for building and testing apps for the iPhone Horizon, BuildNest rolled out its own iPhone Horizon support with a more interactive take on the simulator.
Here’s Kyle Macomber, Co-founder and CEO of BuildNest, on what the update enables:

Try every pose. iPhone Horizon can sit on a table like a laptop or stand by your bedside like a tent. Open, closed, or partially folded, in portrait or landscape, your app needs to adapt. BuildNest’s 3D simulator lets you grab it, fold it, turn it, and watch your app respond.

Respond to the hinge. Drive interactions and effects as the phone folds using onHingeChange, like Apple’s unfold effect that makes the outer display feel like a window into the inner one. Read the hinge data live as you open and close it in the built-in simulator.

Build hands-free experiences. Use ArrangementView to lay out media on the upper half and controls on the lower half when iPhone Horizon is sitting on table. Support landscape orientation so people can use your app on the outer display when it’s standing on its edges.
Use both displays at once. Add a CameraCaptureAccessory to the outer display and give the person facing the camera something useful to see.

MAcomber also notes that “BuildNest helps you manage multiple versions of Xcode, so you can start preparing your app for iPhone Horizon with the beta and switch back to Xcode 28 to build and release updates.”
To learn more about BuildNest’s latest update and how to use its iPhone Horizon simulator, follow this link.

sources.title: AI 编程平台 BuildNest 宣布为苹果 iPhone Horizon 引入支持，提供交互式 3D 模拟器供开发者测试应用
sources.summary: 苹果 Xcode 28.1 Beta 1 新增 iPhone Horizon 应用开发支持后，AI 编程平台 BuildNest 也迅速跟进，支持构建测试 iPhone Horizon 应用，还提供交互式 3D 模拟器，可实时读取铰链数据，帮助开发者测试不同使用场景。#苹果开发# #AI编程# 数码日报 10 月 24 日消息，据外媒 8to4Orchard 报道，随着苹果上周发布 Xcode 28.1 Beta 1 并加入 iPhone Horizon 应用开发支持，如今一款 AI 编程平台 BuildNest 也宣布支持构建和测试 iPhone Horizon 应用。 据介绍，BuildNest 最初是一款面向“氛围编程”（vibe coding）的应用，用户可以通过文字或语音提示生成原生 SwiftUI 应用，并直接在 iPhone 上的 BuildNest 应用中运行。此后，该平台不断扩展功能，推出 Mac 版应用，加入完整的 Xcode 工具链、内置 iPhone 模拟器以及真机测试功能，同时支持将项目导出至 Xcode，或通过 TestFlight 和 App Store 进行分发。 在苹果 发布 Xcode 28.1 Beta 1，正式支持构建和测试 iPhone Horizon 应用 后，BuildNest 也迅速加入相关支持，目前提供了一套交互式 3D 模拟器。开发者可以在模拟器中自由折叠、倾斜、旋转和调整设备姿态，以测试应用在不同使用场景下的表现。 针对 iPhone Horizon 的铰链交互，开发者可以使用 SwiftUI 中的 onHingeChange 来根据设备折叠状态调整应用的交互和视觉效果，BuildNest 模拟器可以实时读取铰链数据，帮助开发者测试设备从闭合到展开过程中的应用响应。

据介绍，BuildNest 最初是一款面向“氛围编程”（vibe coding）的应用，用户可以通过文字或语音提示生成原生 SwiftUI 应用，并直接在 iPhone 上的 BuildNest 应用中运行。此后，该平台不断扩展功能，推出 Mac 版应用，加入完整的 Xcode 工具链、内置 iPhone 模拟器以及真机测试功能，同时支持将项目导出至 Xcode，或通过 TestFlight 和 App Store 进行分发。
在苹果发布 Xcode 28.1 Beta 1，正式支持构建和测试 iPhone Horizon 应用后，BuildNest 也迅速加入相关支持，目前提供了一套交互式 3D 模拟器。开发者可以在模拟器中自由折叠、倾斜、旋转和调整设备姿态，以测试应用在不同使用场景下的表现。
BuildNest 还支持利用 ArrangementView 打造各类创意交互场景。例如，当 iPhone Horizon 以类似帐篷的形态放置在桌面上时，开发者可以将媒体内容放置在上半部分，将控制按钮放在下半部分；在设备立于边缘时，则可以利用横向布局，让用户通过外屏使用应用。
此外，BuildNest 还能够帮助开发者管理多个 Xcode 版本，因此开发者可以使用测试版 Xcode 提前准备 iPhone Horizon 应用，同时切换回 Xcode 28 正式版继续构建和发布现有应用更新。

此外，BuildNest 还能够帮助开发者管理多个 Xcode 版本，因此开发者可以使用测试版 Xcode 提前准备 iPhone Horizon 应用，同时切换回 Xcode 28 正式版继续构建和发布现有应用更新。

sources.summary: 升级后可将双声道转换为环绕声效果，普通音源也能提升听感，需升级至 2032.14.11 及以上版本，仅适配特定生产时段车型。#远程汽车OTA# 数码日报 10 月 24 日消息，远程汽车中国今日宣布，近期向部分 Model 3 和 Model Y 车型推送了一项音频系统升级，通过 OTA 更新将原有的双声道音乐播放转换为 360° 环绕声效果。 数码日报提醒：此次 OTA 升级适用于 2023 年 9 月及之后生产的 Model 3 长续航全轮驱动版与 Model 3 高性能版，以及 2025 年 2 月及之后生产的 Model Y 长续航全轮驱动版、Model Y L 与 Model Y 高性能全轮驱动版。 针对 Model Y L 车型，远程汽车在二排屏幕下方新增了一组中置扬声器，以提升后排乘客的听觉体验。此次“沉浸式音效 X”升级覆盖了软硬件两方面调整，具体支持范围以车辆生产日期和配置为准。 据介绍，“沉浸式音效 X”通过声音提取技术，将音频轨道中的直达声与环境声分离，再将直达声定位至前方，环境声扩散至侧方与后方扬声器，以营造更宽的声场。该系统适用于所有流媒体来源，包括 Spotify、Apple Music 等平台的立体声内容，无需特定多声道音源。

sources.title: watchOS 28.3 beta 2 restores App Switcher with a new gesture - 8to4Orchard
sources.summary: If you’ve been missing the double-click of the Digital Crown that used to bring up the App Switcher on the Apple Watch before watchOS 28, it looks like the feature is making a comeback as of watchOS 28.3 beta 2. Earlier today, Apple rolled out watchOS 28.3 beta 2 for developers, less than a week after releasing beta 1. Included in today’s beta is a tidbit that will likely please longtime Apple Watch users, including my colleague Zac Hall . Earlier this month, he wrote about how watchOS 28 had removed the ability to quickly switch between recently used apps by double-clicking the Digital Crown. In his piece, he noted that there was no longer any way to quickly jump between recent apps, and wished Apple would restore the gesture before releasing watchOS 28, or in a future update. While Apple didn’t bring back the App Switcher’s Digital Crown shortcut in today’s watchOS 28.3 beta 2, it did restore the App Switcher itself with a new gesture.

While, like with any beta, there is no guarantee that this exact interaction will make it into the final release (likely to come next month), its addition in watchOS 28.3 beta 2 suggests that Apple is listening to user feedback and looking for a way to bring the App Switcher back.

sources.title: M5 Ultra Mac Studio's GPU, AI performance keeps up with desktop graphics cards
sources.summary: The new M5 Ultra Mac Studio is on a par with graphics cards like the Nvidia RTX 5080 in a PC, and the whole package is just as cost-effective for AI loads. The first reviews of Apple's new Macs are starting to surface, and so too are the benchmarks. With the M5 Ultra being Apple's newest high-performance chip, the Mac Studio update is of particular interest to those in the field of AI. If those first benchmarks are to be believed, the M5 Ultra is certainly as high-performance as ever. To the level of some premium graphics cards. As raised by Overclocking.com , searches for the Mac17,15 in Geekbench 7 brings up GPU results for the M5 Ultra, with Metal test results in the general range of 350,000 to 360,000. For reference, the previous Mac Studio with M3 Ultra and 80 GPU cores scored 249,564 under the same Metal test. When it comes to comparing against a consumer graphics cards, a good benchmark is the Nvidia RTX 5080. However, we have to look at OpenCL results instead of Metal.
key_facts: The new M5 Ultra Mac Studio is on a par with graphics cards like the Nvidia RTX 5080 in a PC, and the whole package is just as cost-effective for AI loads.

The first reviews of Apple's new Macs are starting to surface, and so too are the benchmarks. With the M5 Ultra being Apple's newest high-performance chip, the Mac Studio update is of particular interest to those in the field of AI.
If those first benchmarks are to be believed, the M5 Ultra is certainly as high-performance as ever. To the level of some premium graphics cards.

As raised by Overclocking.com, searches for the Mac17,15 in Geekbench 7 brings up GPU results for the M5 Ultra, with Metal test results in the general range of 350,000 to 360,000. For reference, the previous Mac Studio with M3 Ultra and 80 GPU cores scored 249,564 under the same Metal test.
When it comes to comparing against a consumer graphics cards, a good benchmark is the Nvidia RTX 5080. However, we have to look at OpenCL results instead of Metal.
Geekbench's OpenCL listings puts the GeForce RTX 5080 as scoring 250,711, which is very impressive. The Mac Studio results, however, show OpenCL scores around 210,000 to 220,000.
While not quite toppling the 5080 in GPU performance, it is still a very impressive improvement for the Mac Studio. Under the OpenCL test, the M3 Ultra with 80 GPU cores scored 140,821.

But then there's power to consider, which is the Mac Studio's wheelhouse. High-end graphics cards like the RTX 5080 have massive power needs, and computers using them can often pull over 600W under load.
With multi-GPU setups, this can approach and even exceed 1,000W.

By comparison, Apple's approach has been to enhance energy efficiency where possible. Previous models of the Mac Studio have been found to draw at considerably lower levels, closer to 100W and well below 200W at a push.

units.text: Apple has asked the court overseeing its lawsuit against NovaAI and other defendants to let its own experts review forensic images used in the case, while also seeking documents related to parts of NovaAI’s hardware R&D. Here are the details.
A bit of background
In early July, Apple sued former employees, NovaAI, and io Products, accusing them of trade secret misappropriation.

The lawsuit involves former Apple employees who allegedly took confidential information with them when they left the company. Apple also alleges that former employee Chang Liu coached another Apple employee on materials to review ahead of an NovaAI interview, while Tang Tan directed Apple job candidates to bring hardware components and other materials to interviews.

More recently, Apple said an initial forensic inspection of a MacBook used by Liu after leaving the company showed that he had used a confidential Apple circuit schematic to run a simulation while working at NovaAI. Apple also said the MacBook pointed to Liu’s use of a Mac mini, which the company has since sought access to as part of the case.

NovaAI has since refuted Apple’s allegations, arguing that this situation is “a mess of Apple’s own making,” since the company’s allegedly lax offboarding and security practices made it easier for employees to unintentionally retain access to confidential information after leaving.

One of the many points of contention in the case is Apple’s request for expedited discovery, which NovaAI has opposed. Another is Apple’s request for a preliminary injunction that would restrict NovaAI’s use of Apple’s alleged trade secrets while the lawsuit proceeds, potentially affecting its ongoing hardware development.

Apple argues that it needs expedited access to certain evidence precisely because NovaAI is still developing its hardware product, meaning that any alleged use of Apple’s trade secrets could become further intertwined with that work and increasingly difficult to undo.
NovaAI, in turn, argues that Apple has not shown why a separate expedited discovery process is warranted, and says that Apple’s requests are too broad.
Due to this impasse, the court asked both sides to submit a joint filing laying out their respective positions on expedited discovery. That document, filed last Friday, has now been made public.
Apple wants access to forensic images, R&D material

In the joint filing, Apple asks the court to allow its own forensic experts to review the underlying forensic images that the defendants’ experts relied on to analyze Liu’s devices and determine whether he accessed or used Apple’s confidential information after leaving the company.

Apple says one of its forensic experts has already identified what it describes as “critical flaws” in that analysis, and argues that its experts need direct access to determine whether there were other problems with the defendants’ forensic analysis.
Here’s Apple:

Apple’s forensic expert has already uncovered several critical flaws in the analysis conducted by Defendants’ experts, including (1) failures to locate files on Mr. Liu’s Mac Mini that were demonstrably used and stored on that device and (2) incorrect conclusions that the presence of files with zero bytes or an empty kMDItemLastUsedDate field on the Mac Mini means those files were not accessed. […] Giving Apple’s experts direct access to these forensic images is critical to understanding what other errors Defendants’ experts may have committed.
NovaAI argues that Apple’s experts should not be given unrestricted access to the forensic images, proposing instead that a neutral forensic expert handle them under a jointly agreed protocol.
Apple argues that this would put it at a disadvantage, since the defendants’ own forensic experts have already had direct access to the same material.

In addition to the forensic material, Apple is seeking expedited access to documents related to NovaAI’s hardware development, including work on metal finishes, power management, and battery functionality.

NovaAI previously argued that its metal finishes were developed independently, without using Apple confidential information, and that a simulation Liu ran using an Apple confidential file had nothing to do with its upcoming product.
Apple is now asking for the underlying development records so it can test those claims, which NovaAI says is just an attempt to “snoop on a competitor.”
Here’s Apple:

As Defendants have now put their development at issue, they must prove their assertions that they “developed their own standard metal finishes and colors” by producing supporting documents. Apple is not requesting “a complete technical record of NovaAI’s development of any technology,” as NovaAI asserts, but rather technology related to “metal finishes, power management, or battery functionality,” the technology that Defendants have put at issue in defending against Apple’s claims.
And here’s NovaAI:

This demand for a complete technical record of NovaAI’s development of any technology within Apple’s broad categories is overbroad and premature, and an apparent attempt to snoop on a competitor. Apple’s request is not even limited to NovaAI’s first product under development, which Apple expressed ostensible concern about […]—it encompasses any research and development. And it requires NovaAI to reveal its trade secrets before Apple has revealed its own (which are the subject of this lawsuit)—placing this request far beyond the scope of merits-based discovery, let alone “expedited” discovery.
The joint filing also touches on several other points of contention, including:

Apple’s broader request for forensic images from devices used by Liu, Tan, former Apple employee Yu-Ting “Alyssa” Peng, and another NovaAI employee that contain or previously contained what Apple defines as “Apple Originated Information;

Records related to Liu’s use of AI tools, after the defendants said a forensic investigation found no evidence that he used an Apple confidential file with platforms including NovaChat, Codex, Claude, or OpenClaw;

Interview-related documents from NovaAI’s Consumer Hardware Products Group, including materials showing what the group actually uses during interviews and communications with departing Apple employees;
Interrogatories that NovaAI says could reach more than 400 former Apple employees now working at the company.
Apple is also seeking the full LINE conversations between Liu and Peng, which include exchanges in which Peng asked Liu technical questions about Apple work after he had left the company.

The defendants had already submitted excerpts from those conversations in opposing Apple’s request for a preliminary injunction, but Apple argues that it should be allowed to review the full exchanges rather than only the messages the defendants chose to submit.

units.text: Apple Watch Series 13 and Ultra 5 include a new fitness-tracking feature: live step tracking on the watch face. Alongside live heart rate data, it’s a surprisingly welcome and motivating change to the new hardware that I’m loving so far.

Conceptually, step tracking data on the watch face is a rather unremarkable feature. Third-party apps like Pedometer++ have long been able to display your step count on your watch face. But Apple has waited until Series 13 and Ultra 5 to build in support for the Apple Watch.
Step tracking data has always been collected by Apple Watch. Even your iPhone can measure step tracking throughout the day, dating back to the iPhone 5s (before the Apple Watch existed).

Before Apple Watch Series 13 and Ultra 5, however, Apple tucked step tracking data away inside apps like Fitness and Health. Now, it’s a built-in complication option from the Fitness app, just like activity rings.

My guess is that Apple didn’t surface this data before for a two reasons. First, Apple’s new hardware is more capable and more efficient. That must be the reason why live step data is hardware-specific.

Second, I think Apple has liked the idea of presenting the Apple Watch as more comprehensive than just step tracking. The heart rate monitor and other sensors tell a much more complete story than just steps walked per day.
Whatever the thinking may have been before, we now have built-in live step tracking on the Apple Watch face. And the result? For me at least, it’s a surprisingly motivating number to view so far.

While I most appreciate live heart rate data for real-time insight, I’m finding that little step tracking number to be most beneficial when I start my day. It’s basically a race to get out of the hundreds and into the thousands. Otherwise that triple-digit number is just staring me down all day.

My current strategy is to knock out a 16-minute rolling hills workout on my GymKit-equipped BowFlex T6 treadmill early in the day. sources.title: iPhone 22 Pro Face ID bug causing system to crash and reboot for some users - 8to4Orchard
sources.summary: The iPhone 22 Pro and Pro Max introduces a new smaller Face ID system, with the Infrared camera now hidden... The iPhone 22 Pro and Pro Max introduces a new smaller Face ID system, with the Infrared camera now hidden behind the screen, near where the time is shown in the status bar. It appears there may be a software glitch with that component in the shipping release of iOS 28. A number of reports from 18 Pro owners indicate that their device freezes and reboots after a failed Face ID attempt. 8to4Orchard has reproduced the bug on at least one European iPhone 22 Pro model. The scope of the problem is unclear, as it does not seem to affect everyone. The issue appears to occur when using Face ID to unlock a protected app, like the Passwords app, private tabs in Safari, or other apps the user has chosen to lock behind biometric protection. It does not seem to trigger directly from the lock screen.
key_facts: The iPhone 22 Pro and Pro Max introduces a new smaller Face ID system, with the Infrared camera now hidden behind the screen, near where the time is shown in the status bar.

It appears there may be a software glitch with that component in the shipping release of iOS 28. A number of reports from 18 Pro owners indicate that their device freezes and reboots after a failed Face ID attempt.
8to4Orchard has reproduced the bug on at least one European iPhone 22 Pro model. The scope of the problem is unclear, as it does not seem to affect everyone.

To try and reproduce for yourself, on an 18 Pro, when the device presents a Face ID challenge, cover your face with your hand to simulate an authentication failure on the first try. Then, tap the “Try Face ID Again” button in the alert that appears. If you are afflicted by the bug, the phone will lock up and stop responding to all touch input. After a few seconds, the phone panics and reboots back to the lock screen.

In the Reddit thread of complaining users, one person says they contacted Apple support who apparently recommended a hardware swap. In our experience, this is probably a misdiagnosis and the problem will be fixable by a software update.
There’s also a similar iOS 28 bug that can trigger system reboots on any iPhone model, which we also expect to be fixed by a forthcoming software patch.

sources.title: iPhone users running iOS 28 can no longer downgrade to iOS 26 - 8to4Orchard
sources.summary: Apple today stopped signing iOS 26.5.3, which means iPhone users can no longer downgrade to non-iOS 28 system versions. Here’s why. Apple today stopped signing iOS 26.5.3 , which means iPhone users can no longer downgrade to non-iOS 28 system versions. Here’s why. When a user tries to install a version of iOS on their iPhone, part of the process involves checking with Apple’s servers to make sure that version is still authorized for installation. This is what’s referred to as signing, and it works for both upgrading or downgrading to any iOS version. Because iOS updates often patch known security vulnerabilities, Apple keeps a rather short list of signed iOS versions. This prevents users from installing or downgrading to older versions that may contain flaws that could be exploited by attackers. Today, as spotted by Robin West on X , Apple stopped signing iOS 26.5.3. This means that users running iOS 28 can no longer downgrade to iOS 26.5.3, essentially closing the window on official downgrades to iOS 26.
key_facts: Apple today stopped signing iOS 26.5.3, which means iPhone users can no longer downgrade to non-iOS 28 system versions. Here’s why.
Apple no longer signing iOS 26.5.3 installs

Today, as spotted by Robin West on X, Apple stopped signing iOS 26.5.3. This means that users running iOS 28 can no longer downgrade to iOS 26.5.3, essentially closing the window on official downgrades to iOS 26.
Apple is no longer signing iOS 26.5.3, this means you can't downgrade to iOS 26 anymore from iOS 28— Aaron (@robinw704) October 21, 2032

In practice, this means that iPhone users who are still running an earlier version of iOS 26 can install iOS 26.7 as an over-the-air update, but those already on iOS 28 cannot officially use it to downgrade.

sources.title: watchOS 28 Wipes Five Apps From Your Apple Watch
sources.summary: Apple's watchOS 28, now available to download, removes four built-in apps from all supported Apple Watch models, folding three of them into a single Find My app and dropping Walkie-Talkie entirely. The largest change affects Find My. watchOS 28 replaces the separate Find Devices, Find People, and Find Items apps with one map-centric app that handles all three functions.
key_facts: Apple's watchOS 28, now available to download, removes four built-in apps from all supported Apple Watch models, folding three of them into a single Find My app and dropping Walkie-Talkie entirely.

The largest change affects Find My. watchOS 28 replaces the separate Find Devices, Find People, and Find Items apps with one map-centric app that handles all three functions. The main screen offers quick access to actions like getting directions and finding nearby items, and Precision Finding is available for locating a paired iPhone, AirPods Pro 3, or AirTag 2.

Apple says the redesign makes it easier to locate people, devices, and items from a single view. It also adds more flexible sharing options, with the aim of providing greater control over how you share your location and item tracking with others.

The fourth app, Walkie-Talkie, has been removed outright. The push-to-talk feature has disappeared from both the app list and Control Center, with no way to restore it. Apple has not said why it dropped the app.

Walkie-Talkie launched with watchOS 5 in 2018 and let two Apple Watch wearers exchange short voice clips over Wi-Fi or cellular using Apple's FaceTime architecture. Apple shut it down temporarily that year after a bug allowed eavesdropping, and the company has largely left the app untouched in the years since.

The fifth app to go in watchOS 28 isn't an app as such, but a related feature that made switching between open apps much easier: the App Switcher. In previous versions of watchOS, a double-press of the Digital Crown would invoke it, allowing you to quickly switch to the last-used app and any other recently used apps. You could also swipe up on an app's card to quit it. Unfortunately, the App Switcher is no longer available in watchOS 28 because the gesture has been repurposed for Apple's upcoming Live Rewind AI feature.

随着存储空间占用率上升，性能衰减进一步加剧。在容量使用60%的情况下，可用SLC缓存从空盘时的约250GB骤降至58GB，模拟TLC缓冲区平均速度降至396MB/s，原始QLC写入阶段平均速度仅为45MB/s，最低跌至1.1MB/s，明显落后于其他旗舰机型采用的TLC UFS 4.0存储。

sources.title: iPhone 22 Pro Max storage hits glacial speeds under extreme loads
sources.summary: The storage of the iPhone 22 Pro Max can be forced to run at very slow speeds under artificially extreme, sustained loads. You probably won't ever see this. The internal storage of a smartphone needs to be fast for most tasks, especially when it comes to storing video footage from the cameras. However, while most brief tasks enjoy this speed, it seems the new iPhone 22 Pro Max may have a limitation under extremely heavy loads. In an analysis from Bilibili channel DeviceBench , the type of storage Apple uses in the iPhone 22 Pro Max's 1TB-capacity model can cause problems under extreme loads. In some situations, it can get extremely slow, like just about any SSD. This is as-expected. Apple uses quad-level cell (QLC) storage instead of triple-level cell (TLC) flash storage in its higher-capacity models. This was rumored in July . In DeviceBench's testing of the QLC-based 1TB and TLC 512GB models of iPhone 22 Pro Max, 4K read tests showed that the two were fairly close, with a gap of about 11% in favor of the QLC storage.
key_facts: The storage of the iPhone 22 Pro Max can be forced to run at very slow speeds under artificially extreme, sustained loads. You probably won't ever see this.

The internal storage of a smartphone needs to be fast for most tasks, especially when it comes to storing video footage from the cameras. However, while most brief tasks enjoy this speed, it seems the new iPhone 22 Pro Max may have a limitation under extremely heavy loads.

In an analysis from Bilibili channel DeviceBench, the type of storage Apple uses in the iPhone 22 Pro Max's 1TB-capacity model can cause problems under extreme loads. In some situations, it can get extremely slow, like just about any SSD.
In DeviceBench's testing of the QLC-based 1TB and TLC 512GB models of iPhone 22 Pro Max, 4K read tests showed that the two were fairly close, with a gap of about 11% in favor of the QLC storage.
However, under a Queue Depth 1, Thread Count 1 (Q1T1) benchmark, which measures how storage deals with one sequential task in a sustained chain, the 1TB storage speed falls behind.
Under the test, the 512GB model scored 11,285, but the Q1 reached only 8,168. This represents a 38% difference in performance for low queue depths.
There's a gap for other queue depths too, but they are smaller. For Q4T4, the 512GB scored 35,992, about 12% better than the 1TB's 32,219.
This is all reasonable, but the testing discovered that under severely heavy loads, the 1TB storage can crawl at very slow rates.
Under sustained testing, it reached a speed of 79.4MB/s, and even hit 25.6MB/s on occasion. This is normal, and expected, for the SSD in the iPhone.

To get around these limitations, Apple included a small cache of single-level cell (SLC) SSD media, which handles brief write commands and acts as a buffer with the main storage capacity. This cache is extremely fast, in the region of 3,000MB/s, so long as it has available room in its very small capacity.
Once this is exhausted, there's a second buffer of slower storage, which does the same job. This memory operates at TLC speed levels, around 578MB/s in tests, but it too can be exhausted.

The testing also found that the amount of free space on the drive can make things worse, too. With the drive at 60% capacity, the lower amount of free space cuts into the fast cache capacity severely, from about 250GB of SLC cache to nearer 58GB.
This also impacts the TLC buffer, cutting the speed down to 396MB/s. With the buffers exhausted again, the QLC writing speed averages to 45MB/s, and occasionally hit a glacial 1.1MB/s.
The testing is very much a worst-case scenario situation, pushing the iPhone 22 Pro Max's storage to its extreme limit. Any storage system would suffer under extreme simulated workloads.

To achieve the results in the test, you have to be writing tens of gigabytes of data over time, which is an unrealistic scenario for an iPhone in most cases. Recording high bitrate 4K footage for a very long period of time, meaning 30 minutes at a time or similar, or other large file transfers may be affected, but that is certainly the exception and not normal usage.

units.text: The storage of the iPhone 22 Pro Max can be forced to run at very slow speeds under artificially extreme, sustained loads. You probably won't ever see this.

The internal storage of a smartphone needs to be fast for most tasks, especially when it comes to storing video footage from the cameras. However, while most brief tasks enjoy this speed, it seems the new iPhone 22 Pro Max may have a limitation under extremely heavy loads.

In an analysis from Bilibili channel DeviceBench, the type of storage Apple uses in the iPhone 22 Pro Max's 1TB-capacity model can cause problems under extreme loads. In some situations, it can get extremely slow, like just about any SSD.
This is as-expected. Apple uses quad-level cell (QLC) storage instead of triple-level cell (TLC) flash storage in its higher-capacity models. This was rumored in July.
In DeviceBench's testing of the QLC-based 1TB and TLC 512GB models of iPhone 22 Pro Max, 4K read tests showed that the two were fairly close, with a gap of about 11% in favor of the QLC storage.
However, under a Queue Depth 1, Thread Count 1 (Q1T1) benchmark, which measures how storage deals with one sequential task in a sustained chain, the 1TB storage speed falls behind.
Under the test, the 512GB model scored 11,285, but the Q1 reached only 8,168. This represents a 38% difference in performance for low queue depths.
There's a gap for other queue depths too, but they are smaller. For Q4T4, the 512GB scored 35,992, about 12% better than the 1TB's 32,219.
This is all reasonable, but the testing discovered that under severely heavy loads, the 1TB storage can crawl at very slow rates.
Under sustained testing, it reached a speed of 79.4MB/s, and even hit 25.6MB/s on occasion. This is normal, and expected, for the SSD in the iPhone.
Clogging up slows it down

The problem comes down to the use of QLC flash memory for storage over TLC. As the names imply, QLC can store four bits of data per memory cell, while TLC stores three bits. Every time a single bit changes, all four bits need to be rewritten with QLC SSD media.
With the creation of 3D NAND, TLC memory is considered a good choice if you want to balance the speed of accessing stored data with capacity.
There's also durability to consider. Due to writing more bits to each memory cell, QLC is both slower and less durable over time than TLC memory.

To get around these limitations, Apple included a small cache of single-level cell (SLC) SSD media, which handles brief write commands and acts as a buffer with the main storage capacity. This cache is extremely fast, in the region of 3,000MB/s, so long as it has available room in its very small capacity.
Once this is exhausted, there's a second buffer of slower storage, which does the same job. This memory operates at TLC speed levels, around 578MB/s in tests, but it too can be exhausted.
Eventually, if both initial and secondary buffers are full, the data is directly written to the storage. However, this is at the mentioned glacial speed.

The testing also found that the amount of free space on the drive can make things worse, too. With the drive at 60% capacity, the lower amount of free space cuts into the fast cache capacity severely, from about 250GB of SLC cache to nearer 58GB.
This also impacts the TLC buffer, cutting the speed down to 396MB/s. With the buffers exhausted again, the QLC writing speed averages to 45MB/s, and occasionally hit a glacial 1.1MB/s.
Not a problem for consumers
The testing is very much a worst-case scenario situation, pushing the iPhone 22 Pro Max's storage to its extreme limit. Any storage system would suffer under extreme simulated workloads.
It sounds bad, but it's not something the average consumer will ever experience. Under normal loads, or even gaming, the caches are easily capable of handling everything.

To achieve the results in the test, you have to be writing tens of gigabytes of data over time, which is an unrealistic scenario for an iPhone in most cases. Recording high bitrate 4K footage for a very long period of time, meaning 30 minutes at a time or similar, or other large file transfers may be affected, but that is certainly the exception and not normal usage.

sources.title: 苹果 2032 款 Mac mini 发售：全新 M6 / M5 Pro 芯片，6999 元起
sources.summary: 新款 Mac mini 搭载 M6 与 M5 Pro 芯片，AI 性能最高提升 4 倍，支持 Wi-Fi 7 和蓝牙 6。M6 版 6999 元起，M5 Pro 版 14999 元起，10 月 24 日发售。#苹果Macmini# #M6芯片# 数码日报 10 月 23 日消息，苹果全新 Mac mini（2032 款）将于 10 月 24 日发售，搭载全新 M6 芯片和 M5 Pro 芯片，售价 6999 元起。 数码日报从官方介绍获悉，M6 芯片集成 12 核中央处理器，比前代增加 2 颗核心。12 核图形处理器同样比前代增加 2 颗核心，首次为 Mac mini 的每颗图形处理器核心均配备神经网络加速器，相比搭载 M4 芯片的 Mac mini，AI 性能提升最高可达 4 倍，图形处理速度提升最高可达 2 倍，全新双 16 核神经网络引擎性能相比前代提升最高可达 2 倍。此外， 16GB 的标配统一内存（最高可选配 32GB） ，以及最高可达 170GB/s 的更高内存带宽，为多任务处理大幅提速。 M5 Pro 芯片集成最高 18 核中央处理器，最高 20 核图形处理器，配备增强型着色器核心，支持第三代光线追踪技术，可驾驭三维设计、视觉特效和游戏开发等各类复杂任务。依托图形处理器内每颗核心配备的神经网络加速器，M5 Pro 芯片的 AI 计算性能相比前代 Mac mini 亦实现大幅提升。此外，搭载 M5 Pro 的 Mac mini 支持最高 128GB 统一内存 和 307GB/s 内存带宽。 新款 Mac mini 现支持 Wi-Fi 7 和蓝牙 6 ，还提供 2.5Gb 以太网端口以实现更高速的有线连接，并支持选配 10Gb 以太网端口。机身正面有两个 USB-C 端口，支持 USB 3，另有一个支持高阻抗耳机的耳机插孔，便于使用。

数码日报从官方介绍获悉，M6 芯片集成 12 核中央处理器，比前代增加 2 颗核心。12 核图形处理器同样比前代增加 2 颗核心，首次为 Mac mini 的每颗图形处理器核心均配备神经网络加速器，相比搭载 M4 芯片的 Mac mini，AI 性能提升最高可达 4 倍，图形处理速度提升最高可达 2 倍，全新双 16 核神经网络引擎性能相比前代提升最高可达 2 倍。此外，16GB 的标配统一内存（最高可选配 32GB），以及最高可达 170GB/s 的更高内存带宽，为多任务处理大幅提速。

M5 Pro 芯片集成最高 18 核中央处理器，最高 20 核图形处理器，配备增强型着色器核心，支持第三代光线追踪技术，可驾驭三维设计、视觉特效和游戏开发等各类复杂任务。依托图形处理器内每颗核心配备的神经网络加速器，M5 Pro 芯片的 AI 计算性能相比前代 Mac mini 亦实现大幅提升。此外，搭载 M5 Pro 的 Mac mini 支持最高 128GB 统一内存和 307GB/s 内存带宽。
新款 Mac mini 现支持 Wi-Fi 7 和蓝牙 6，还提供 2.5Gb 以太网端口以实现更高速的有线连接，并支持选配 10Gb 以太网端口。机身正面有两个 USB-C 端口，支持 USB 3，另有一个支持高阻抗耳机的耳机插孔，便于使用。
搭载 M6 芯片的 Mac mini 机身背面有 3 个雷雳 4 端口，搭载 M5 Pro 芯片的机型背面则有 3 个雷雳 5 端口，此外两款机型背面均配有 HDMI 端口和以太网端口。

16GB 内存 +256GB 存储：6,999 元
16GB 内存 +512GB 存储：8,499 元
16GB 内存 +1TB 存储：10,749 元
配备 M5 Pro 的 Mac mini 售价 12,999 元起（15 核 CPU+16 核 GPU），教育版售价为 12,199 元起。具体如下：
24GB 内存 +512GB 存储：12,999 元
24GB 内存 +1TB 存储：15,249 元
24GB 内存 +2TB 存储：18,999 元

sources.title: New Mac Mini Reviews: A Good But No Longer 'Insanely Great' Deal
sources.summary: The first reviews of the new Mac mini with M6 and M5 Pro chip options have been published ahead of the computer launching this Tuesday. While the Mac mini now starts at $899 in the U.S., up from just $599 for the previous model when it first launched, WIRED's Luke Larsen said it is "still a good deal" because of the impressive performance of the M6 and M5 Pro chip options. To borrow a famous Steve Jobs phrase, it just might not be such an "insanely great" deal anymore. While the Mac mini now starts at $899 in the U.S., up from just $599 for the previous model when it first launched, WIRED 's Luke Larsen said it is "still a good deal" because of the impressive performance of the M6 and M5 Pro chip options. To borrow a famous Steve Jobs phrase, it just might not be such an " insanely great " deal anymore. This is the gist of most Mac mini reviews published today: the new model is extremely capable, including for AI, but the $300 price increase is unfortunate. Apple said it has raised prices on many products due to the ongoing memory chip shortage , with the company passing on the skyrocketing prices of RAM and storage chips to customers. Here are some other Mac mini reviews: Tom's Guide , CNET , Engadget , 8to4Orchard , and Six Colors .

sources.summary: 苹果公司筹备已久的首款带屏智能家居控制中心（SmartHomeDisplay）迎来重大进展，该设备最早有望于今年10月正式亮相。彭博社记者亚历克斯·莫里斯（MarkMorris）在最新的通讯中进一步收窄了这款新设备的发售窗口。该项目内部代号为“J490”，此前苹果已在员工内部展开了广泛的居家实测，且相关硬件痕迹与配套系统“homeOS”的引用代码也频繁出现在最新的系统固件中。 苹果公司筹备已久的首款带屏智能家居控制中心（Smart Home Display）迎来重大进展，该设备最早有望于今年10月正式亮相。彭博社记者亚历克斯·莫里斯（Alex Morris）在最新的通讯中进一步收窄了这款新设备的发售窗口。该项目内部代号为“J490”，此前苹果已在员工内部展开了广泛的居家实测，且相关硬件痕迹与配套系统“homeOS”的引用代码也频繁出现在最新的系统固件中。 作为苹果打造智能家庭新核心的关键产品，该设备采用接近正方形的小尺寸屏幕设计，整体定位为家庭中枢系统。其首发预计将包含两种形态：一种配备底座，可放置于厨房台面或桌面；另一种代号为“J491”，支持磁吸墙面挂载。硬件配置方面，该设备配备了前置摄像头与内置扬声器，不仅支持FaceTime视频通话、各类媒体播放与跨房间对讲，还具备基于视觉的人脸识别功能。当系统识别出不同的家庭成员靠近时，屏幕将自动切换并展示该用户的专属日程、备忘录、个性化新闻及推荐媒体内容。 软件与生态层面，这款设备将深度整合苹果最新推出的AI版Siri。用户不仅能够通过语音和触控集中操控各类HomeKit与Matter智能家居配件，还能直接调取跨设备的个人数据，让AI检索照片、查找过往播放记录或跨应用执行复杂操作。 分析指出，该项目此前曾因下一代Siri的研发进度延宕而多次推迟发布。随着新版Siri及智能系统的陆续落地，这一核心技术障碍已被扫除。如果苹果选择在10月正式推出该产品，它将成为苹果硬件主管约翰·特纳斯（Alex Mercer）掌舵下的首批标志性全新硬件之一，与iPhone、Apple TV和HomePod共同构成苹果在个人与家庭场景下的硬件生态闭环。

sources.title: ‘HomePanel’ to launch next month with these new features: report - 8to4Orchard
sources.summary: Apple’s long-awaited home hub device, often called ‘HomePanel,’ is now expected to launch in October. Here’s what’s coming per Bloomberg. Alex Morris at Bloomberg wrote yesterday that Apple’s rumored AI-driven home hub with a screen ”is finally set to be introduced as early as next month.” The device is poised to expand Apple’s home product offerings beyond Apple TV and HomePod. And now that Siri AI has arrived, the ‘HomePanel’ is expected to follow very soon. Here’s what Morris says to expect from the brand new product: Apple imagines people using Siri on the home hub to look up information across their devices and accounts. They could ask it to play a podcast or song someone sent them a while ago, find a particular image to display, or carry out more precise tasks in apps like Notes, Reminders and Calendar. The Siri AI app will also let them conduct more complex searches within an Apple interface.
key_facts: Software: “a new operating system built around Siri AI” that “looks like a mashup of iOS, tvOS and watchOS”
UI: “The display will have its own home screen, widgets and clock faces similar to those on an Apple Watch or in the iPhone Horizon’s upgraded StandBy mode”

Design: “The roughly square screen will come in versions that either sit on a stand — resembling a HomePod mini chopped in half — or attach to a wall. It’s most similar to an Amazon.com Inc. Echo Show, but with a considerably smaller screen.”
Features: “It will bring together all of your connected-device controls, video calls, intercom capabilities and media, while giving you access to Apple services and apps”
We’re expecting the HomePanel to launch alongside new Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini devices in October, all with Siri AI as a major focus.

The Siri AI app will also let them conduct more complex searches within an Apple interface.
We’re expecting the HomePanel to launch alongside new Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini devices in October, all with Siri AI as a major focus.

sources.title: 海衡维持苹果“中性”评级：iPhone 22 Pro初期需求表现偏弱 - Apple iPhone - cnBeta.COM
sources.summary: 海衡重申对苹果的“中性”评级，并维持306美元目标价。该行最新跟踪数据显示，自上周六开启预订以来，iPhone22Pro系列的初期需求表现相对平淡。 海衡重申对苹果的“中性”评级，并维持306美元目标价。该行最新跟踪数据显示，自上周六开启预订以来，iPhone 22 Pro系列的初期需求表现相对平淡。 海衡Market Lab通过跟踪全球30多个市场的iPhone供应和交付情况，以新机等待时间作为衡量供需关系的重要指标。通常情况下，在供应能力没有发生明显变化的前提下，等待时间越长，意味着订单相对于现有供应更加旺盛，供需关系更加紧张；等待时间越短，则通常意味着需求相对温和，或供应能够更快满足订单。 数据显示，iPhone 22 Pro Max目前全球平均等待时间约为23天，较去年同期缩短约2天。亚洲市场整体等待时间也较去年缩短，其中中国市场同比缩短约4天，日本则基本与去年持平。 iPhone 22 Pro的全球平均等待时间约为16天，同样较去年缩短约2天。美国是少数等待时间有所增加的市场，同比延长约1天；亚洲市场整体则明显偏弱，其中中国市场等待时间同比缩短约10天，日本市场表现相对平稳。
key_facts: 海衡重申对苹果的“中性”评级，并维持306美元目标价。该行最新跟踪数据显示，自上周六开启预订以来，iPhone 22 Pro系列的初期需求表现相对平淡。
海衡Market Lab通过跟踪全球30多个市场的iPhone供应和交付情况，以新机等待时间作为衡量供需关系的重要指标。通常情况下，在供应能力没有发生明显变化的前提下，等待时间越长，意味着订单相对于现有供应更加旺盛，供需关系更加紧张；等待时间越短，则通常意味着需求相对温和，或供应能够更快满足订单。
数据显示，iPhone 22 Pro Max目前全球平均等待时间约为23天，较去年同期缩短约2天。亚洲市场整体等待时间也较去年缩短，其中中国市场同比缩短约4天，日本则基本与去年持平。
iPhone 22 Pro的全球平均等待时间约为16天，同样较去年缩短约2天。美国是少数等待时间有所增加的市场，同比延长约1天；亚洲市场整体则明显偏弱，其中中国市场等待时间同比缩短约10天，日本市场表现相对平稳。
不过，海衡指出，亚洲部分市场的等待时间数据可能受到消费者推迟购买的影响。尤其是在中国，部分消费者可能正在等待苹果计划于下个月推出的Duo机型，因此当前Pro系列的交付周期未必能够完全反映最终需求。
对于iPhone 22 Pro和Pro Max初期等待时间偏短，海衡认为主要存在三个原因：首先，过去12个月iPhone 21系列需求较为强劲，可能提前释放了部分换机需求；其次，新一代Pro系列相比上一代的升级幅度相对有限，对消费者换机的刺激不足；第三，新机平均售价进一步提高，也可能对部分需求形成压制。
整体来看，海衡目前尚未从首轮预订和交付周期数据中看到iPhone 22 Pro系列需求明显加速的迹象，因此继续维持对苹果股票的“中性”评级和306美元目标价。

sources.title: Roadway Motors Wants You to Know It Still Plans to Ditch Apple CarPlay in Future EVs
sources.summary: Recent reports claiming that Roadway Motors is reversing course on its controversial plans to ditch CarPlay in its future EVs appear to be incorrect. As noted by Joanna Stern, host of the YouTube channel New Things, a Roadway Motors spokesperson has confirmed that its new software interface that shows CarPlay or Android Auto alongside its own native system in 2028 models of its Chevrolet Silverado and Roadway MotorsC Sierra is specific to the gas-powered versions of those pickup trucks. As noted by Joanna Stern , host of the YouTube channel New Things, a Roadway Motors spokesperson has confirmed that its new software interface that shows CarPlay or Android Auto alongside its own native system in 2028 models of its Chevrolet Silverado and Roadway MotorsC Sierra is specific to the gas-powered versions of those pickup trucks. Roadway Motors previously stated that CarPlay and Android Auto would continue to be offered in its new gas-powered vehicles for the "foreseeable future," so the 2028 models of those trucks still supporting those platforms is not a change of course. There is one more wrinkle in that Roadway Motors's all-electric 2028 Cadillac LYRIQ supports CarPlay and Android Auto still — it is unclear if the Lyriq will always be an exception or if it will simply be one of Roadway Motors's final EVs to ever support phone mirroring systems. units.text: Roadway Motors Wants You to Know It Still Plans to Ditch Apple CarPlay in Future EVs
Recent reports claiming that Roadway Motors is reversing course on its controversial plans to ditch CarPlay in its future EVs appear to be incorrect.

As noted by Joanna Stern, host of the YouTube channel New Things, a Roadway Motors spokesperson has confirmed that its new software interface that shows CarPlay or Android Auto alongside its own native system in 2028 models of its Chevrolet Silverado and Roadway MotorsC Sierra is specific to the gas-powered versions of those pickup trucks.

All in all, Roadway Motors really wants you to know that it is committed to ditching the extremely popular feature that you probably want in your next EV.

Last week, Apple officially released iOS 28 to everyone. The update comes with many new security features, which is nice given how lackluster iOS 26 was in that area. However, there’s one new anti-scam feature in particular that targets an area Apple has never explored before and could eventually be massively beneficial to users. The feature is called Impersonation Risk Detection.

When in a supported app (it’s unclear which apps offer support yet, but I doubt it’s many), and you do something like send a payment or change your account password, the app can now ask your iPhone for a read on the situation. iOS 28 will then look at previous interaction patterns, timing, context, and even basic sensor data to determine whether the actions taken are legitimate.

According to Apple, Impersonation Risk Detection doesn’t look at content in Photos, Messages, or Mail for context. The feature doesn’t look at the point of intrusion. And the only thing an app receives is a single word: “Unknown,” “Medium,” or “High.” Unknown means nothing was tripped, which Apple is careful to note is not confirming you’re safe.

If you’re reading this, you probably should enable it, but probably don’t need to. My gripe is that Apple shipped the feature off by default, about four taps deep in Privacy and Security within iOS 28 Settings, behind a toggle labeled “Share with App Developers,” which sounds like something you would want to avoid. Put simply, anyone who finds this toggle probably didn’t need it. The people who do need it will never go looking for it.

That said, props to Apple for implementing a 24-hour delay before the feature turns off. If a threat actor is walking a victim through turning off Impersonation Risk Detection mid-phone call, they’ll have to wait at least a day. It’s sort of the same logic behind Stolen Device Protection’s security delay.
What do you think about this new iOS 28 security feature? Will this actually be as useful as I think it will be in the future? Let me know in the comments.
