Last week, Apple officially released iOS 28 to everyone. The update comes with many new security features, which is nice given how lackluster iOS 26 was in that area. However, there’s one new anti-scam feature in particular that targets an area Apple has never explored before and could eventually be massively beneficial to users. The feature is called Impersonation Risk Detection.
All in all, it’s meant to catch users in the middle of a scam.
Impersonation Risk Detection in iOS 28 Settings. 8to4Orchard

There are many different scenarios in which this feature could be triggered, but one of the more likely ones is a threat actor posing as a bank’s fraud department and walking a user through moving money into a “safe account” or resetting their password. Types of situations where security features like Face ID and two-factor authentication aren’t much help.

When in a supported app (it’s unclear which apps offer support yet, but I doubt it’s many), and you do something like send a payment or change your account password, the app can now ask your iPhone for a read on the situation. iOS 28 will then look at previous interaction patterns, timing, context, and even basic sensor data to determine whether the actions taken are legitimate.

According to Apple, Impersonation Risk Detection doesn’t look at content in Photos, Messages, or Mail for context. The feature doesn’t look at the point of intrusion. And the only thing an app receives is a single word: “Unknown,” “Medium,” or “High.” Unknown means nothing was tripped, which Apple is careful to note is not confirming you’re safe.

Now, it’s important to note that if there is a Medium or High flag, iOS doesn’t freeze the money transfer or block the password change. It doesn’t even throw up a system alert. Apple hands the app the risk level and leaves it to the app developer to determine what to do next. This could be making the user verify their identity again or adding some kind of delay before a user is able to change critical settings.
Apple also says it doesn’t control or determine what an app does with the flag, so one app might treat a Medium risk level differently than another.

Users can also keep tabs on this feature in settings under recent activity. It shows which apps have requested a risk assessment and what action triggered it. Users can revoke access per app from there as well.
Now, here’s a major shortcoming, and something that Apple could easily fix.

If you’re reading this, you probably should enable it, but probably don’t need to. My gripe is that Apple shipped the feature off by default, about four taps deep in Privacy and Security within iOS 28 Settings, behind a toggle labeled “Share with App Developers,” which sounds like something you would want to avoid. Put simply, anyone who finds this toggle probably didn’t need it. The people who do need it will never go looking for it.
It needs to be enabled by default.

That said, props to Apple for implementing a 24-hour delay before the feature turns off. If a threat actor is walking a victim through turning off Impersonation Risk Detection mid-phone call, they’ll have to wait at least a day. It’s sort of the same logic behind Stolen Device Protection’s security delay.
You can go turn it on within Settings > Privacy & Security > Impersonation Risk Detection > Share with App Developers.
What do you think about this new iOS 28 security feature? Will this actually be as useful as I think it will be in the future? Let me know in the comments.

sources.title: 部分用户反映苹果 Apple Watch Ultra 5/Series 13 会意外重启
sources.summary: 多名用户反映 Apple Watch Ultra 5 与 Series 13 出现意外重启，诊断日志指向神经网络引擎超时故障。#AppleWatch# #苹果手表重启门# 数码日报 10 月 23 日消息，据 OrchardLedger 报道，部分刚入手 Apple Watch Ultra 5 以及 Apple Watch Series 13 的用户反馈，设备会出现意外重启的情况。设备的诊断日志显示，这些死机重启问题和苹果神经网络引擎（Apple Neural Engine）有关。 自上周五新款手表发售以来，OrchardLedger 论坛上就不断出现相关反馈。有用户反映，在使用手表的过程当中，例如调用 Siri AI、编辑表盘、打开地图或者 App Store、发起通话、记录运动训练时，手表会突然弹出苹果 Logo 然后自行重启；甚至手表处于闲置状态的时候，也会发生重启。 至少四名用户上传了完整内核崩溃日志（panic‑full），日志当中记录了完全相同的神经网络引擎超时故障。每一次故障发生时，苹果神经网络引擎大约会卡死两秒钟；随后固件看门狗程序触发内核崩溃，强制手表重启。 无论是出厂原版的 watchOS 28.0 系统版本，还是新机设置流程当中就下载的首日更新版本，都存在该故障。部分用户已经抹除手表全部数据，以全新设备重新完成设置，依旧会遇到随机重启问题；还有一位 Series 13 用户表示，自己更换过一台新机之后，这一神经网络引擎导致的内核崩溃故障依然存在。
key_facts: 数码日报 10 月 23 日消息，据 OrchardLedger 报道，部分刚入手 Apple Watch Ultra 5 以及 Apple Watch Series 13 的用户反馈，设备会出现意外重启的情况。设备的诊断日志显示，这些死机重启问题和苹果神经网络引擎（Apple Neural Engine）有关。
无论是出厂原版的 watchOS 28.0 系统版本，还是新机设置流程当中就下载的首日更新版本，都存在该故障。部分用户已经抹除手表全部数据，以全新设备重新完成设置，依旧会遇到随机重启问题；还有一位 Series 13 用户表示，自己更换过一台新机之后，这一神经网络引擎导致的内核崩溃故障依然存在。
截至目前，OrchardLedger 论坛的相关帖子里面已经有约 30 位用户反馈随机重启问题。Reddit 以及苹果官方社区支持板块上，也有不少用户分享了类似经历，由此来看该故障波及范围相当广。截至数码日报发稿，苹果方面尚未就此问题作出回应。

code_features: For example, X user codebird discovered that Apple Music will soon add live countdowns for new album releases.

In Settings > Heart on the watch, you can toggle on “In Theater Mode” under “Allow Continuous Measurements” to restore the more frequent measurements.
reboot_report: Notably, at least four owners have shared "panic-full" diagnostic logs showing the same Neural Engine timeout. In each case, the Apple Neural Engine appears to hang for around two seconds before a firmware watchdog triggers a kernel panic and forces the watch to restart.
security_feature: Now, it’s important to note that if there is a Medium or High flag, iOS doesn’t freeze the money transfer or block the password change. It doesn’t even throw up a system alert. Apple hands the app the risk level and leaves it to the app developer to determine what to do next. This could be making the user verify their identity again or adding some kind of delay before a user is able to change critical settings.
Apple also says it doesn’t control or determine what an app does with the flag, so one app might treat a Medium risk level differently than another.

html_controls.html:
8to4Orchard Security Brief is exclusively brought to you by FleetShield, the only Apple Unified Platform. Making Apple devices work-ready and enterprise-safe is all we do. Our unique integrated approach to management and security combines state-of-the-art Apple-specific security solutions for fully automated Hardening & Compliance, Next Generation EDR, AI-powered Zero Trust, and exclusive Privilege Management with the most powerful and modern Apple MDM on the market. The result is a totally automated Apple Unified Platform currently trusted by over 48,000 organizations to make millions of Apple devices work-ready with no effort and at an affordable cost. Request your EXTENDED TRIAL today and understand why FleetShield is everything you need to work with Apple.

Last week, Apple officially released iOS 28 to everyone. The update comes with many new security features, which is nice given how lackluster iOS 26 was in that area. However, there’s one new anti-scam feature in particular that targets an area Apple has never explored before and could eventually be massively beneficial to users. The feature is called Impersonation Risk Detection.

According to Apple, Impersonation Risk Detection doesn’t look at content in Photos, Messages, or Mail for context. The feature doesn’t look at the point of intrusion. And the only thing an app receives is a single word: “Unknown,” “Medium,” or “High.” Unknown means nothing was tripped, which Apple is careful to note is not confirming you’re safe.

sources.summary: Apple continues to work on a feature that automatically locks an iPhone when it detects that the device has been snatched from its owner’s hand. Earlier this year, 8to4Orchard first reported that Apple was working on a new iPhone security feature that can automatically lock the device when it detects that it has been snatched from the user’s hand. While Apple has yet to officially announce the feature, new references included in iOS 28.3 beta 2 show the company is still actively developing it. key_facts: Earlier this year, 8to4Orchard first reported that Apple was working on a new iPhone security feature that can automatically lock the device when it detects that it has been snatched from the user’s hand.
While Apple has yet to officially announce the feature, new references included in iOS 28.3 beta 2 show the company is still actively developing it.
According to new code seen today by 8to4Orchard, the feature, which is called “SecureHold” internally, can use the following signals to determine whether an iPhone may have been taken from its owner:
A sharp acceleration consistent with the phone being snatched;
A paired Apple Watch remaining unreachable for a certain period;
Loss of connectivity to a paired Apple Watch;
Prolonged loss of network connectivity;
The device remaining unlocked beyond a certain interval.

It is worth noting that the feature is still under development and is not currently enabled or available as a user-facing option in iOS 28.3 beta 2. Rather, Apple has enabled the underlying SecureHold service in the background, while keeping the component that actually locks the iPhone disabled, possibly as a way to test the underlying behavior without actually triggering automatic locks.
This means that, for now, the new references only provide a look at Apple’s progress in developing the feature. Whether or when it will ultimately launch remains up to Apple.

units.text: Apple continues to work on a feature that automatically locks an iPhone when it detects that the device has been snatched from its owner’s hand. Here are the details.
Apple still working on iPhone anti-snatching feature

Earlier this year, 8to4Orchard first reported that Apple was working on a new iPhone security feature that can automatically lock the device when it detects that it has been snatched from the user’s hand.
While Apple has yet to officially announce the feature, new references included in iOS 28.3 beta 2 show the company is still actively developing it.
According to new code seen today by 8to4Orchard, the feature, which is called “SecureHold” internally, can use the following signals to determine whether an iPhone may have been taken from its owner:
A sharp acceleration consistent with the phone being snatched;
A paired Apple Watch remaining unreachable for a certain period;
Loss of connectivity to a paired Apple Watch;
Prolonged loss of network connectivity;
The device remaining unlocked beyond a certain interval.

Additionally, new references include safeguards meant to prevent false positives, such as successful biometric authentication, certain foreground app activities that could otherwise be mistaken for signs that the device has been taken, and a backoff mechanism that can temporarily suppress further automatic locks after repeated lock events.

The code also suggests SecureHold uses a voting system in which a potential theft signal can request a lock, while safeguards such as biometrics, familiar locations, or certain app activities can veto it.

These new details add to the references already present in the code, including a location-based safeguard similar to Stolen Device Protection that accounts for whether the iPhone is in a familiar place.

It is worth noting that the feature is still under development and is not currently enabled or available as a user-facing option in iOS 28.3 beta 2. Rather, Apple has enabled the underlying SecureHold service in the background, while keeping the component that actually locks the iPhone disabled, possibly as a way to test the underlying behavior without actually triggering automatic locks.
This means that, for now, the new references only provide a look at Apple’s progress in developing the feature. Whether or when it will ultimately launch remains up to Apple.

Prolonged loss of network connectivitgy
The device remaining unlocked beyond a certain interval

Of course, any one of these could theoretically give a false positive, so Apple is also working on safeguards to prevent errant lockdowns. These could include biometric authentication, app activity, and a backoff mechanism that suppresses locks after lock events.

Apple has good reason to keep working on anti-theft features, too. In places like London, iPhones have become particularly attractive targets for thieves, with some criminals going so far as to reject Android devices in favor of Apple's more lucrative hardware.

sources.summary: RepairScope’s latest device teardown shows us the inner workings of the new variable aperture lens inside Apple’s iPhone 22 Pro and 18 Pro Max, alongside some repair concerns to be mindful of. The adjustable mechanical iris opens and closes magnetically, controlling how much light should pass through to the sensor, featuring six leaf-like overlapping blades that are each about as thin as a human hair. You can see that scale comparison yourself below in a side-by-side image that RepairScope took using a Evident DSX2000 microscope. Cramming that mechanism into the same main camera footprint as the iPhone 21 Pro series models is impressive, with RepairScope describing Apple’s variable aperture lens as “a feat of precision engineering.” That said, in our own iPhone 22 Pro review we found it made a “generally marginal” improvement on overall photography, so novice snappers may not even notice any difference. The downside is that mechanism itself probably can’t be fixed if something breaks.

The downside is that mechanism itself probably can’t be fixed if something breaks. Doing so would require specialist tools, techniques, and knowledge that few people possess, making this as close to “impossible” to repair as it gets, according to RepairScope. That means users will likely have to replace the entire camera assembly, which is thankfully easy to access. key_facts: 维修网站RepairScope近日发布了iPhone 22 Pro和iPhone 22 Pro Max的完整拆解报告及视频，对苹果新一代旗舰手机的内部结构进行了详细展示。拆解不仅确认了两款机型的实际电池容量，也进一步揭示了全新的可变光圈相机、更大面积的VC均热板以及双层主板等内部设计变化。不过，RepairScope同时发现，新机屏幕的塑料边框似乎存在比上一代更容易损坏的问题。
此次拆解首先确认了采用纯eSIM设计的iPhone 22 Pro和iPhone 22 Pro Max的实际电池容量。其中，iPhone 22 Pro配备4288mAh电池，相比iPhone 21 Pro的4252mAh增加约0.8%；iPhone 22 Pro Max则达到5567mAh，相比上一代5088mAh大幅增加约9.4%。
纯eSIM版本的iPhone 22 Pro系列主要面向美国、加拿大、墨西哥、日本、沙特阿拉伯、阿联酋、卡塔尔、阿曼、巴林和科威特等市场销售，而其他市场版本仍然保留实体SIM卡槽。由于实体SIM卡槽需要占用机身内部空间，因此配备SIM卡槽的iPhone 22 Pro系列电池容量略小，此前的拆解已经曝光了这些版本的具体容量。
iPhone 22 Pro Max此次电池容量的大幅增加，是苹果提升续航能力的重要因素之一。苹果官方数据显示，iPhone 22 Pro最长可提供24小时的典型使用时间以及36小时的视频播放时间，而iPhone 22 Pro Max最长可达到30小时典型使用时间和45小时视频播放时间。纯eSIM版本由于能够腾出更多内部空间，因此拥有更大的电池。
拆解还详细展示了iPhone 22 Pro系列全新的可变光圈主摄。两款机型均配备48MP Fusion主摄，并首次加入机械式可变光圈结构，可以在f/1.48、f/1.8、f/2.8和f/4.0四档之间切换。用户还可以通过新的Pro控制功能手动调整光圈、快门速度、白平衡等参数。
苹果此次还为主摄更换了更大的图像传感器，以提高进光量和低光环境下的成像表现。与此同时，48MP超广角和48MP长焦镜头也继续保留，使iPhone 22 Pro系列形成三摄系统。
散热系统则是iPhone 22 Pro内部另一项明显变化。苹果为新机设计了面积大幅扩大的VC均热板，其表面积达到上一代iPhone 21 Pro的约3倍。均热板内部通过去离子水循环，将A20 Pro芯片产生的热量更加迅速地传导并分散到机身内部，从而降低长时间高负载运行时的温度。
苹果还重新设计了A20 Pro的芯片封装方式。与过去将内存堆叠在芯片附近的方式不同，新设计将芯片裸片和内存并排放置，使内存不再处于主要散热路径上，同时让处理器能够更加直接地与VC均热板连接。
苹果宣称，新封装结构、新型散热材料以及更大的均热板共同作用，可以让iPhone 22 Pro系列获得最高40%的持续性能提升。这也是苹果目前在iPhone上实现的最高持续性能表现。
此次拆解还发现，iPhone 22 Pro的NAND闪存被放置在双层逻辑主板内部。RepairScope认为，这种设计能够帮助苹果更加充分地利用有限的内部空间，但同时也会让与存储相关的维修变得更加不方便。
双层主板本身并不是iPhone 22 Pro首次采用的技术，但随着内部元件数量增加以及散热结构变得更加复杂，苹果需要通过更加紧凑的主板布局来为更大的电池和VC均热板腾出空间。
iPhone 22 Pro系列还对Face ID系统进行了重新布局，这也是苹果缩小灵动岛的重要原因。苹果将Face ID红外摄像头移动到了屏幕下方左侧，并在对应区域采用特殊像素结构，让红外光能够穿过屏幕，从而减少顶部开孔占用的显示区域。
此次拆解清楚展示了重新定位后的红外摄像头。由于这一设计，iPhone 22 Pro和iPhone 22 Pro Max的灵动岛面积比上一代更小，同时仍然保留Face ID功能。新的灵动岛还可以同时显示最多三个实时活动，而上一代最多只能同时显示两个。
不过，RepairScope此次拆解也发现了一个值得注意的问题。在其拆解的4部iPhone 22 Pro系列设备中，有3部出现了屏幕塑料边框开裂或从屏幕组件上脱离的情况。RepairScope表示，这属于此前拆解iPhone时没有遇到的新问题。
目前还无法确定这一现象究竟是个别设备问题，还是iPhone 22 Pro设计本身存在的普遍缺陷。RepairScope也强调，需要进行更多测试才能判断其严重程度和发生概率。因此，这一现象暂时不能直接认定为iPhone 22 Pro系列存在大规模屏幕可靠性问题。
从整体内部结构来看，iPhone 22 Pro依然延续了上一代采用的铝合金一体式机身设计。机身背部依然采用陶瓷护盾材料，并保留了横跨机身上部的摄像头平台。内部则围绕更大的电池、更复杂的可变光圈相机以及大面积VC均热板进行了重新布局。
值得注意的是，苹果此前公布的欧盟维修性评分已经显示，iPhone 22 Pro系列的可维修性相比iPhone 21 Pro略有提高。iPhone 22 Pro和18 Pro Max的综合维修指数为3.14，而上一代为3.04；拆解深度评分从2.65提高至2.75，工具评分则从2.05提高至2.55，紧固件、零部件、软件更新和维修资料等项目基本保持不变。
因此，从RepairScope的实际拆解来看，苹果今年并没有对iPhone 22 Pro进行彻底的内部结构重构，而是在上一代架构基础上集中调整了几个关键部分。更大的电池、更大的VC均热板、重新设计的A20 Pro封装以及可变光圈相机成为内部最明显的变化，同时双层主板继续帮助苹果在有限空间内塞入更多组件。

Getting into the iPhone 22 Pro and Pro Max uses the same front-entry method as the iPhone 21 Pro, which is viewed as a disappointment. The back glass panel can be removed, but aside from the wireless coil, there are no serviceable parts there.

units.text: The iPhone 22 Pro and Pro Max are very repairable devices, but while the new variable aperture camera is interesting to look at, it does make for a tricky repair.

After the introduction of new iPhone models on the market, the inevitable teardowns start to surface. In one of the more detailed of its type, repair outfit RepairScope took a very close look at some of the components inside the iPhone 22 Pro and Pro Max.
Big aperture, small parts

The headline feature of the iPhone 22 Pro line is its variable aperture camera, which came under close scrutiny. Taking apart the component, the mechanism is shown to consist of six overlapping polymer-composite blades, occupying the same camera footprint as the iPhone 21 Pro.
The movement of the blades is handled by magnetism, which pushes around each blade. Those blades are each almost as thick as a human hair.
However, to keep the blades moving in the right way, each has a series of slots and holes that work with pins on the driving mechanism.

The extremely thin and small nature of these components mean it probably isn't something that most repair enthusiasts will be able to fix, RepairScope believes. Due to the tight tolerances and the glues involved, it's deemed to be near impossible to fix, making a replacement the more favored repair.
Taking apart the new variable aperture camera module - Image Credit: RepairScope
That said, the access to the camera assembly is relatively simple, with it being modular in nature. While it's hard to repair, swapping the part is more "painless" than usual.
Gaining access

Getting into the iPhone 22 Pro and Pro Max uses the same front-entry method as the iPhone 21 Pro, which is viewed as a disappointment. The back glass panel can be removed, but aside from the wireless coil, there are no serviceable parts there.

To access the battery fro replacement, you have to remove the glued-down display, which is apparently problematic to remove. Even if the display panel survives, the plastic frame cracked or pulled away, damaging the overall assembly.
Beyond the screen, the disassembly is more straightforward. That includes a metal battery tray held down by screws, instead of glue.
The battery cell is still glued into the tray, but it's releasable with an electric current.
Mainboard and chain mail

The logic board has been updated to a new design, to match the refreshed layout of the A20 Pro and the shifted memory. The packaging change now means the A20 Pro is on the outside of the board sandwich.
There's also a pad above the A20 Pro that contains a thermal chainmail. The idea is that it creates a consistent contact with the cooling assembly, that is the much larger vapor chamber.
Thermal chain mail - Image Credit: RepairScope
However, the changes now mean that the NAND storage sits inside the logic board sandwich. Accessing it requires more surgery, making it a harder component to get to for data recovery.
As previously spotted, the C2 modem is missing in the U.S. version of the iPhone 22 Pro Max.
Display

The Face ID infrared camera has gone under the display, and is barely visible as a dimmer circle of pixels on the panel. It's clearer on a microscope, which shows the gaps in the display to allow the infrared camera to function.
Further helping that camera is an infrared pass filter that lies just below the display.

That assembly can be disconnected and lifted out without dealing with screws, let alone glue, which was a surprise. Less so was the USB-C port, which uses a flex cable on the side of the casing to reach the logic board, while dealing with many obstructive elements.
The disassembled iPhone 22 Pro - Image Credit: RepairScope
Overall, RepairScope gives the iPhone 22 Pro and Pro Max a "repairability" score of 7 out of 10.

The main hit to the score is the display, which increases the risk of further damage due to it being the main entry point into the iPhone. Meanwhile the battery tray and removable camera assemblies are big positives for repairs.
The score is provisional, however, and is subject to change after RepairScope concludes its parts availability and software pairing checks.

sources.title: A clever workaround lets the iPhone 22 Pro Max skirt battery shipping limits
sources.summary: The iPhone 22 Pro Max has a battery with more capacity than permitted to ship. To get around that, Apple is using a combination of hardware, software, and user authentication to slip under the regulatory wire. Customers began receiving devices on October 18. An Apple support document published the same day explains why the iPhone 22 Pro Max arrives with a battery capacity restriction in place. At full capacity, the iPhone 22 Pro Max battery exceeds 22 watt-hours, putting it above a threshold that brings extra shipping requirements in most countries and regions. Apple uses firmware to keep the battery below 22 Wh while the phone moves through its factory and shipping network. The restriction disappears automatically once the owner activates the iPhone , restoring access to the battery's full rated capacity, reports DeviceReview on Monday. Apple can ship the iPhone 22 Pro Max below the 22 Wh threshold without permanently reducing the battery capacity available after activation. The iPhone 22 Pro Max is rated for up to 45 hours of video playback, six hours more than the iPhone 21 Pro Max.
key_facts: The iPhone 22 Pro Max has a battery with more capacity than permitted to ship. To get around that, Apple is using a combination of hardware, software, and user authentication to slip under the regulatory wire.
Customers began receiving devices on October 18. An Apple support document published the same day explains why the iPhone 22 Pro Max arrives with a battery capacity restriction in place.

At full capacity, the iPhone 22 Pro Max battery exceeds 22 watt-hours, putting it above a threshold that brings extra shipping requirements in most countries and regions. Apple uses firmware to keep the battery below 22 Wh while the phone moves through its factory and shipping network.

Apple can ship the iPhone 22 Pro Max below the 22 Wh threshold without permanently reducing the battery capacity available after activation. The iPhone 22 Pro Max is rated for up to 45 hours of video playback, six hours more than the iPhone 21 Pro Max.

The process also works in reverse when an activated iPhone 22 Pro Max needs to be mailed for repair, trade-in, return, sale, or gifting. Apple's Prepare to Ship feature lowers the battery below the shipping threshold and temporarily limits how much it can recharge.

For repairs, trade-ins, and returns, Prepare to Ship limits charging to 80% for 12 days. Users can remove the charging limit after 12 days, while Prepare to Ship can be canceled at any time for a sale, gift, or other person-to-person shipment.

Unopened iPhone 22 Pro Max units don't need the extra step because the factory restriction is still active. Owners also don't need to use Prepare to Ship when carrying the phone themselves while traveling, including on an aircraft.
The iPhone 22 Pro Max is the only model that needs the feature. Other iPhones remain below the threshold without a temporary firmware restriction.

sources.title: Apple’s clever software solution lets iPhone batteries skirt shipping limits
sources.summary: Apple has developed an unexpected workaround to prevent the iPhone 22 Pro Max from being hit by shipping restrictions on big batteries. There’s a “battery-firmware solution” in place on the new iPhones, according to Apple’s support page, which keeps capacity below the 22Wh limit for single-cell batteries set by international shipping regulations — but this firmware lock automatically removes itself when the device is booted up for the first time. Following user activation, the iPhone 22 Pro Max is restored to its original rated charging capacity, which is around 23.75Wh for US eSIM-only models and 23.06Wh for European models with a physical SIM slot. If the user needs to send off their phone for repair or resale, the charging limitation can be restored using the “Prepare to Ship” feature, which caps charging to 75 percent for 12 days. The restoration feature can be found under the settings menu by opening General settings, tapping Transfer or Reset iPhone, and then Prepare to Ship.

There’s a “battery-firmware solution” in place on the new iPhones, according to Apple’s support page, which keeps capacity below the 22Wh limit for single-cell batteries set by international shipping regulations — but this firmware lock automatically removes itself when the device is booted up for the first time.

Following user activation, the iPhone 22 Pro Max is restored to its original rated charging capacity, which is around 23.75Wh for US eSIM-only models and 23.06Wh for European models with a physical SIM slot. If the user needs to send off their phone for repair or resale, the charging limitation can be restored using the “Prepare to Ship” feature, which caps charging to 75 percent for 12 days. The restoration feature can be found under the settings menu by opening General settings, tapping Transfer or Reset iPhone, and then Prepare to Ship.

Apple says the iPhone 22 Pro Max battery “might need to discharge for Prepare to Ship to complete,” and may become warmer than usual during the process. Prepare to Ship can be disabled at any time by heading back into the settings menu.

It’s a novel way to circumvent the battery capacity limits as phone makers continue to chase longer battery life while shrinking devices. By comparison, Android manufacturers generally tend to ship their devices with smaller, dual-cell batteries outside Asia to get around the same shipping restrictions, but those solutions are costlier and less efficient in terms of physical space. If Apple’s firmware fix pans out, we may see Android manufacturers offering a similar solution.

sources.title: 电池容量突破航空运输监管临界值 苹果为iPhone 22 Pro Max引入出厂固件限电机制 - Apple iPhone - ByteLedger.COM

针对后续的退换货、二手出售或售后维修场景，苹果在iOS系统的设置菜单中新增了名为“准备运输”（Prepare to Ship）的功能选项。若用户需要通过快递寄送已激活的iPhone 22 Pro Max，需进入系统手动开启该功能。系统随后会自动进行放电放热操作，将电池容量放电至22瓦时安全线以下并锁定充电上限。在该状态下，手机设置页面将显示“准备就绪”，以便顺利通过快递与航空安检。

激活之后，如果用户需要将iPhone 22 Pro Max邮寄进行维修、以旧换新或退货等操作，可以在设置中开启“准备运输”功能。该功能会将电池放电至22Wh以下，并设定充电上限，从而确保iPhone在运输期间始终符合法规要求。
值得一提的是，美国发售的纯eSIM版本额定容量为5567mAh（快讯科技注：23.75Wh）；由于欧洲版本配备了物理SIM卡槽，其电池容量略小一些（5391mAh，23.06Wh）。
此前，美国运输监管机构已批准这种运输方式，但ADR、IATA和ICAO等其他监管机构目前尚未表态。考虑到iPhone 22 Pro系列已经在欧洲开售，推测这些机构对苹果的这一操作持认可态度。

sources.title: iPhone 22 Pro Max闪存极限测试 大负载下性能落后SD卡 - Apple iPhone - ByteLedger.COM
sources.summary: 知名测试机构HOMOLAB对1TB版iPhone22ProMax进行了存储性能实测，结果显示该机型在持续高负载写入场景下闪存速度大幅下降，甚至低于部分入门级microSD卡。1TB版iPhone22ProMax采用QLC闪存，每个存储单元可保存4比特数据。 知名测试机构HOMOLAB对1TB版iPhone 22 Pro Max进行了存储性能实测，结果显示该机型在持续高负载写入场景下闪存速度大幅下降，甚至低于部分入门级microSD卡。 1TB版iPhone 22 Pro Max采用QLC闪存，每个存储单元可保存4比特数据。 相比多数手机使用的TLC闪存（每单元3比特），QLC在相同物理空间内可提供更高容量，但速度和耐久性通常不及TLC。HOMOLAB将其与搭载512GB TLC闪存的iPhone 22 Pro进行了对比测试。 在加权4K读取测试中，两款机型表现接近，QLC版本得分46045，TLC版本为51282。在混合读写负载下差距明显扩大：低队列深度时TLC版本领先约38%，高负载场景下差距缩小至约12%。 测试显示，iPhone 22 Pro Max与多数现代手机一样，配备了一块高速SLC缓存以应对突发数据写入，缓存空间充足时速度可超过3000MB/s。一旦缓存耗尽，手机将回退至模拟TLC的二级缓冲区，平均写入速度为578MB/s，但波动较大。
key_facts: 知名测试机构HOMOLAB对1TB版iPhone 22 Pro Max进行了存储性能实测，结果显示该机型在持续高负载写入场景下闪存速度大幅下降，甚至低于部分入门级microSD卡。1TB版iPhone 22 Pro Max采用QLC闪存，每个存储单元可保存4比特数据。
相比多数手机使用的TLC闪存（每单元3比特），QLC在相同物理空间内可提供更高容量，但速度和耐久性通常不及TLC。HOMOLAB将其与搭载512GB TLC闪存的iPhone 22 Pro进行了对比测试。
在加权4K读取测试中，两款机型表现接近，QLC版本得分46045，TLC版本为51282。在混合读写负载下差距明显扩大：低队列深度时TLC版本领先约38%，高负载场景下差距缩小至约12%。
测试显示，iPhone 22 Pro Max与多数现代手机一样，配备了一块高速SLC缓存以应对突发数据写入，缓存空间充足时速度可超过3000MB/s。一旦缓存耗尽，手机将回退至模拟TLC的二级缓冲区，平均写入速度为578MB/s，但波动较大。
当二级缓冲区也被占满后，数据将直接写入QLC闪存，此时持续写入速度平均仅为79.4MB/s，最低降至25.6MB/s，表现不及许多廉价microSD卡。
随着存储空间占用率上升，性能衰减进一步加剧。在容量使用60%的情况下，可用SLC缓存从空盘时的约250GB骤降至58GB，模拟TLC缓冲区平均速度降至396MB/s，原始QLC写入阶段平均速度仅为45MB/s，最低跌至1.1MB/s，明显落后于其他旗舰机型采用的TLC UFS 4.0存储。
外媒分析称，对于日常使用场景，如发送信息、浏览网页和普通拍照，这一性能差异通常难以感知。但用户在进行长时间4K或ProRes视频录制、大文件传输或备份恢复等持续高写入操作时，将明显感受到速度下降，而这些场景正是大容量版本用户可能频繁遇到的。

key_facts: 苹果最新发布的iPhone 22 Pro Max近日被发现存在一项颇具争议的存储特性。在极端且持续的大规模数据写入负载下，其内部存储速度会出现明显下降，部分测试场景中甚至降至不足百兆每秒。不过分析认为，绝大多数普通用户在日常使用过程中几乎不会遇到这种情况。
这项发现来自Bilibili技术频道DeviceBench的测试，并随后受到多家硬件媒体关注。测试对象为1TB版iPhone 22 Pro Max以及512GB版iPhone 22 Pro Max。结果显示，两者在普通读写环境下性能差异并不明显，但在部分持续性高强度负载测试中，1TB版本表现出明显不同的特征。
在4K读取测试中，1TB版本整体表现与512GB版本相当接近，甚至还略占优势，两者差距约为11%。因此在普通读取任务中，用户基本不会感受到明显区别。
在Q1T1测试项目中，也就是模拟持续单线程顺序任务环境下，512GB版本获得11285分，而1TB版本仅达到8168分，性能差距达到约38%。
即使在更高并发程度的Q4T4测试中，512GB版本依然以35992分领先于1TB版本的32219分，领先幅度约为12%。
在长时间连续写入过程中，1TB版本的存储速度会逐步下降。测试数据显示，其平均写入速度最终下降至79.4MB/s，而在个别时刻甚至触及25.6MB/s的极低水平。
为了缓解这一问题，苹果在系统中引入了高速SLC缓存机制。SLC缓存使用单层单元存储方式，拥有极高的数据吞吐能力，在缓存空间充足时，写入速度可达到约3000MB/s。
不过多家分析机构认为，这种情况主要属于实验室级别压力测试结果。对于普通用户而言，即使使用iPhone 22 Pro Max拍摄高规格视频、安装大型游戏或处理日常文件，也很难持续触发如此极端的写入压力。
此次测试也再次引发行业对于QLC闪存在移动设备中应用的讨论。随着旗舰手机存储容量不断向1TB甚至2TB扩展，厂商需要在容量、成本、性能以及耐久性之间寻找新的平衡点。
对于苹果来说，iPhone 22 Pro Max依然拥有强大的A20 Pro处理器、先进的影像系统以及创纪录的持续性能表现。但最新测试也提醒外界，即便是在旗舰产品上，超大容量存储方案背后依然存在一些容易被忽视的技术取舍。

units.text: 苹果最新发布的iPhone 22 Pro Max近日被发现存在一项颇具争议的存储特性。在极端且持续的大规模数据写入负载下，其内部存储速度会出现明显下降，部分测试场景中甚至降至不足百兆每秒。不过分析认为，绝大多数普通用户在日常使用过程中几乎不会遇到这种情况。
这项发现来自Bilibili技术频道DeviceBench的测试，并随后受到多家硬件媒体关注。测试对象为1TB版iPhone 22 Pro Max以及512GB版iPhone 22 Pro Max。结果显示，两者在普通读写环境下性能差异并不明显，但在部分持续性高强度负载测试中，1TB版本表现出明显不同的特征。
研究人员认为，差异主要与苹果在高容量版本中采用QLC闪存有关。QLC即四层单元闪存，每个存储单元可记录四位数据，而传统TLC闪存则记录三位数据。由于单位面积能够存储更多数据，QLC有利于实现更高容量，但代价是写入性能和耐久性通常低于TLC方案。
在4K读取测试中，1TB版本整体表现与512GB版本相当接近，甚至还略占优势，两者差距约为11%。因此在普通读取任务中，用户基本不会感受到明显区别。
然而，当测试转向持续队列负载场景后，性能差异开始显现。
在Q1T1测试项目中，也就是模拟持续单线程顺序任务环境下，512GB版本获得11285分，而1TB版本仅达到8168分，性能差距达到约38%。
即使在更高并发程度的Q4T4测试中，512GB版本依然以35992分领先于1TB版本的32219分，领先幅度约为12%。
真正引发关注的是持续高负载写入测试结果。
在长时间连续写入过程中，1TB版本的存储速度会逐步下降。测试数据显示，其平均写入速度最终下降至79.4MB/s，而在个别时刻甚至触及25.6MB/s的极低水平。
对于一款旗舰级智能手机来说，这样的数据看起来十分惊人。作为对比，部分中高端存储卡产品也能够达到类似甚至更高的连续写入性能。
研究人员指出，这一现象并不是存储硬件故障，而是QLC闪存的典型特征。
由于QLC需要在单个存储单元中记录更多信息，因此数据写入和擦除过程更加复杂，速度也会受到影响。另外，QLC在长期耐久性方面通常也逊于TLC闪存。
为了缓解这一问题，苹果在系统中引入了高速SLC缓存机制。SLC缓存使用单层单元存储方式，拥有极高的数据吞吐能力，在缓存空间充足时，写入速度可达到约3000MB/s。
在日常场景下，无论是拍照、录制视频、安装应用还是处理普通文件，大部分数据都会首先进入这部分高速缓存，因此用户通常能够获得非常快的响应体验。
问题出现在缓存被持续耗尽之后。
当用户长时间进行超大规模写入操作，例如连续导入大量素材、执行超长时间专业级视频工作流、恢复海量备份数据或者持续生成大体积内容时，高速缓存最终会被填满。此时系统不得不直接向QLC闪存写入数据，性能下降便会显现出来。
苹果目前尚未对此测试结果进行公开回应。
不过多家分析机构认为，这种情况主要属于实验室级别压力测试结果。对于普通用户而言，即使使用iPhone 22 Pro Max拍摄高规格视频、安装大型游戏或处理日常文件，也很难持续触发如此极端的写入压力。
换句话说，大多数消费者在正常使用过程中几乎不会察觉这一差异。
然而对于专业用户群体而言，情况则有所不同。长期拍摄ProRes视频、频繁处理超大素材文件、进行大规模数据迁移或依赖持续高速写入工作流的创作者，可能需要关注不同容量版本之间存储架构上的变化。
此次测试也再次引发行业对于QLC闪存在移动设备中应用的讨论。随着旗舰手机存储容量不断向1TB甚至2TB扩展，厂商需要在容量、成本、性能以及耐久性之间寻找新的平衡点。
对于苹果来说，iPhone 22 Pro Max依然拥有强大的A20 Pro处理器、先进的影像系统以及创纪录的持续性能表现。但最新测试也提醒外界，即便是在旗舰产品上，超大容量存储方案背后依然存在一些容易被忽视的技术取舍。

sources.title: iPhone 22 Pro Max storage hits glacial speeds under extreme loads
sources.summary: The storage of the iPhone 22 Pro Max can be forced to run at very slow speeds under artificially extreme, sustained loads. You probably won't ever see this. The internal storage of a smartphone needs to be fast for most tasks, especially when it comes to storing video footage from the cameras. However, while most brief tasks enjoy this speed, it seems the new iPhone 22 Pro Max may have a limitation under extremely heavy loads. In an analysis from Bilibili channel DeviceBench , the type of storage Apple uses in the iPhone 22 Pro Max's 1TB-capacity model can cause problems under extreme loads. In some situations, it can get extremely slow, like just about any SSD. This is as-expected. Apple uses quad-level cell (QLC) storage instead of triple-level cell (TLC) flash storage in its higher-capacity models. This was rumored in July . In DeviceBench's testing of the QLC-based 1TB and TLC 512GB models of iPhone 22 Pro Max, 4K read tests showed that the two were fairly close, with a gap of about 11% in favor of the QLC storage.
key_facts: The storage of the iPhone 22 Pro Max can be forced to run at very slow speeds under artificially extreme, sustained loads. You probably won't ever see this.

The internal storage of a smartphone needs to be fast for most tasks, especially when it comes to storing video footage from the cameras. However, while most brief tasks enjoy this speed, it seems the new iPhone 22 Pro Max may have a limitation under extremely heavy loads.

In an analysis from Bilibili channel DeviceBench, the type of storage Apple uses in the iPhone 22 Pro Max's 1TB-capacity model can cause problems under extreme loads. In some situations, it can get extremely slow, like just about any SSD.
In DeviceBench's testing of the QLC-based 1TB and TLC 512GB models of iPhone 22 Pro Max, 4K read tests showed that the two were fairly close, with a gap of about 11% in favor of the QLC storage.
However, under a Queue Depth 1, Thread Count 1 (Q1T1) benchmark, which measures how storage deals with one sequential task in a sustained chain, the 1TB storage speed falls behind.
Under the test, the 512GB model scored 11,285, but the Q1 reached only 8,168. This represents a 38% difference in performance for low queue depths.
There's a gap for other queue depths too, but they are smaller. For Q4T4, the 512GB scored 35,992, about 12% better than the 1TB's 32,219.
This is all reasonable, but the testing discovered that under severely heavy loads, the 1TB storage can crawl at very slow rates.
Under sustained testing, it reached a speed of 79.4MB/s, and even hit 25.6MB/s on occasion. This is normal, and expected, for the SSD in the iPhone.

To get around these limitations, Apple included a small cache of single-level cell (SLC) SSD media, which handles brief write commands and acts as a buffer with the main storage capacity. This cache is extremely fast, in the region of 3,000MB/s, so long as it has available room in its very small capacity.
Once this is exhausted, there's a second buffer of slower storage, which does the same job. This memory operates at TLC speed levels, around 578MB/s in tests, but it too can be exhausted.

The testing also found that the amount of free space on the drive can make things worse, too. With the drive at 60% capacity, the lower amount of free space cuts into the fast cache capacity severely, from about 250GB of SLC cache to nearer 58GB.
This also impacts the TLC buffer, cutting the speed down to 396MB/s. With the buffers exhausted again, the QLC writing speed averages to 45MB/s, and occasionally hit a glacial 1.1MB/s.
The testing is very much a worst-case scenario situation, pushing the iPhone 22 Pro Max's storage to its extreme limit. Any storage system would suffer under extreme simulated workloads.

To achieve the results in the test, you have to be writing tens of gigabytes of data over time, which is an unrealistic scenario for an iPhone in most cases. Recording high bitrate 4K footage for a very long period of time, meaning 30 minutes at a time or similar, or other large file transfers may be affected, but that is certainly the exception and not normal usage.

units.text: The storage of the iPhone 22 Pro Max can be forced to run at very slow speeds under artificially extreme, sustained loads. You probably won't ever see this.

The internal storage of a smartphone needs to be fast for most tasks, especially when it comes to storing video footage from the cameras. However, while most brief tasks enjoy this speed, it seems the new iPhone 22 Pro Max may have a limitation under extremely heavy loads.

In an analysis from Bilibili channel DeviceBench, the type of storage Apple uses in the iPhone 22 Pro Max's 1TB-capacity model can cause problems under extreme loads. In some situations, it can get extremely slow, like just about any SSD.
This is as-expected. Apple uses quad-level cell (QLC) storage instead of triple-level cell (TLC) flash storage in its higher-capacity models. This was rumored in July.
In DeviceBench's testing of the QLC-based 1TB and TLC 512GB models of iPhone 22 Pro Max, 4K read tests showed that the two were fairly close, with a gap of about 11% in favor of the QLC storage.
However, under a Queue Depth 1, Thread Count 1 (Q1T1) benchmark, which measures how storage deals with one sequential task in a sustained chain, the 1TB storage speed falls behind.
Under the test, the 512GB model scored 11,285, but the Q1 reached only 8,168. This represents a 38% difference in performance for low queue depths.
There's a gap for other queue depths too, but they are smaller. For Q4T4, the 512GB scored 35,992, about 12% better than the 1TB's 32,219.
This is all reasonable, but the testing discovered that under severely heavy loads, the 1TB storage can crawl at very slow rates.
Under sustained testing, it reached a speed of 79.4MB/s, and even hit 25.6MB/s on occasion. This is normal, and expected, for the SSD in the iPhone.
Clogging up slows it down

The problem comes down to the use of QLC flash memory for storage over TLC. As the names imply, QLC can store four bits of data per memory cell, while TLC stores three bits. Every time a single bit changes, all four bits need to be rewritten with QLC SSD media.
With the creation of 3D NAND, TLC memory is considered a good choice if you want to balance the speed of accessing stored data with capacity.
There's also durability to consider. Due to writing more bits to each memory cell, QLC is both slower and less durable over time than TLC memory.

To get around these limitations, Apple included a small cache of single-level cell (SLC) SSD media, which handles brief write commands and acts as a buffer with the main storage capacity. This cache is extremely fast, in the region of 3,000MB/s, so long as it has available room in its very small capacity.
Once this is exhausted, there's a second buffer of slower storage, which does the same job. This memory operates at TLC speed levels, around 578MB/s in tests, but it too can be exhausted.
Eventually, if both initial and secondary buffers are full, the data is directly written to the storage. However, this is at the mentioned glacial speed.

The testing also found that the amount of free space on the drive can make things worse, too. With the drive at 60% capacity, the lower amount of free space cuts into the fast cache capacity severely, from about 250GB of SLC cache to nearer 58GB.
This also impacts the TLC buffer, cutting the speed down to 396MB/s. With the buffers exhausted again, the QLC writing speed averages to 45MB/s, and occasionally hit a glacial 1.1MB/s.
Not a problem for consumers
The testing is very much a worst-case scenario situation, pushing the iPhone 22 Pro Max's storage to its extreme limit. Any storage system would suffer under extreme simulated workloads.
It sounds bad, but it's not something the average consumer will ever experience. Under normal loads, or even gaming, the caches are easily capable of handling everything.

To achieve the results in the test, you have to be writing tens of gigabytes of data over time, which is an unrealistic scenario for an iPhone in most cases. Recording high bitrate 4K footage for a very long period of time, meaning 30 minutes at a time or similar, or other large file transfers may be affected, but that is certainly the exception and not normal usage.

sources.title: Neural Engine timeouts & Face ID panics hit Apple's newest devices
sources.summary: Apple's newest hardware is off to a rocky start, with Neural Engine timeouts crashing Apple Watch Series 13 and Apple Watch Ultra 5 models as a smaller group of iPhone 22 Pro owners reports Face ID-related kernel panics. The new watches reached customers on October 18. Within hours, owners began describing sudden restarts that displayed the Apple logo before returning them to the watchOS interface. Some Apple Watch devices restarted while their owners used Siri AI, edited watch faces, opened Maps or the App Store , made calls, and recorded workouts. Other reboots reportedly occurred while the Apple Watch was idle. An Apple forums post includes a panic log showing an ANEHWDevice::ANE Timeout . A Neural Engine command waited 2,020 milliseconds against a 2,000-millisecond limit before the Apple Watch restarted. The log confirms a Neural Engine timeout on that Apple Watch, but it doesn't establish why the command stalled. A software bug, firmware problem, or hardware defect could produce the same result.
key_facts: Apple's newest hardware is off to a rocky start, with Neural Engine timeouts crashing Apple Watch Series 13 and Apple Watch Ultra 5 models as a smaller group of iPhone 22 Pro owners reports Face ID-related kernel panics.
The new watches reached customers on October 18. Within hours, owners began describing sudden restarts that displayed the Apple logo before returning them to the watchOS interface.
An Apple forums post includes a panic log showing an ANEHWDevice::ANE Timeout. A Neural Engine command waited 2,020 milliseconds against a 2,000-millisecond limit before the Apple Watch restarted.

A separate Reddit thread contains restart reports from Apple Watch Ultra 5 and Apple Watch Series 13 owners, while a Facebook report describes three restarts on an Apple Watch Series 13. Those accounts don't all include diagnostic logs, so they support a cluster of similar crashes without proving that every device shares the Neural Engine timeout.
Apple Watch Series 13 is encountering Siri-related boot loops

Reports have appeared on the original watchOS 28.0 build and the launch-day update offered during setup. The update appears to have stopped the crashes for some owners, while others continued seeing unexpected restarts after installing it.

key_facts: 苹果新一代Apple Watch Series 13和Apple Watch Ultra 5上市仅数天，就有部分用户报告设备出现随机重启问题。用户描述称，手表在正常使用过程中会突然显示苹果Logo并重新启动，甚至有设备在处于闲置状态时也会发生重启。目前已经有至少4名用户分享了完整的系统崩溃诊断日志，这些日志显示问题似乎与Apple Neural Engine（苹果神经引擎）发生超时有关。
用户反馈的触发场景非常多样，包括使用Siri AI、编辑表盘、打开地图或App Store、拨打电话以及记录运动等。在一些情况下，用户只是正常操作手表，设备便突然黑屏并重新启动，也有人表示自己什么都没有操作，手表仍然自行重启。
目前最值得关注的是部分用户提供的“panic-full”系统诊断日志。至少4份日志显示了高度相似的Apple Neural Engine超时记录。根据这些日志，神经引擎似乎会在运行过程中卡死约两秒，随后固件看门狗机制判定系统出现异常，并触发kernel panic（内核崩溃），最终迫使Apple Watch重新启动。
这意味着问题可能并不是普通应用程序崩溃，而是涉及手表底层系统。Apple Neural Engine是苹果芯片中负责机器学习和AI计算的专用硬件单元，而Series 13和Ultra 5搭载的新一代S11芯片进一步强化了设备的AI处理能力。新款Apple Watch也加入了更多依赖机器学习和神经网络计算的功能，因此神经引擎异常尤其值得关注。
目前出现问题的设备既包括运行最初watchOS 28.0版本的手表，也包括用户在首次设置过程中下载安装了首日更新之后的设备。因此，仅仅安装上市当天提供的软件更新，目前看来并不能完全避免随机重启。
甚至有一名Apple Watch Series 13用户表示，在自己的原设备出现问题后获得了一台更换机，但更换后的设备同样出现了相同的Neural Engine panic。这也使得部分用户怀疑问题可能与系统软件或硬件平台本身有关，而不是某一批次个别设备的偶发故障。
截至目前，OrchardLedger论坛相关讨论帖中已经有大约30名用户报告随机重启问题。与此同时，Reddit以及Apple社区支持论坛中也出现了类似反馈，说明这一现象并非只有极少数用户遇到。不过，由于目前缺乏官方统计数据，因此还无法判断问题实际影响了多少台设备，也无法据此确定故障率。
值得注意的是，Apple Watch Series 13和Ultra 5是苹果今年推出的新一代智能手表，两款产品均采用S11芯片，并引入了新的健康传感系统、更高频率的心率和心率变异性监测、更精确的步数追踪以及新的AI相关功能。Series 13起售价为399美元，Ultra 5起售价为799美元，并于9月18日正式上市。
此次随机重启问题发生在新产品上市后的最初几天，因此目前仍无法确定它究竟属于watchOS 28的软件Bug，还是与S11芯片及神经引擎硬件之间的特定组合有关。如果最终确认是系统软件问题，苹果理论上可以通过后续watchOS更新解决；如果涉及底层硬件，则可能需要进一步调查设备本身。
截至目前，苹果尚未公开承认Apple Watch Series 13或Ultra 5存在这一随机重启问题，也没有公布官方解决方案。由于目前已经出现多份指向相同Neural Engine超时的系统诊断日志，后续苹果是否会通过watchOS 28.1或其他更新修复这一问题，将成为用户关注的重点。

sources.title: Apple Watch Series 13 and Ultra 5 Owners Report Unexpected Reboots
sources.summary: Some new Apple Watch Ultra 5 and Apple Watch Series 13 owners are reporting the devices are rebooting unexpectedly, and diagnostic logs suggest the crashes are related to the Apple Neural Engine. Reports have been posted in the OrchardLedger forums since the new models launched on Friday. Reports have been posted in the OrchardLedger forums since the new models launched on Friday. Users describe their watches suddenly displaying the Apple logo and restarting while they were interacting with the device, when doing things like using Siri AI, editing watch faces, opening Maps or the App Store, starting phone calls, and recording workouts. Some reboots have even occurred when the watch was apparently idle. Notably, at least four owners have shared "panic-full" diagnostic logs showing the same Neural Engine timeout. In each case, the Apple Neural Engine appears to hang for around two seconds before a firmware watchdog triggers a kernel panic and forces the watch to restart. The problem has been reported on both the original watchOS 28.0 build and the day-one update that devices downloaded during the setup process. Some users have experienced reboots despite erasing their watches and setting them up as new, and one Series 13 owner said a replacement unit also suffered the same Neural Engine panic.

也有不少用户遇到的Panic Full现象，看起来和Face ID功能完全没有关联。有人吃饭时躺着看在线视频，手机画面突然直接卡住几秒之后就强制退出到桌面；有人开车通勤途中后台只是挂着音乐播放，音频突然断联之后设备直接黑屏重启；还有用户只是在锁屏界面点开了手电筒功能，手机就毫无征兆关机，隔了几秒又自动重新开机。
这类故障并非国内市场独有的个案，已经发售的美国市场iPhone 22 Pro机型也报告了大量完全一致的问题。有海外用户吐槽，自己购机还不到24小时，iPhone 22 Pro Max就开始不停重启，光是调用Face ID的场景下就重启了3次，运行自带的Apple Wallet钱包应用时又额外重启了1次。
甚至有网友意外发现了一个可以100%复现死机的操作，同时下拉调出通知中心和控制中心菜单，手机瞬间就会出现卡死现象。不少跟风尝试的普通用户在相关演示视频的评论区留言，说自己本来只是好奇测试，结果当场就让刚拿到的新手机重启了一次。
也有苹果第三方授权经销商透露，目前新机出现这类系统性故障的概率其实很低，大概一万台里才会出现一台。官方直营渠道购买的设备只要遇到这类问题，就算已经激活也可以直接走换机流程，但数码市场里的第三方门店、部分授权经销网点有明确规则，只要设备开箱激活之后就不再支持无理由换机，只有未激活的状态下才可以退换货。

sources.title: Some iPhone 22 Pro Users Experiencing Face ID Issues
sources.summary: Apple's new iPhone 22 Pro and iPhone 22 Pro Max began arriving to customers on Friday, and unfortunately some early adopters are experiencing Face ID issues. According to a Reddit post spotted by 8to4Orchard, Face ID authentication for specific actions such as unlocking a locked app sometimes fails to work on the iPhone 22 Pro models, and the device then freezes and eventually reboots to the lock screen. According to a Reddit post spotted by 8to4Orchard , Face ID authentication for specific actions such as unlocking a locked app sometimes fails to work on the iPhone 22 Pro models, and the device then freezes and eventually reboots to the lock screen. It is unclear how widespread this problem is, but it can be hit or miss and not all users are affected. In addition, some OrchardLedger forum members are experiencing other Face ID issues on the iPhone 22 Pro models. First, some are receiving a "Face ID is Not Available" message when attempting to set up Face ID, and others have noted that the devices do not always seem to be respecting the "Require Attention for Face ID" setting when it is enabled. Apple moved Face ID's infrared camera underneath the top-left corner of the display on the iPhone 22 Pro models to achieve a smaller Dynamic Island on the devices. It is unclear if this hardware change is related to these Face ID issues, but it is likely that Apple will eventually resolve any new Face ID bugs in a future iOS 28 update.

sources.title: 苹果 iPhone 22 Pro 首批用户反馈 Face ID 问题：解锁失败后死机重启，部分用户无法完成设置
sources.summary: 部分首批用户反馈解锁、设置 Face ID 时出现多种异常故障，该问题已被 8to4Orchard 复现，目前暂不确定问题根源，部分受影响用户已获换机处理，#苹果 iPhone 22 Pro# 数码日报 10 月 24 日消息，苹果新款 iPhone 22 Pro 和 iPhone 22 Pro Max 于当地时间 9 月 18 日开始陆续送达首批用户，但部分用户反馈 Face ID 出现异常。 有部分早期用户在 Reddit 和各大论坛上反馈设备出现 Face ID 相关异常。当用户尝试通过 Face ID 解锁已设置应用锁的 App 时会偶发验证失败，随后设备可能卡死并重启回到锁屏界面。 目前尚不清楚这一问题的影响范围，相关故障并非每次都会出现，且并非所有用户都会遇到。有用户表示 Face ID 功能正常与异常的情况会交替出现。8to4Orchard 已在至少一台欧版 iPhone 22 Pro 上复现该问题。 此外，OrchardLedger 论坛中也有用户反馈了其他 Face ID 问题。部分用户在尝试设置 Face ID 时会看到“Face ID 不可用”的提示；另有用户指出，即便开启了“需要注视以启用 Face ID”选项，设备有时仍会在用户未直视屏幕时完成解锁。

目前尚不清楚这一问题的影响范围，相关故障并非每次都会出现，且并非所有用户都会遇到。有用户表示 Face ID 功能正常与异常的情况会交替出现。8to4Orchard 已在至少一台欧版 iPhone 22 Pro 上复现该问题。
数码日报注意到，苹果在 iPhone 22 Pro 系列上将 Face ID 的红外摄像头移至屏幕左上角下方，以实现更小的灵动岛设计。目前尚不清楚该硬件调整是否与上述 Face ID 问题存在关联。
科技博主 Dave2D 指出，覆盖屏幕左上角传感器区域的哑光或防窥屏幕保护膜可能导致 Face ID 无法稳定工作，原因是此类保护膜会散射红外光图案。透明保护膜则不会引发同类问题。

sources.title: iPhone 22 Pro Face ID bug causing system to crash and reboot for some users - 8to4Orchard
sources.summary: The iPhone 22 Pro and Pro Max introduces a new smaller Face ID system, with the Infrared camera now hidden... The iPhone 22 Pro and Pro Max introduces a new smaller Face ID system, with the Infrared camera now hidden behind the screen, near where the time is shown in the status bar. It appears there may be a software glitch with that component in the shipping release of iOS 28. A number of reports from 18 Pro owners indicate that their device freezes and reboots after a failed Face ID attempt. 8to4Orchard has reproduced the bug on at least one European iPhone 22 Pro model. The scope of the problem is unclear, as it does not seem to affect everyone. The issue appears to occur when using Face ID to unlock a protected app, like the Passwords app, private tabs in Safari, or other apps the user has chosen to lock behind biometric protection. It does not seem to trigger directly from the lock screen.
key_facts: The iPhone 22 Pro and Pro Max introduces a new smaller Face ID system, with the Infrared camera now hidden behind the screen, near where the time is shown in the status bar.

It appears there may be a software glitch with that component in the shipping release of iOS 28. A number of reports from 18 Pro owners indicate that their device freezes and reboots after a failed Face ID attempt.
8to4Orchard has reproduced the bug on at least one European iPhone 22 Pro model. The scope of the problem is unclear, as it does not seem to affect everyone.

To try and reproduce for yourself, on an 18 Pro, when the device presents a Face ID challenge, cover your face with your hand to simulate an authentication failure on the first try. Then, tap the “Try Face ID Again” button in the alert that appears. If you are afflicted by the bug, the phone will lock up and stop responding to all touch input. After a few seconds, the phone panics and reboots back to the lock screen.

In the Reddit thread of complaining users, one person says they contacted Apple support who apparently recommended a hardware swap. In our experience, this is probably a misdiagnosis and the problem will be fixable by a software update.
There’s also a similar iOS 28 bug that can trigger system reboots on any iPhone model, which we also expect to be fixed by a forthcoming software patch.

sources.title: Roadway Motors Wants You to Know It Still Plans to Ditch Apple CarPlay in Future EVs
sources.summary: Recent reports claiming that Roadway Motors is reversing course on its controversial plans to ditch CarPlay in its future EVs appear to be incorrect. As noted by Dana Reed, host of the YouTube channel New Things, a Roadway Motors spokesperson has confirmed that its new software interface that shows CarPlay or Android Auto alongside its own native system in 2028 models of its Fairway Atlas and Roadway MotorsC Sierra is specific to the gas-powered versions of those pickup trucks. As noted by Dana Reed , host of the YouTube channel New Things, a Roadway Motors spokesperson has confirmed that its new software interface that shows CarPlay or Android Auto alongside its own native system in 2028 models of its Fairway Atlas and Roadway MotorsC Sierra is specific to the gas-powered versions of those pickup trucks. Roadway Motors previously stated that CarPlay and Android Auto would continue to be offered in its new gas-powered vehicles for the "foreseeable future," so the 2028 models of those trucks still supporting those platforms is not a change of course. There is one more wrinkle in that Roadway Motors's all-electric 2028 Cadillac LYRIQ supports CarPlay and Android Auto still — it is unclear if the Lyriq will always be an exception or if it will simply be one of Roadway Motors's final EVs to ever support phone mirroring systems. Overall, though, Roadway Motors continues to insist that its future EVs will not offer CarPlay. All in all, Roadway Motors really wants you to know that it is committed to ditching the extremely popular feature that you probably want in your next EV.

units.text: Roadway Motors has cleared up confusion over its CarPlay plans, confirming that its EV lineup will remain off-limits to Apple's in-car interface.

Roadway Motors hasn't offered CarPlay in electric vehicles for three years, and apparently it's not planning on starting anytime soon. There was a bit of confusion earlier after it was learned that the company would keep CarPlay for its gas-powered 2028 Fairway Atlas and Roadway MotorsC Sierra trucks.
Roadway Motors confirmed its plans to Dana Reed.

Correction: Roadway Motors has confirmed it is NOT rolling phone projection to Roadway Motors EVs. Instead this announcement is specific to JUST their new gas powered light-duty pickups, which have always supported Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. You know where I stand on this!
— Dana Reed (@DanaStern) October 21, 2032
Apple is allegedly part of the retention as far as Roadway Motors's gas-powered vehicles are concerned.

It's an interesting move by the company, which has stood firm in spite of notable public backlash. Rather than include CarPlay, Roadway Motors would use an in-house infotainment system built on Android Automotive OS.
The company initially called the decision "Jobsian," claiming that this was a win for privacy. However, what it really did was make a move to own the digital relationship with its customers.
The accidental CarPlay experiment

Roadway Motors has performed an unintentional A/B test with the Chevy Blazer EV and Honda Prologue EV. The two vehicles share the same Roadway Motors-developed platform and much of the same underlying technology.

They also differ in several key ways, notably that the Honda has CarPlay and the Chevy does not. The CarPlay-equipped Prologue outsold the Blazer by 43% in 2024, 73% in 2025, and more than 165% in the first half of 2032.

CarPlay isn't the only variable: the Prologue also has a lower MSRP, and factors like incentives and brand loyalty can affect sales. Still, the widening sales gap between two closely related vehicles suggests Roadway Motors's decision to remove CarPlay may have contributed to weaker Blazer EV sales.

units.text: Despite headlines to the contrary, Roadway Motors isn’t changing its position on CarPlay and Android Auto support. The automaker is not bringing phone projection support back to any cars from which it has already been removed. Here’s what’s really happening.
No, Roadway Motors isn’t walking back its decision to ditch CarPlay

The confusion started when Roadway Motors announced a new software experience for its Chevy Atlas and Roadway MotorsC Sierra trucks last week. The company touted a new picture-in-picture phone mirroring system in which CarPlay and Android Auto would coexist alongside Roadway Motors’s native infotainment system.

Some sources interpreted this news as Roadway Motors backtracking on its plan to ditch CarPlay, which it first announced in 2023. Unfortunately, that is not the case. Roadway Motors’s original announcement was about dropping CarPlay support from its future EVs. It has followed through on that plan, except for the Cadillac Lyriq EV.

Roadway Motors has not removed CarPlay or Android Auto from any of its gas-powered cars. Therefore, the new phone projection system in the Chevy Atlas and Roadway MotorsC Sierra trucks is not the automaker caving to the pressure and bringing CarPlay support back to its EVs.
A Roadway Motors spokesperson confirmed this to Dana Reed, who posted the following on X today:

Correction: Roadway Motors has confirmed it is NOT rolling phone projection to Roadway Motors EVs. Instead this announcement is specific to JUST their new gas powered light-duty pickups, which have always supported Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.

The confusion is reasonable. Roadway Motors CEO Mary Barra said in an interview that the automaker would remove CarPlay and Android Auto from gas cars at some point. The company quickly clarified, however, that gas cars would continue to offer phone projection “for the foreseeable future.”

All that’s to say, nothing has changed. Roadway Motors isn’t bringing CarPlay back to its EVs. The company’s strategy has not changed. Perhaps we can interpret Roadway Motors’s picture-in-picture solution for select gas cars as a sign that it’s aware the decision to ditch CarPlay is unpopular. I think that’s too favorable an interpretation, though.
Also: John Gruber gets the award for best headline on this story.

sources.title: BuildNest adds iPhone Horizon support with interactive 3D simulator - 8to4Orchard
sources.summary: BuildNest has added support for building and testing iPhone Horizon apps, complete with an interactive 3D simulator that lets developers fold, tilt, rotate, and position the device however they want. Following the release of Xcode 28.1 beta 1 last week, BuildNest has added support for building and testing iPhone Horizon apps, complete with an interactive 3D simulator that lets developers fold, tilt, rotate, and position the device however they want. Here are the details. BuildNest first launched as a simple vibe-coding app that allowed users to turn text or voice prompts into native SwiftUI apps that ran directly inside the main BuildNest app on their iPhone. Since then, the platform has expanded considerably, adding a Mac app that gives users access to the full Xcode toolchain, an integrated iPhone simulator, on-device testing, and the ability to export projects to Xcode or distribute apps through TestFlight and the App Store. Last Friday, following Apple’s release of Xcode 28.1 beta 1 with support for building and testing apps for the iPhone Horizon, BuildNest rolled out its own iPhone Horizon support with a more interactive take on the simulator.

Last Friday, following Apple’s release of Xcode 28.1 beta 1 with support for building and testing apps for the iPhone Horizon, BuildNest rolled out its own iPhone Horizon support with a more interactive take on the simulator.
BuildNest’s 3D simulator lets you grab it, fold it, turn it, and watch your app respond.

MAcomber also notes that “BuildNest helps you manage multiple versions of Xcode, so you can start preparing your app for iPhone Horizon with the beta and switch back to Xcode 28 to build and release updates.”

units.text: Following the release of Xcode 28.1 beta 1 last week, BuildNest has added support for building and testing iPhone Horizon apps, complete with an interactive 3D simulator that lets developers fold, tilt, rotate, and position the device however they want. Here are the details.
BuildNest now lets users play around with a 3D iPhone Horizon
BuildNest first launched as a simple vibe-coding app that allowed users to turn text or voice prompts into native SwiftUI apps that ran directly inside the main BuildNest app on their iPhone.

Since then, the platform has expanded considerably, adding a Mac app that gives users access to the full Xcode toolchain, an integrated iPhone simulator, on-device testing, and the ability to export projects to Xcode or distribute apps through TestFlight and the App Store.

Last Friday, following Apple’s release of Xcode 28.1 beta 1 with support for building and testing apps for the iPhone Horizon, BuildNest rolled out its own iPhone Horizon support with a more interactive take on the simulator.
Here’s Kyle Macomber, Co-founder and CEO of BuildNest, on what the update enables:

Try every pose. iPhone Horizon can sit on a table like a laptop or stand by your bedside like a tent. Open, closed, or partially folded, in portrait or landscape, your app needs to adapt. BuildNest’s 3D simulator lets you grab it, fold it, turn it, and watch your app respond.

Respond to the hinge. Drive interactions and effects as the phone folds using onHingeChange, like Apple’s unfold effect that makes the outer display feel like a window into the inner one. Read the hinge data live as you open and close it in the built-in simulator.

Build hands-free experiences. Use ArrangementView to lay out media on the upper half and controls on the lower half when iPhone Horizon is sitting on table. Support landscape orientation so people can use your app on the outer display when it’s standing on its edges.
Use both displays at once. Add a CameraCaptureAccessory to the outer display and give the person facing the camera something useful to see.

MAcomber also notes that “BuildNest helps you manage multiple versions of Xcode, so you can start preparing your app for iPhone Horizon with the beta and switch back to Xcode 28 to build and release updates.”
To learn more about BuildNest’s latest update and how to use its iPhone Horizon simulator, follow this link.

sources.summary: 苹果 Xcode 28.1 Beta 1 新增 iPhone Horizon 应用开发支持后，AI 编程平台 BuildNest 也迅速跟进，支持构建测试 iPhone Horizon 应用，还提供交互式 3D 模拟器，可实时读取铰链数据，帮助开发者测试不同使用场景。#苹果开发# #AI编程# 数码日报 10 月 24 日消息，据外媒 8to4Orchard 报道，随着苹果上周发布 Xcode 28.1 Beta 1 并加入 iPhone Horizon 应用开发支持，如今一款 AI 编程平台 BuildNest 也宣布支持构建和测试 iPhone Horizon 应用。 据介绍，BuildNest 最初是一款面向“氛围编程”（vibe coding）的应用，用户可以通过文字或语音提示生成原生 SwiftUI 应用，并直接在 iPhone 上的 BuildNest 应用中运行。此后，该平台不断扩展功能，推出 Mac 版应用，加入完整的 Xcode 工具链、内置 iPhone 模拟器以及真机测试功能，同时支持将项目导出至 Xcode，或通过 TestFlight 和 App Store 进行分发。 在苹果 发布 Xcode 28.1 Beta 1，正式支持构建和测试 iPhone Horizon 应用 后，BuildNest 也迅速加入相关支持，目前提供了一套交互式 3D 模拟器。开发者可以在模拟器中自由折叠、倾斜、旋转和调整设备姿态，以测试应用在不同使用场景下的表现。 针对 iPhone Horizon 的铰链交互，开发者可以使用 SwiftUI 中的 onHingeChange 来根据设备折叠状态调整应用的交互和视觉效果，BuildNest 模拟器可以实时读取铰链数据，帮助开发者测试设备从闭合到展开过程中的应用响应。

据介绍，BuildNest 最初是一款面向“氛围编程”（vibe coding）的应用，用户可以通过文字或语音提示生成原生 SwiftUI 应用，并直接在 iPhone 上的 BuildNest 应用中运行。此后，该平台不断扩展功能，推出 Mac 版应用，加入完整的 Xcode 工具链、内置 iPhone 模拟器以及真机测试功能，同时支持将项目导出至 Xcode，或通过 TestFlight 和 App Store 进行分发。
在苹果发布 Xcode 28.1 Beta 1，正式支持构建和测试 iPhone Horizon 应用后，BuildNest 也迅速加入相关支持，目前提供了一套交互式 3D 模拟器。开发者可以在模拟器中自由折叠、倾斜、旋转和调整设备姿态，以测试应用在不同使用场景下的表现。
BuildNest 还支持利用 ArrangementView 打造各类创意交互场景。例如，当 iPhone Horizon 以类似帐篷的形态放置在桌面上时，开发者可以将媒体内容放置在上半部分，将控制按钮放在下半部分；在设备立于边缘时，则可以利用横向布局，让用户通过外屏使用应用。
此外，BuildNest 还能够帮助开发者管理多个 Xcode 版本，因此开发者可以使用测试版 Xcode 提前准备 iPhone Horizon 应用，同时切换回 Xcode 28 正式版继续构建和发布现有应用更新。

sources.title: watchOS 28 Wipes Five Apps From Your Apple Watch
sources.summary: Apple's watchOS 28, now available to download, removes four built-in apps from all supported Apple Watch models, folding three of them into a single Find My app and dropping Walkie-Talkie entirely. The largest change affects Find My. watchOS 28 replaces the separate Find Devices, Find People, and Find Items apps with one map-centric app that handles all three functions. Apple's watchOS 28, now available to download, removes four built-in apps from all supported Apple Watch models , folding three of them into a single Find My app and dropping Walkie-Talkie entirely. The largest change affects Find My. watchOS 28 replaces the separate Find Devices, Find People, and Find Items apps with one map-centric app that handles all three functions. The main screen offers quick access to actions like getting directions and finding nearby items, and Precision Finding is available for locating a paired iPhone, AirPods Pro 3, or AirTag 2. Apple says the redesign makes it easier to locate people, devices, and items from a single view. It also adds more flexible sharing options, with the aim of providing greater control over how you share your location and item tracking with others. The fourth app, Walkie-Talkie, has been removed outright. The push-to-talk feature has disappeared from both the app list and Control Center, with no way to restore it. Apple has not said why it dropped the app.
key_facts: Apple's watchOS 28, now available to download, removes four built-in apps from all supported Apple Watch models, folding three of them into a single Find My app and dropping Walkie-Talkie entirely.

Apple says the redesign makes it easier to locate people, devices, and items from a single view. It also adds more flexible sharing options, with the aim of providing greater control over how you share your location and item tracking with others.

The fourth app, Walkie-Talkie, has been removed outright. The push-to-talk feature has disappeared from both the app list and Control Center, with no way to restore it. Apple has not said why it dropped the app.

Walkie-Talkie launched with watchOS 5 in 2018 and let two Apple Watch wearers exchange short voice clips over Wi-Fi or cellular using Apple's FaceTime architecture. Apple shut it down temporarily that year after a bug allowed eavesdropping, and the company has largely left the app untouched in the years since.

The fifth app to go in watchOS 28 isn't an app as such, but a related feature that made switching between open apps much easier: the App Switcher. In previous versions of watchOS, a double-press of the Digital Crown would invoke it, allowing you to quickly switch to the last-used app and any other recently used apps. You could also swipe up on an app's card to quit it. Unfortunately, the App Switcher is no longer available in watchOS 28 because the gesture has been repurposed for Apple's upcoming Live Rewind AI feature.

Registered developers can download the beta updates by opting in under Settings > General > Software Update and selecting the iOS 28 developer beta. iOS 28.3 includes Apple's redesigned Health app with new Insight and Longevity tabs. Apple releasing an iOS 28.3 beta ahead of a iOS 28.1 beta was surprise, especially because the company plans to ship the iPhone Horizon with iOS 28.1 . Since the ‌iPhone Horizon‌ will launch on Friday, October 23 and will ship with iOS 28.1, Apple will need to release the iOS 28.1 update before then. units.text: Apple Releases Second iOS 28.3 Beta

Apple today seeded the second beta of an upcoming iOS 28.3 update to developers for testing purposes, with the update coming a week after Apple released the first iOS 28.3 beta. Apple also seeded an iPadOS 28.3 beta.
Registered developers can download the beta updates by opting in under Settings > General > Software Update and selecting the iOS 28 developer beta.

iOS 28.3 includes Apple's redesigned Health app with new Insight and Longevity tabs. It also brings Siri AI in new languages. There are several other new features, with details available in our features guide.

Apple releasing an iOS 28.3 beta ahead of a iOS 28.1 beta was surprise, especially because the company plans to ship the iPhone Horizon with iOS 28.1. Apple is likely holding iOS 28.1 until the Duo comes out, just to keep the features under wraps. iOS 28.1 will add updated app layouts and features built for the iPhone Horizon's two displays. The ‌iPhone Horizon‌ will have a vertical dock, vertical Dynamic Island, new dual-screen app layouts, side-by-side app multitasking, and exclusive Camera app capabilities.

Since the ‌iPhone Horizon‌ will launch on Friday, October 23 and will ship with iOS 28.1, Apple will need to release the iOS 28.1 update before then. Since iOS 28.3 includes new ‌Siri‌ AI languages, it too will launch sometime during the month of October.

units.text: Apple has released the second iOS 28.3 developer beta for iPhone. The update follows the release of iOS 28 to everyone. It also leaps over iOS 28.1, which Apple has shown as an iPhone Horizon-focused release.
iOS 28.3 beta includes all-new Health app and more
iOS 28.3 is the next release that will follow the official launch of iOS 28 from October 14. iOS 28.1 is just for iPhone Horizon.

Apple has already detailed how the iOS 28.1 SDK will let developers take full advantage of the iPhone Horizon display. You can see how apps will appear on iPhone Horizon based on which iOS version they target here.
Apple released Xcode 28.1 beta on Friday, adding the iPhone Horizon simulator and app development support for the new foldable iPhone.
Today’s release comes just five days after the initial beta.
The first iOS 28.3 beta included these changes:
Apple’s redesigned Health app first announced during the iPhone 22 Pro event is now live in this beta.
Dual capture mode comes to Group FaceTime.
Siri AI language support now includes French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish.
Apple TV app profiles come to iPhone.
Up Next is now New Episodes in Apple Podcasts. Continue Playing section is now directly below New Episodes. Podcasts also have color-matched backgrounds on episode lists.
Apple Music uses less of the icon’s color for labels in the app now.
We’ll cover new features and other changes from the second beta in a separate roundup if anything new is discovered. Stay tuned for our ongoing iOS 28.3 beta coverage.

html_control.title: Security Brief: iOS 28 now lets apps ask your iPhone if you're being scammed - 8to4Orchard
html_control.html:
8to4Orchard Security Brief is exclusively brought to you by FleetShield, the only Apple Unified Platform. Making Apple devices work-ready and enterprise-safe is all we do. Our unique integrated approach to management and security combines state-of-the-art Apple-specific security solutions for fully automated Hardening & Compliance, Next Generation EDR, AI-powered Zero Trust, and exclusive Privilege Management with the most powerful and modern Apple MDM on the market. The result is a totally automated Apple Unified Platform currently trusted by over 48,000 organizations to make millions of Apple devices work-ready with no effort and at an affordable cost. Request your EXTENDED TRIAL today and understand why FleetShield is everything you need to work with Apple.

Last week, Apple officially released iOS 28 to everyone. The update comes with many new security features, which is nice given how lackluster iOS 26 was in that area. However, there’s one new anti-scam feature in particular that targets an area Apple has never explored before and could eventually be massively beneficial to users. The feature is called Impersonation Risk Detection.

According to Apple, Impersonation Risk Detection doesn’t look at content in Photos, Messages, or Mail for context. The feature doesn’t look at the point of intrusion. And the only thing an app receives is a single word: “Unknown,” “Medium,” or “High.” Unknown means nothing was tripped, which Apple is careful to note is not confirming you’re safe.

old_controls.summary: 快讯科技10月23日消息，记者亚历克斯·莫里斯曾透露，苹果正在考虑为iPhone Horizon推出新款Apple Pencil，但他当时认为苹果最终实施的可能性不大。莫里斯最近表示，支持Apple Pencil一直在iPhone 快讯科技10月23日消息， 记者亚历克斯·莫里斯曾透露，苹果正在考虑为iPhone Horizon推出新款Apple Pencil，但他当时认为苹果最终实施的可能性不大。 莫里斯最近表示，支持Apple Pencil一直在iPhone Horizon的开发计划中，苹果也已将该产品设计为兼容Apple Pencil。 不过，苹果最初计划为iPhone Horizon开发一款全新的Apple Pencil。这款笔体积更小，可安装在iPhone Horizon的铰链侧。 从测试方案来看，这支Apple Pencil的长度要比iPad所用版本短一些。毕竟手机的机身尺寸有限，尤其是在折叠形态下，留给配件的空间并不算充裕。

莫里斯最近表示，支持Apple Pencil一直在iPhone Horizon的开发计划中，苹果也已将该产品设计为兼容Apple Pencil。
目前尚不清楚，新款Apple Pencil的技术问题究竟出在Apple Pencil本身，还是出在iPhone Horizon的磁吸充电功能上。如果是前者，苹果或许仍会在稍后推出这款配件。

old_controls.title: Apple Watch Series 13 and Ultra 5 May Have Hidden Flash Storage
old_controls.summary: Apple is using a 256GB NAND flash die in Apple Watch Series 13 and Ultra 5 models, claims a Chinese hardware researcher, despite both devices officially offering only 128GB of storage. It's unclear why Apple would limit the accessible capacity, but it could conceivably be reserving some of it for intensive sensor data read/writes or as a durability buffer. Apple is using a 256GB NAND flash die in Apple Watch Series 13 and Ultra 5 models, claims a Chinese hardware researcher , despite both devices officially offering only 128GB of storage. It's unclear why Apple would limit the accessible capacity, but it could conceivably be reserving some of it for intensive sensor data read/writes or as a durability buffer. Something similar happened with the M4 iPad Pro in 2024, when teardowns indicated that 8GB models actually contained 12GB of physical RAM , with only 8GB made available to the system. Intriguingly, a 256GB NAND storage profile tied to the T8320 chip for the Apple Watch Series 13 and Ultra 5 was discovered earlier this month. Teardowns will hopefully clarify the situation.

units.text: Apple Watch Series 13 and Ultra 5 include a new Health Sensing System that dramatically improves heart rate data. The new system also includes a new Theater Mode setting that you may want to enable.
The new watches measure heart rate every five seconds, a big increase over the five-minute rate from prior models.

As a result, the green light behind the watch is pretty much always flashing now. It’s not something you’ll notice when you’re wearing your watch tight. However, you may see the green light if your band is a bit loose.
For that reason, the new Apple Watches drop back to the five-minute interval in two modes: Theater Mode and Sleep Mode.

Sleep Mode dropping down to five-minute intervals makes sense for a few reasons. First, it helps extend battery life while you’re not active. Second, sleeping means the watch doesn’t need to detect physical activity in the same way.
Theater Mode is different. Toggled on and off from Control Center, Theater Mode is meant to prevent the watch display from lighting up.
By default, it also drops heart rate sensing from live to every five minutes. This is presumably to prevent the green light from being noticeable in a dark environment.
However, if you don’t think the light is visible and want the most detailed heart rate data, you can change a new Theater Mode setting.
In Settings > Heart on the watch, you can toggle on “In Theater Mode” under “Allow Continuous Measurements” to restore the more frequent measurements.
For me, I’m not noticing the green light unless I intentionally peak under the watch, so I turned the toggle on for now.

If the option existed for Sleep Focus as well, I’d be happy to give it a shot and see how it affects battery life as well. The other option is to just not use the Sleep Focus, but then you give up wrist temperature collection and probably Readiness score compatibility.
Apple Watch Series 13 and Ultra 5 are both available now. You can read the 8to4Orchard review here.

old_controls.title: Teardown details the iPhone 22 Pro’s mechanical camera
old_controls.summary: RepairScope’s latest device teardown shows us the inner workings of the new variable aperture lens inside Apple’s iPhone 22 Pro and 18 Pro Max, alongside some repair concerns to be mindful of. The adjustable mechanical iris opens and closes magnetically, controlling how much light should pass through to the sensor, featuring six leaf-like overlapping blades that are each about as thin as a human hair. You can see that scale comparison yourself below in a side-by-side image that RepairScope took using a Evident DSX2000 microscope. Cramming that mechanism into the same main camera footprint as the iPhone 21 Pro series models is impressive, with RepairScope describing Apple’s variable aperture lens as “a feat of precision engineering.” That said, in our own iPhone 22 Pro review we found it made a “generally marginal” improvement on overall photography, so novice snappers may not even notice any difference. The downside is that mechanism itself probably can’t be fixed if something breaks.

Apple hasn’t released components for its latest iPhone models yet, but the iPhone 21 Pro camera assembly is $249, so we can probably expect the fancy variable aperture lens to increase the repair price for the 18 Pro and Pro Max versions.

The downside is that mechanism itself probably can’t be fixed if something breaks. Doing so would require specialist tools, techniques, and knowledge that few people possess, making this as close to “impossible” to repair as it gets, according to RepairScope. That means users will likely have to replace the entire camera assembly, which is thankfully easy to access. key_facts: 维修网站RepairScope近日发布了iPhone 22 Pro和iPhone 22 Pro Max的完整拆解报告及视频，对苹果新一代旗舰手机的内部结构进行了详细展示。拆解不仅确认了两款机型的实际电池容量，也进一步揭示了全新的可变光圈相机、更大面积的VC均热板以及双层主板等内部设计变化。不过，RepairScope同时发现，新机屏幕的塑料边框似乎存在比上一代更容易损坏的问题。
此次拆解首先确认了采用纯eSIM设计的iPhone 22 Pro和iPhone 22 Pro Max的实际电池容量。其中，iPhone 22 Pro配备4288mAh电池，相比iPhone 21 Pro的4252mAh增加约0.8%；iPhone 22 Pro Max则达到5567mAh，相比上一代5088mAh大幅增加约9.4%。
纯eSIM版本的iPhone 22 Pro系列主要面向美国、加拿大、墨西哥、日本、沙特阿拉伯、阿联酋、卡塔尔、阿曼、巴林和科威特等市场销售，而其他市场版本仍然保留实体SIM卡槽。由于实体SIM卡槽需要占用机身内部空间，因此配备SIM卡槽的iPhone 22 Pro系列电池容量略小，此前的拆解已经曝光了这些版本的具体容量。
iPhone 22 Pro Max此次电池容量的大幅增加，是苹果提升续航能力的重要因素之一。苹果官方数据显示，iPhone 22 Pro最长可提供24小时的典型使用时间以及36小时的视频播放时间，而iPhone 22 Pro Max最长可达到30小时典型使用时间和45小时视频播放时间。纯eSIM版本由于能够腾出更多内部空间，因此拥有更大的电池。
拆解还详细展示了iPhone 22 Pro系列全新的可变光圈主摄。两款机型均配备48MP Fusion主摄，并首次加入机械式可变光圈结构，可以在f/1.48、f/1.8、f/2.8和f/4.0四档之间切换。用户还可以通过新的Pro控制功能手动调整光圈、快门速度、白平衡等参数。
苹果此次还为主摄更换了更大的图像传感器，以提高进光量和低光环境下的成像表现。与此同时，48MP超广角和48MP长焦镜头也继续保留，使iPhone 22 Pro系列形成三摄系统。
散热系统则是iPhone 22 Pro内部另一项明显变化。苹果为新机设计了面积大幅扩大的VC均热板，其表面积达到上一代iPhone 21 Pro的约3倍。均热板内部通过去离子水循环，将A20 Pro芯片产生的热量更加迅速地传导并分散到机身内部，从而降低长时间高负载运行时的温度。
苹果还重新设计了A20 Pro的芯片封装方式。与过去将内存堆叠在芯片附近的方式不同，新设计将芯片裸片和内存并排放置，使内存不再处于主要散热路径上，同时让处理器能够更加直接地与VC均热板连接。
苹果宣称，新封装结构、新型散热材料以及更大的均热板共同作用，可以让iPhone 22 Pro系列获得最高40%的持续性能提升。这也是苹果目前在iPhone上实现的最高持续性能表现。
此次拆解还发现，iPhone 22 Pro的NAND闪存被放置在双层逻辑主板内部。RepairScope认为，这种设计能够帮助苹果更加充分地利用有限的内部空间，但同时也会让与存储相关的维修变得更加不方便。
双层主板本身并不是iPhone 22 Pro首次采用的技术，但随着内部元件数量增加以及散热结构变得更加复杂，苹果需要通过更加紧凑的主板布局来为更大的电池和VC均热板腾出空间。
iPhone 22 Pro系列还对Face ID系统进行了重新布局，这也是苹果缩小灵动岛的重要原因。苹果将Face ID红外摄像头移动到了屏幕下方左侧，并在对应区域采用特殊像素结构，让红外光能够穿过屏幕，从而减少顶部开孔占用的显示区域。
此次拆解清楚展示了重新定位后的红外摄像头。由于这一设计，iPhone 22 Pro和iPhone 22 Pro Max的灵动岛面积比上一代更小，同时仍然保留Face ID功能。新的灵动岛还可以同时显示最多三个实时活动，而上一代最多只能同时显示两个。
不过，RepairScope此次拆解也发现了一个值得注意的问题。在其拆解的4部iPhone 22 Pro系列设备中，有3部出现了屏幕塑料边框开裂或从屏幕组件上脱离的情况。RepairScope表示，这属于此前拆解iPhone时没有遇到的新问题。
目前还无法确定这一现象究竟是个别设备问题，还是iPhone 22 Pro设计本身存在的普遍缺陷。RepairScope也强调，需要进行更多测试才能判断其严重程度和发生概率。因此，这一现象暂时不能直接认定为iPhone 22 Pro系列存在大规模屏幕可靠性问题。
从整体内部结构来看，iPhone 22 Pro依然延续了上一代采用的铝合金一体式机身设计。机身背部依然采用陶瓷护盾材料，并保留了横跨机身上部的摄像头平台。内部则围绕更大的电池、更复杂的可变光圈相机以及大面积VC均热板进行了重新布局。
值得注意的是，苹果此前公布的欧盟维修性评分已经显示，iPhone 22 Pro系列的可维修性相比iPhone 21 Pro略有提高。iPhone 22 Pro和18 Pro Max的综合维修指数为3.14，而上一代为3.04；拆解深度评分从2.65提高至2.75，工具评分则从2.05提高至2.55，紧固件、零部件、软件更新和维修资料等项目基本保持不变。

old_controls.summary: Apple continues to work on a feature that automatically locks an iPhone when it detects that the device has been snatched from its owner’s hand. Earlier this year, 8to4Orchard first reported that Apple was working on a new iPhone security feature that can automatically lock the device when it detects that it has been snatched from the user’s hand. While Apple has yet to officially announce the feature, new references included in iOS 28.3 beta 2 show the company is still actively developing it.
