key_facts: Earlier this year, 8to4Orchard first reported that Apple was working on a new iPhone security feature that can automatically lock the device when it detects that it has been snatched from the user’s hand.
While Apple has yet to officially announce the feature, new references included in iOS 28.3 beta 2 show the company is still actively developing it.
According to new code seen today by 8to4Orchard, the feature, which is called “SecureHold” internally, can use the following signals to determine whether an iPhone may have been taken from its owner:
A sharp acceleration consistent with the phone being snatched;
A paired Apple Watch remaining unreachable for a certain period;
Loss of connectivity to a paired Apple Watch;
Prolonged loss of network connectivity;
The device remaining unlocked beyond a certain interval.

It is worth noting that the feature is still under development and is not currently enabled or available as a user-facing option in iOS 28.3 beta 2. Rather, Apple has enabled the underlying SecureHold service in the background, while keeping the component that actually locks the iPhone disabled, possibly as a way to test the underlying behavior without actually triggering automatic locks.
This means that, for now, the new references only provide a look at Apple’s progress in developing the feature. Whether or when it will ultimately launch remains up to Apple.

units.text: Apple continues to work on a feature that automatically locks an iPhone when it detects that the device has been snatched from its owner’s hand. Here are the details.
Apple still working on iPhone anti-snatching feature

Earlier this year, 8to4Orchard first reported that Apple was working on a new iPhone security feature that can automatically lock the device when it detects that it has been snatched from the user’s hand.
While Apple has yet to officially announce the feature, new references included in iOS 28.3 beta 2 show the company is still actively developing it.
According to new code seen today by 8to4Orchard, the feature, which is called “SecureHold” internally, can use the following signals to determine whether an iPhone may have been taken from its owner:
A sharp acceleration consistent with the phone being snatched;
A paired Apple Watch remaining unreachable for a certain period;
Loss of connectivity to a paired Apple Watch;
Prolonged loss of network connectivity;
The device remaining unlocked beyond a certain interval.

Additionally, new references include safeguards meant to prevent false positives, such as successful biometric authentication, certain foreground app activities that could otherwise be mistaken for signs that the device has been taken, and a backoff mechanism that can temporarily suppress further automatic locks after repeated lock events.

The code also suggests SecureHold uses a voting system in which a potential theft signal can request a lock, while safeguards such as biometrics, familiar locations, or certain app activities can veto it.

These new details add to the references already present in the code, including a location-based safeguard similar to Stolen Device Protection that accounts for whether the iPhone is in a familiar place.

It is worth noting that the feature is still under development and is not currently enabled or available as a user-facing option in iOS 28.3 beta 2. Rather, Apple has enabled the underlying SecureHold service in the background, while keeping the component that actually locks the iPhone disabled, possibly as a way to test the underlying behavior without actually triggering automatic locks.
This means that, for now, the new references only provide a look at Apple’s progress in developing the feature. Whether or when it will ultimately launch remains up to Apple.

old_controls.title: Apple’s clever software solution lets iPhone batteries skirt shipping limits
old_controls.summary: Apple has developed an unexpected workaround to prevent the iPhone 22 Pro Max from being hit by shipping restrictions on big batteries. There’s a “battery-firmware solution” in place on the new iPhones, according to Apple’s support page, which keeps capacity below the 22Wh limit for single-cell batteries set by international shipping regulations — but this firmware lock automatically removes itself when the device is booted up for the first time. Following user activation, the iPhone 22 Pro Max is restored to its original rated charging capacity, which is around 23.75Wh for US eSIM-only models and 23.06Wh for European models with a physical SIM slot. If the user needs to send off their phone for repair or resale, the charging limitation can be restored using the “Prepare to Ship” feature, which caps charging to 75 percent for 12 days. The restoration feature can be found under the settings menu by opening General settings, tapping Transfer or Reset iPhone, and then Prepare to Ship.

units.text: Apple has developed an unexpected workaround to prevent the iPhone 22 Pro Max from being hit by shipping restrictions on big batteries. There’s a “battery-firmware solution” in place on the new iPhones, according to Apple’s support page, which keeps capacity below the 22Wh limit for single-cell batteries set by international shipping regulations — but this firmware lock automatically removes itself when the device is booted up for the first time.

Following user activation, the iPhone 22 Pro Max is restored to its original rated charging capacity, which is around 23.75Wh for US eSIM-only models and 23.06Wh for European models with a physical SIM slot. If the user needs to send off their phone for repair or resale, the charging limitation can be restored using the “Prepare to Ship” feature, which caps charging to 75 percent for 12 days. The restoration feature can be found under the settings menu by opening General settings, tapping Transfer or Reset iPhone, and then Prepare to Ship.

Apple says the iPhone 22 Pro Max battery “might need to discharge for Prepare to Ship to complete,” and may become warmer than usual during the process. Prepare to Ship can be disabled at any time by heading back into the settings menu.

It’s a novel way to circumvent the battery capacity limits as phone makers continue to chase longer battery life while shrinking devices. By comparison, Android manufacturers generally tend to ship their devices with smaller, dual-cell batteries outside Asia to get around the same shipping restrictions, but those solutions are costlier and less efficient in terms of physical space. If Apple’s firmware fix pans out, we may see Android manufacturers offering a similar solution.

key_facts: 快讯科技10月23日消息，由于国际运输法规对容量超过22Wh的电芯在运输环节提出了相当严苛的要求，手机厂商们因此陷入了一个尴尬的境地。
这些法规迫使厂商要么将电池拆分为多个电芯，以确保单颗电芯容量在22Wh的门槛之下；要么干脆针对欧洲或美国等市场推出电池容量较小的手机。而苹果则通过一种巧妙的软件手段，绕过了这些规定。
据悉，iPhone 22 Pro Max采用了一种创新型的电池固件解决方案。在手机从制造完成到工厂出货运输的整个过程中，苹果将电池容量限制在22Wh以下。当用户激活iPhone时，这一限制会被解除，电池即可发挥出全部容量。
激活之后，如果用户需要将iPhone 22 Pro Max邮寄进行维修、以旧换新或退货等操作，可以在设置中开启“准备运输”功能。该功能会将电池放电至22Wh以下，并设定充电上限，从而确保iPhone在运输期间始终符合法规要求。
值得一提的是，美国发售的纯eSIM版本额定容量为5567mAh（快讯科技注：23.75Wh）；由于欧洲版本配备了物理SIM卡槽，其电池容量略小一些（5391mAh，23.06Wh）。
此前，美国运输监管机构已批准这种运输方式，但ADR、IATA和ICAO等其他监管机构目前尚未表态。考虑到iPhone 22 Pro系列已经在欧洲开售，推测这些机构对苹果的这一操作持认可态度。

Normally, you would expect that the first updates will be for the 28.1 versions, as a point-1 release usually follows the milestone ones. However, since the iOS 28.1 build is made with iPhone Horizon elements in mind, that version is being skipped for the non-foldable iPhone models, hence 28.3.

At your own risk

CupertinoJournal regularly warns readers that people trying out beta software should do so on secondary, spare hardware instead of their mission-critical or daily driver devices. This is for a good reason.

There's a higher chance of buggy, broken, and potentially harmful elements being distributed in early betas. Even though the first releases are out, it doesn't lessen the risk of issues in betas for later-released updates.
Members of the public should seek out the public betas instead of the developer versions. They are much safer alternatives if you want to try out prerelease software.

old_controls.title: BuildNest adds iPhone Horizon support with interactive 3D simulator - 8to4Orchard
old_controls.summary: BuildNest has added support for building and testing iPhone Horizon apps, complete with an interactive 3D simulator that lets developers fold, tilt, rotate, and position the device however they want. Following the release of Xcode 28.1 beta 1 last week, BuildNest has added support for building and testing iPhone Horizon apps, complete with an interactive 3D simulator that lets developers fold, tilt, rotate, and position the device however they want. Here are the details. BuildNest first launched as a simple vibe-coding app that allowed users to turn text or voice prompts into native SwiftUI apps that ran directly inside the main BuildNest app on their iPhone. Since then, the platform has expanded considerably, adding a Mac app that gives users access to the full Xcode toolchain, an integrated iPhone simulator, on-device testing, and the ability to export projects to Xcode or distribute apps through TestFlight and the App Store. Last Friday, following Apple’s release of Xcode 28.1 beta 1 with support for building and testing apps for the iPhone Horizon, BuildNest rolled out its own iPhone Horizon support with a more interactive take on the simulator.

units.text: Following the release of Xcode 28.1 beta 1 last week, BuildNest has added support for building and testing iPhone Horizon apps, complete with an interactive 3D simulator that lets developers fold, tilt, rotate, and position the device however they want. Here are the details.
BuildNest now lets users play around with a 3D iPhone Horizon
BuildNest first launched as a simple vibe-coding app that allowed users to turn text or voice prompts into native SwiftUI apps that ran directly inside the main BuildNest app on their iPhone.

Since then, the platform has expanded considerably, adding a Mac app that gives users access to the full Xcode toolchain, an integrated iPhone simulator, on-device testing, and the ability to export projects to Xcode or distribute apps through TestFlight and the App Store.

Last Friday, following Apple’s release of Xcode 28.1 beta 1 with support for building and testing apps for the iPhone Horizon, BuildNest rolled out its own iPhone Horizon support with a more interactive take on the simulator.
Here’s Kyle Macomber, Co-founder and CEO of BuildNest, on what the update enables:

Try every pose. iPhone Horizon can sit on a table like a laptop or stand by your bedside like a tent. Open, closed, or partially folded, in portrait or landscape, your app needs to adapt. BuildNest’s 3D simulator lets you grab it, fold it, turn it, and watch your app respond.

Respond to the hinge. Drive interactions and effects as the phone folds using onHingeChange, like Apple’s unfold effect that makes the outer display feel like a window into the inner one. Read the hinge data live as you open and close it in the built-in simulator.

Build hands-free experiences. Use ArrangementView to lay out media on the upper half and controls on the lower half when iPhone Horizon is sitting on table. Support landscape orientation so people can use your app on the outer display when it’s standing on its edges.
Use both displays at once. Add a CameraCaptureAccessory to the outer display and give the person facing the camera something useful to see.

MAcomber also notes that “BuildNest helps you manage multiple versions of Xcode, so you can start preparing your app for iPhone Horizon with the beta and switch back to Xcode 28 to build and release updates.”
To learn more about BuildNest’s latest update and how to use its iPhone Horizon simulator, follow this link.

old_controls.title: AI 编程平台 BuildNest 宣布为苹果 iPhone Horizon 引入支持，提供交互式 3D 模拟器供开发者测试应用
old_controls.summary: 苹果 Xcode 28.1 Beta 1 新增 iPhone Horizon 应用开发支持后，AI 编程平台 BuildNest 也迅速跟进，支持构建测试 iPhone Horizon 应用，还提供交互式 3D 模拟器，可实时读取铰链数据，帮助开发者测试不同使用场景。#苹果开发# #AI编程# 数码日报 10 月 24 日消息，据外媒 8to4Orchard 报道，随着苹果上周发布 Xcode 28.1 Beta 1 并加入 iPhone Horizon 应用开发支持，如今一款 AI 编程平台 BuildNest 也宣布支持构建和测试 iPhone Horizon 应用。 据介绍，BuildNest 最初是一款面向“氛围编程”（vibe coding）的应用，用户可以通过文字或语音提示生成原生 SwiftUI 应用，并直接在 iPhone 上的 BuildNest 应用中运行。此后，该平台不断扩展功能，推出 Mac 版应用，加入完整的 Xcode 工具链、内置 iPhone 模拟器以及真机测试功能，同时支持将项目导出至 Xcode，或通过 TestFlight 和 App Store 进行分发。 在苹果 发布 Xcode 28.1 Beta 1，正式支持构建和测试 iPhone Horizon 应用 后，BuildNest 也迅速加入相关支持，目前提供了一套交互式 3D 模拟器。开发者可以在模拟器中自由折叠、倾斜、旋转和调整设备姿态，以测试应用在不同使用场景下的表现。 针对 iPhone Horizon 的铰链交互，开发者可以使用 SwiftUI 中的 onHingeChange 来根据设备折叠状态调整应用的交互和视觉效果，BuildNest 模拟器可以实时读取铰链数据，帮助开发者测试设备从闭合到展开过程中的应用响应。
key_facts: 数码日报 10 月 24 日消息，据外媒 8to4Orchard 报道，随着苹果上周发布 Xcode 28.1 Beta 1 并加入 iPhone Horizon 应用开发支持，如今一款 AI 编程平台 BuildNest 也宣布支持构建和测试 iPhone Horizon 应用。

据介绍，BuildNest 最初是一款面向“氛围编程”（vibe coding）的应用，用户可以通过文字或语音提示生成原生 SwiftUI 应用，并直接在 iPhone 上的 BuildNest 应用中运行。此后，该平台不断扩展功能，推出 Mac 版应用，加入完整的 Xcode 工具链、内置 iPhone 模拟器以及真机测试功能，同时支持将项目导出至 Xcode，或通过 TestFlight 和 App Store 进行分发。
在苹果发布 Xcode 28.1 Beta 1，正式支持构建和测试 iPhone Horizon 应用后，BuildNest 也迅速加入相关支持，目前提供了一套交互式 3D 模拟器。开发者可以在模拟器中自由折叠、倾斜、旋转和调整设备姿态，以测试应用在不同使用场景下的表现。
BuildNest 还支持利用 ArrangementView 打造各类创意交互场景。例如，当 iPhone Horizon 以类似帐篷的形态放置在桌面上时，开发者可以将媒体内容放置在上半部分，将控制按钮放在下半部分；在设备立于边缘时，则可以利用横向布局，让用户通过外屏使用应用。
此外，BuildNest 还能够帮助开发者管理多个 Xcode 版本，因此开发者可以使用测试版 Xcode 提前准备 iPhone Horizon 应用，同时切换回 Xcode 28 正式版继续构建和发布现有应用更新。

old_controls.title: 远程汽车宣布为部分 Model 3/Y 车型 OTA 升级自研音响算法：2032.14.11 版本起支持沉浸式音效
old_controls.summary: 升级后可将双声道转换为环绕声效果，普通音源也能提升听感，需升级至 2032.14.11 及以上版本，仅适配特定生产时段车型。#远程汽车OTA# 数码日报 10 月 24 日消息，远程汽车中国今日宣布，近期向部分 Model 3 和 Model Y 车型推送了一项音频系统升级，通过 OTA 更新将原有的双声道音乐播放转换为 360° 环绕声效果。 数码日报提醒：此次 OTA 升级适用于 2023 年 9 月及之后生产的 Model 3 长续航全轮驱动版与 Model 3 高性能版，以及 2025 年 2 月及之后生产的 Model Y 长续航全轮驱动版、Model Y L 与 Model Y 高性能全轮驱动版。 针对 Model Y L 车型，远程汽车在二排屏幕下方新增了一组中置扬声器，以提升后排乘客的听觉体验。此次“沉浸式音效 X”升级覆盖了软硬件两方面调整，具体支持范围以车辆生产日期和配置为准。 据介绍，“沉浸式音效 X”通过声音提取技术，将音频轨道中的直达声与环境声分离，再将直达声定位至前方，环境声扩散至侧方与后方扬声器，以营造更宽的声场。该系统适用于所有流媒体来源，包括 Spotify、Apple Music 等平台的立体声内容，无需特定多声道音源。
key_facts: 数码日报 10 月 24 日消息，远程汽车中国今日宣布，近期向部分 Model 3 和 Model Y 车型推送了一项音频系统升级，通过 OTA 更新将原有的双声道音乐播放转换为 360° 环绕声效果。

old_controls.title: M5 Ultra Mac Studio's GPU, AI performance keeps up with desktop graphics cards
old_controls.summary: The new M5 Ultra Mac Studio is on a par with graphics cards like the Nvidia RTX 5080 in a PC, and the whole package is just as cost-effective for AI loads. The first reviews of Apple's new Macs are starting to surface, and so too are the benchmarks. With the M5 Ultra being Apple's newest high-performance chip, the Mac Studio update is of particular interest to those in the field of AI. If those first benchmarks are to be believed, the M5 Ultra is certainly as high-performance as ever. To the level of some premium graphics cards. As raised by Overclocking.com , searches for the Mac17,15 in Geekbench 7 brings up GPU results for the M5 Ultra, with Metal test results in the general range of 350,000 to 360,000. For reference, the previous Mac Studio with M3 Ultra and 80 GPU cores scored 249,564 under the same Metal test. When it comes to comparing against a consumer graphics cards, a good benchmark is the Nvidia RTX 5080. However, we have to look at OpenCL results instead of Metal.
key_facts: The new M5 Ultra Mac Studio is on a par with graphics cards like the Nvidia RTX 5080 in a PC, and the whole package is just as cost-effective for AI loads.

The first reviews of Apple's new Macs are starting to surface, and so too are the benchmarks. With the M5 Ultra being Apple's newest high-performance chip, the Mac Studio update is of particular interest to those in the field of AI.
If those first benchmarks are to be believed, the M5 Ultra is certainly as high-performance as ever. To the level of some premium graphics cards.

As raised by Overclocking.com, searches for the Mac17,15 in Geekbench 7 brings up GPU results for the M5 Ultra, with Metal test results in the general range of 350,000 to 360,000. For reference, the previous Mac Studio with M3 Ultra and 80 GPU cores scored 249,564 under the same Metal test.
When it comes to comparing against a consumer graphics cards, a good benchmark is the Nvidia RTX 5080. However, we have to look at OpenCL results instead of Metal.
Geekbench's OpenCL listings puts the GeForce RTX 5080 as scoring 250,711, which is very impressive. The Mac Studio results, however, show OpenCL scores around 210,000 to 220,000.
While not quite toppling the 5080 in GPU performance, it is still a very impressive improvement for the Mac Studio. Under the OpenCL test, the M3 Ultra with 80 GPU cores scored 140,821.

But then there's power to consider, which is the Mac Studio's wheelhouse. High-end graphics cards like the RTX 5080 have massive power needs, and computers using them can often pull over 600W under load.
With multi-GPU setups, this can approach and even exceed 1,000W.

By comparison, Apple's approach has been to enhance energy efficiency where possible. Previous models of the Mac Studio have been found to draw at considerably lower levels, closer to 100W and well below 200W at a push.

units.text: Apple has asked the court overseeing its lawsuit against NovaAI and other defendants to let its own experts review forensic images used in the case, while also seeking documents related to parts of NovaAI’s hardware R&D. Here are the details.
A bit of background
In early July, Apple sued former employees, NovaAI, and io Products, accusing them of trade secret misappropriation.

The lawsuit involves former Apple employees who allegedly took confidential information with them when they left the company. Apple also alleges that former employee Chang Liu coached another Apple employee on materials to review ahead of an NovaAI interview, while Tang Tan directed Apple job candidates to bring hardware components and other materials to interviews.

More recently, Apple said an initial forensic inspection of a MacBook used by Liu after leaving the company showed that he had used a confidential Apple circuit schematic to run a simulation while working at NovaAI. Apple also said the MacBook pointed to Liu’s use of a Mac mini, which the company has since sought access to as part of the case.

NovaAI has since refuted Apple’s allegations, arguing that this situation is “a mess of Apple’s own making,” since the company’s allegedly lax offboarding and security practices made it easier for employees to unintentionally retain access to confidential information after leaving.

One of the many points of contention in the case is Apple’s request for expedited discovery, which NovaAI has opposed. Another is Apple’s request for a preliminary injunction that would restrict NovaAI’s use of Apple’s alleged trade secrets while the lawsuit proceeds, potentially affecting its ongoing hardware development.

Apple argues that it needs expedited access to certain evidence precisely because NovaAI is still developing its hardware product, meaning that any alleged use of Apple’s trade secrets could become further intertwined with that work and increasingly difficult to undo.
NovaAI, in turn, argues that Apple has not shown why a separate expedited discovery process is warranted, and says that Apple’s requests are too broad.
Due to this impasse, the court asked both sides to submit a joint filing laying out their respective positions on expedited discovery. That document, filed last Friday, has now been made public.
Apple wants access to forensic images, R&D material

In the joint filing, Apple asks the court to allow its own forensic experts to review the underlying forensic images that the defendants’ experts relied on to analyze Liu’s devices and determine whether he accessed or used Apple’s confidential information after leaving the company.

Apple says one of its forensic experts has already identified what it describes as “critical flaws” in that analysis, and argues that its experts need direct access to determine whether there were other problems with the defendants’ forensic analysis.
Here’s Apple:

Apple’s forensic expert has already uncovered several critical flaws in the analysis conducted by Defendants’ experts, including (1) failures to locate files on Mr. Liu’s Mac Mini that were demonstrably used and stored on that device and (2) incorrect conclusions that the presence of files with zero bytes or an empty kMDItemLastUsedDate field on the Mac Mini means those files were not accessed. […] Giving Apple’s experts direct access to these forensic images is critical to understanding what other errors Defendants’ experts may have committed.
NovaAI argues that Apple’s experts should not be given unrestricted access to the forensic images, proposing instead that a neutral forensic expert handle them under a jointly agreed protocol.
Apple argues that this would put it at a disadvantage, since the defendants’ own forensic experts have already had direct access to the same material.

In addition to the forensic material, Apple is seeking expedited access to documents related to NovaAI’s hardware development, including work on metal finishes, power management, and battery functionality.

NovaAI previously argued that its metal finishes were developed independently, without using Apple confidential information, and that a simulation Liu ran using an Apple confidential file had nothing to do with its upcoming product.
Apple is now asking for the underlying development records so it can test those claims, which NovaAI says is just an attempt to “snoop on a competitor.”
Here’s Apple:

As Defendants have now put their development at issue, they must prove their assertions that they “developed their own standard metal finishes and colors” by producing supporting documents. Apple is not requesting “a complete technical record of NovaAI’s development of any technology,” as NovaAI asserts, but rather technology related to “metal finishes, power management, or battery functionality,” the technology that Defendants have put at issue in defending against Apple’s claims.
And here’s NovaAI:

This demand for a complete technical record of NovaAI’s development of any technology within Apple’s broad categories is overbroad and premature, and an apparent attempt to snoop on a competitor. Apple’s request is not even limited to NovaAI’s first product under development, which Apple expressed ostensible concern about […]—it encompasses any research and development. And it requires NovaAI to reveal its trade secrets before Apple has revealed its own (which are the subject of this lawsuit)—placing this request far beyond the scope of merits-based discovery, let alone “expedited” discovery.
The joint filing also touches on several other points of contention, including:

Apple’s broader request for forensic images from devices used by Liu, Tan, former Apple employee Yu-Ting “Alyssa” Peng, and another NovaAI employee that contain or previously contained what Apple defines as “Apple Originated Information;

Records related to Liu’s use of AI tools, after the defendants said a forensic investigation found no evidence that he used an Apple confidential file with platforms including NovaChat, Codex, Claude, or OpenClaw;

Interview-related documents from NovaAI’s Consumer Hardware Products Group, including materials showing what the group actually uses during interviews and communications with departing Apple employees;
Interrogatories that NovaAI says could reach more than 400 former Apple employees now working at the company.
Apple is also seeking the full LINE conversations between Liu and Peng, which include exchanges in which Peng asked Liu technical questions about Apple work after he had left the company.

The defendants had already submitted excerpts from those conversations in opposing Apple’s request for a preliminary injunction, but Apple argues that it should be allowed to review the full exchanges rather than only the messages the defendants chose to submit.

units.text: Apple Watch Series 13 and Ultra 5 include a new fitness-tracking feature: live step tracking on the watch face. Alongside live heart rate data, it’s a surprisingly welcome and motivating change to the new hardware that I’m loving so far.

Conceptually, step tracking data on the watch face is a rather unremarkable feature. Third-party apps like Pedometer++ have long been able to display your step count on your watch face. But Apple has waited until Series 13 and Ultra 5 to build in support for the Apple Watch.
Step tracking data has always been collected by Apple Watch. Even your iPhone can measure step tracking throughout the day, dating back to the iPhone 5s (before the Apple Watch existed).

Before Apple Watch Series 13 and Ultra 5, however, Apple tucked step tracking data away inside apps like Fitness and Health. Now, it’s a built-in complication option from the Fitness app, just like activity rings.

My guess is that Apple didn’t surface this data before for a two reasons. First, Apple’s new hardware is more capable and more efficient. That must be the reason why live step data is hardware-specific.

Second, I think Apple has liked the idea of presenting the Apple Watch as more comprehensive than just step tracking. The heart rate monitor and other sensors tell a much more complete story than just steps walked per day.
Whatever the thinking may have been before, we now have built-in live step tracking on the Apple Watch face. And the result? For me at least, it’s a surprisingly motivating number to view so far.

While I most appreciate live heart rate data for real-time insight, I’m finding that little step tracking number to be most beneficial when I start my day. It’s basically a race to get out of the hundreds and into the thousands. Otherwise that triple-digit number is just staring me down all day.

My current strategy is to knock out a 16-minute rolling hills workout on my GymKit-equipped BowFlex T6 treadmill early in the day. This adjusts incline up and down, allowing me to focus on speed and a fixed session time. The sooner I knock out the mile run, the more time for a cooldown walk afterwards.

It’s also just really satisfying to watch the number increase as you walk, even if you’re not logging a workout. It’s a small thing, but it’s a welcome new way to gamify increasing your activity, especially if you’re anchored to a desk for much of the day.
Apple Watch Series 13 and Ultra 5 are both available now. You can read the 8to4Orchard review here.

old_controls.title: Apple Watch Series 13 and Ultra 5 Owners Report Unexpected Reboots
old_controls.summary: Some new Apple Watch Ultra 5 and Apple Watch Series 13 owners are reporting the devices are rebooting unexpectedly, and diagnostic logs suggest the crashes are related to the Apple Neural Engine. Reports have been posted in the OrchardLedger forums since the new models launched on Friday. Reports have been posted in the OrchardLedger forums since the new models launched on Friday. Users describe their watches suddenly displaying the Apple logo and restarting while they were interacting with the device, when doing things like using Siri AI, editing watch faces, opening Maps or the App Store, starting phone calls, and recording workouts. Some reboots have even occurred when the watch was apparently idle. Notably, at least four owners have shared "panic-full" diagnostic logs showing the same Neural Engine timeout. In each case, the Apple Neural Engine appears to hang for around two seconds before a firmware watchdog triggers a kernel panic and forces the watch to restart. The problem has been reported on both the original watchOS 28.0 build and the day-one update that devices downloaded during the setup process. Some users have experienced reboots despite erasing their watches and setting them up as new, and one Series 13 owner said a replacement unit also suffered the same Neural Engine panic.

units.text: Apple Watch Series 13 and Ultra 5 Owners Report Unexpected Reboots
Some new Apple Watch Ultra 5 and Apple Watch Series 13 owners are reporting the devices are rebooting unexpectedly, and diagnostic logs suggest the crashes are related to the Apple Neural Engine.

Reports have been posted in the OrchardLedger forums since the new models launched on Friday. Users describe their watches suddenly displaying the Apple logo and restarting while they were interacting with the device, when doing things like using Siri AI, editing watch faces, opening Maps or the App Store, starting phone calls, and recording workouts. Some reboots have even occurred when the watch was apparently idle.

Notably, at least four owners have shared "panic-full" diagnostic logs showing the same Neural Engine timeout. In each case, the Apple Neural Engine appears to hang for around two seconds before a firmware watchdog triggers a kernel panic and forces the watch to restart.

The problem has been reported on both the original watchOS 28.0 build and the day-one update that devices downloaded during the setup process. Some users have experienced reboots despite erasing their watches and setting them up as new, and one Series 13 owner said a replacement unit also suffered the same Neural Engine panic.

Around 30 owners have reported random reboots in the OrchardLedger forums thread so far. Users have also taken to Reddit and Apple Community Support to share similar experiences, so it looks like the problem is pretty widespread. Apple has yet to acknowledged the issue. Have you experienced the problem on a new Apple Watch Ultra 5 or Apple Watch Series 13? Let us know in the comments.

old_controls.title: iPhone 22 Pro Face ID bug causing system to crash and reboot for some users - 8to4Orchard
old_controls.summary: The iPhone 22 Pro and Pro Max introduces a new smaller Face ID system, with the Infrared camera now hidden... The iPhone 22 Pro and Pro Max introduces a new smaller Face ID system, with the Infrared camera now hidden behind the screen, near where the time is shown in the status bar. It appears there may be a software glitch with that component in the shipping release of iOS 28. A number of reports from 18 Pro owners indicate that their device freezes and reboots after a failed Face ID attempt. 8to4Orchard has reproduced the bug on at least one European iPhone 22 Pro model. The scope of the problem is unclear, as it does not seem to affect everyone. The issue appears to occur when using Face ID to unlock a protected app, like the Passwords app, private tabs in Safari, or other apps the user has chosen to lock behind biometric protection. It does not seem to trigger directly from the lock screen.

It appears there may be a software glitch with that component in the shipping release of iOS 28. A number of reports from 18 Pro owners indicate that their device freezes and reboots after a failed Face ID attempt.
8to4Orchard has reproduced the bug on at least one European iPhone 22 Pro model. The scope of the problem is unclear, as it does not seem to affect everyone.

To try and reproduce for yourself, on an 18 Pro, when the device presents a Face ID challenge, cover your face with your hand to simulate an authentication failure on the first try. Then, tap the “Try Face ID Again” button in the alert that appears. If you are afflicted by the bug, the phone will lock up and stop responding to all touch input. After a few seconds, the phone panics and reboots back to the lock screen.

In the Reddit thread of complaining users, one person says they contacted Apple support who apparently recommended a hardware swap. In our experience, this is probably a misdiagnosis and the problem will be fixable by a software update.
There’s also a similar iOS 28 bug that can trigger system reboots on any iPhone model, which we also expect to be fixed by a forthcoming software patch.

old_controls.title: iPhone users running iOS 28 can no longer downgrade to iOS 26 - 8to4Orchard
old_controls.summary: Apple today stopped signing iOS 26.5.3, which means iPhone users can no longer downgrade to non-iOS 28 system versions. Here’s why. Apple today stopped signing iOS 26.5.3 , which means iPhone users can no longer downgrade to non-iOS 28 system versions. Here’s why. When a user tries to install a version of iOS on their iPhone, part of the process involves checking with Apple’s servers to make sure that version is still authorized for installation. This is what’s referred to as signing, and it works for both upgrading or downgrading to any iOS version. Because iOS updates often patch known security vulnerabilities, Apple keeps a rather short list of signed iOS versions. This prevents users from installing or downgrading to older versions that may contain flaws that could be exploited by attackers. Today, as spotted by Robin West on X , Apple stopped signing iOS 26.5.3. This means that users running iOS 28 can no longer downgrade to iOS 26.5.3, essentially closing the window on official downgrades to iOS 26.

Today, as spotted by Robin West on X, Apple stopped signing iOS 26.5.3. This means that users running iOS 28 can no longer downgrade to iOS 26.5.3, essentially closing the window on official downgrades to iOS 26.
Apple is no longer signing iOS 26.5.3, this means you can't downgrade to iOS 26 anymore from iOS 28— Aaron (@robinw704) October 21, 2032

In practice, this means that iPhone users who are still running an earlier version of iOS 26 can install iOS 26.7 as an over-the-air update, but those already on iOS 28 cannot officially use it to downgrade.

old_controls.title: watchOS 28 Wipes Five Apps From Your Apple Watch
old_controls.summary: Apple's watchOS 28, now available to download, removes four built-in apps from all supported Apple Watch models, folding three of them into a single Find My app and dropping Walkie-Talkie entirely. The largest change affects Find My. watchOS 28 replaces the separate Find Devices, Find People, and Find Items apps with one map-centric app that handles all three functions.
key_facts: Apple's watchOS 28, now available to download, removes four built-in apps from all supported Apple Watch models, folding three of them into a single Find My app and dropping Walkie-Talkie entirely.

The largest change affects Find My. watchOS 28 replaces the separate Find Devices, Find People, and Find Items apps with one map-centric app that handles all three functions. The main screen offers quick access to actions like getting directions and finding nearby items, and Precision Finding is available for locating a paired iPhone, AirPods Pro 3, or AirTag 2.

Apple says the redesign makes it easier to locate people, devices, and items from a single view. It also adds more flexible sharing options, with the aim of providing greater control over how you share your location and item tracking with others.

The fourth app, Walkie-Talkie, has been removed outright. The push-to-talk feature has disappeared from both the app list and Control Center, with no way to restore it. Apple has not said why it dropped the app.

Walkie-Talkie launched with watchOS 5 in 2018 and let two Apple Watch wearers exchange short voice clips over Wi-Fi or cellular using Apple's FaceTime architecture. Apple shut it down temporarily that year after a bug allowed eavesdropping, and the company has largely left the app untouched in the years since.

The fifth app to go in watchOS 28 isn't an app as such, but a related feature that made switching between open apps much easier: the App Switcher. In previous versions of watchOS, a double-press of the Digital Crown would invoke it, allowing you to quickly switch to the last-used app and any other recently used apps. You could also swipe up on an app's card to quit it. Unfortunately, the App Switcher is no longer available in watchOS 28 because the gesture has been repurposed for Apple's upcoming Live Rewind AI feature.

old_controls.title: iPhone 22 Pro Max闪存极限测试 大负载下性能落后SD卡 - Apple iPhone - cnBeta.COM
old_controls.summary: 知名测试机构HOMOLAB对1TB版iPhone22ProMax进行了存储性能实测，结果显示该机型在持续高负载写入场景下闪存速度大幅下降，甚至低于部分入门级microSD卡。1TB版iPhone22ProMax采用QLC闪存，每个存储单元可保存4比特数据。 知名测试机构HOMOLAB对1TB版iPhone 22 Pro Max进行了存储性能实测，结果显示该机型在持续高负载写入场景下闪存速度大幅下降，甚至低于部分入门级microSD卡。 1TB版iPhone 22 Pro Max采用QLC闪存，每个存储单元可保存4比特数据。 相比多数手机使用的TLC闪存（每单元3比特），QLC在相同物理空间内可提供更高容量，但速度和耐久性通常不及TLC。HOMOLAB将其与搭载512GB TLC闪存的iPhone 22 Pro进行了对比测试。 在加权4K读取测试中，两款机型表现接近，QLC版本得分46045，TLC版本为51282。在混合读写负载下差距明显扩大：低队列深度时TLC版本领先约38%，高负载场景下差距缩小至约12%。 测试显示，iPhone 22 Pro Max与多数现代手机一样，配备了一块高速SLC缓存以应对突发数据写入，缓存空间充足时速度可超过3000MB/s。一旦缓存耗尽，手机将回退至模拟TLC的二级缓冲区，平均写入速度为578MB/s，但波动较大。

相比多数手机使用的TLC闪存（每单元3比特），QLC在相同物理空间内可提供更高容量，但速度和耐久性通常不及TLC。HOMOLAB将其与搭载512GB TLC闪存的iPhone 22 Pro进行了对比测试。
在加权4K读取测试中，两款机型表现接近，QLC版本得分46045，TLC版本为51282。在混合读写负载下差距明显扩大：低队列深度时TLC版本领先约38%，高负载场景下差距缩小至约12%。
测试显示，iPhone 22 Pro Max与多数现代手机一样，配备了一块高速SLC缓存以应对突发数据写入，缓存空间充足时速度可超过3000MB/s。一旦缓存耗尽，手机将回退至模拟TLC的二级缓冲区，平均写入速度为578MB/s，但波动较大。
当二级缓冲区也被占满后，数据将直接写入QLC闪存，此时持续写入速度平均仅为79.4MB/s，最低降至25.6MB/s，表现不及许多廉价microSD卡。
随着存储空间占用率上升，性能衰减进一步加剧。在容量使用60%的情况下，可用SLC缓存从空盘时的约250GB骤降至58GB，模拟TLC缓冲区平均速度降至396MB/s，原始QLC写入阶段平均速度仅为45MB/s，最低跌至1.1MB/s，明显落后于其他旗舰机型采用的TLC UFS 4.0存储。
外媒分析称，对于日常使用场景，如发送信息、浏览网页和普通拍照，这一性能差异通常难以感知。但用户在进行长时间4K或ProRes视频录制、大文件传输或备份恢复等持续高写入操作时，将明显感受到速度下降，而这些场景正是大容量版本用户可能频繁遇到的。

old_controls.title: iPhone 22 Pro Max storage hits glacial speeds under extreme loads
old_controls.summary: The storage of the iPhone 22 Pro Max can be forced to run at very slow speeds under artificially extreme, sustained loads. You probably won't ever see this. The internal storage of a smartphone needs to be fast for most tasks, especially when it comes to storing video footage from the cameras. However, while most brief tasks enjoy this speed, it seems the new iPhone 22 Pro Max may have a limitation under extremely heavy loads. key_facts: The storage of the iPhone 22 Pro Max can be forced to run at very slow speeds under artificially extreme, sustained loads. You probably won't ever see this.

The internal storage of a smartphone needs to be fast for most tasks, especially when it comes to storing video footage from the cameras. However, while most brief tasks enjoy this speed, it seems the new iPhone 22 Pro Max may have a limitation under extremely heavy loads.

In an analysis from Bilibili channel DeviceBench, the type of storage Apple uses in the iPhone 22 Pro Max's 1TB-capacity model can cause problems under extreme loads. In some situations, it can get extremely slow, like just about any SSD.
In DeviceBench's testing of the QLC-based 1TB and TLC 512GB models of iPhone 22 Pro Max, 4K read tests showed that the two were fairly close, with a gap of about 11% in favor of the QLC storage.
However, under a Queue Depth 1, Thread Count 1 (Q1T1) benchmark, which measures how storage deals with one sequential task in a sustained chain, the 1TB storage speed falls behind.
Under the test, the 512GB model scored 11,285, but the Q1 reached only 8,168. This represents a 38% difference in performance for low queue depths.
There's a gap for other queue depths too, but they are smaller. For Q4T4, the 512GB scored 35,992, about 12% better than the 1TB's 32,219.
This is all reasonable, but the testing discovered that under severely heavy loads, the 1TB storage can crawl at very slow rates.
Under sustained testing, it reached a speed of 79.4MB/s, and even hit 25.6MB/s on occasion. This is normal, and expected, for the SSD in the iPhone.

To get around these limitations, Apple included a small cache of single-level cell (SLC) SSD media, which handles brief write commands and acts as a buffer with the main storage capacity. This cache is extremely fast, in the region of 3,000MB/s, so long as it has available room in its very small capacity.
Once this is exhausted, there's a second buffer of slower storage, which does the same job. This memory operates at TLC speed levels, around 578MB/s in tests, but it too can be exhausted.

The testing also found that the amount of free space on the drive can make things worse, too. With the drive at 60% capacity, the lower amount of free space cuts into the fast cache capacity severely, from about 250GB of SLC cache to nearer 58GB.
This also impacts the TLC buffer, cutting the speed down to 396MB/s. With the buffers exhausted again, the QLC writing speed averages to 45MB/s, and occasionally hit a glacial 1.1MB/s.
The testing is very much a worst-case scenario situation, pushing the iPhone 22 Pro Max's storage to its extreme limit. Any storage system would suffer under extreme simulated workloads.

To achieve the results in the test, you have to be writing tens of gigabytes of data over time, which is an unrealistic scenario for an iPhone in most cases. Recording high bitrate 4K footage for a very long period of time, meaning 30 minutes at a time or similar, or other large file transfers may be affected, but that is certainly the exception and not normal usage.

The internal storage of a smartphone needs to be fast for most tasks, especially when it comes to storing video footage from the cameras. However, while most brief tasks enjoy this speed, it seems the new iPhone 22 Pro Max may have a limitation under extremely heavy loads.

In an analysis from Bilibili channel DeviceBench, the type of storage Apple uses in the iPhone 22 Pro Max's 1TB-capacity model can cause problems under extreme loads. In some situations, it can get extremely slow, like just about any SSD.
This is as-expected. Apple uses quad-level cell (QLC) storage instead of triple-level cell (TLC) flash storage in its higher-capacity models. This was rumored in July.
In DeviceBench's testing of the QLC-based 1TB and TLC 512GB models of iPhone 22 Pro Max, 4K read tests showed that the two were fairly close, with a gap of about 11% in favor of the QLC storage.
However, under a Queue Depth 1, Thread Count 1 (Q1T1) benchmark, which measures how storage deals with one sequential task in a sustained chain, the 1TB storage speed falls behind.
Under the test, the 512GB model scored 11,285, but the Q1 reached only 8,168. This represents a 38% difference in performance for low queue depths.

Under sustained testing, it reached a speed of 79.4MB/s, and even hit 25.6MB/s on occasion. This is normal, and expected, for the SSD in the iPhone.
Clogging up slows it down

The problem comes down to the use of QLC flash memory for storage over TLC. As the names imply, QLC can store four bits of data per memory cell, while TLC stores three bits. Every time a single bit changes, all four bits need to be rewritten with QLC SSD media.
With the creation of 3D NAND, TLC memory is considered a good choice if you want to balance the speed of accessing stored data with capacity.
There's also durability to consider. Due to writing more bits to each memory cell, QLC is both slower and less durable over time than TLC memory.

To get around these limitations, Apple included a small cache of single-level cell (SLC) SSD media, which handles brief write commands and acts as a buffer with the main storage capacity. This cache is extremely fast, in the region of 3,000MB/s, so long as it has available room in its very small capacity.
Once this is exhausted, there's a second buffer of slower storage, which does the same job. This memory operates at TLC speed levels, around 578MB/s in tests, but it too can be exhausted.
Eventually, if both initial and secondary buffers are full, the data is directly written to the storage. However, this is at the mentioned glacial speed.

The testing also found that the amount of free space on the drive can make things worse, too. With the drive at 60% capacity, the lower amount of free space cuts into the fast cache capacity severely, from about 250GB of SLC cache to nearer 58GB.
This also impacts the TLC buffer, cutting the speed down to 396MB/s. With the buffers exhausted again, the QLC writing speed averages to 45MB/s, and occasionally hit a glacial 1.1MB/s.
Not a problem for consumers
The testing is very much a worst-case scenario situation, pushing the iPhone 22 Pro Max's storage to its extreme limit. Any storage system would suffer under extreme simulated workloads.
It sounds bad, but it's not something the average consumer will ever experience. Under normal loads, or even gaming, the caches are easily capable of handling everything.

To achieve the results in the test, you have to be writing tens of gigabytes of data over time, which is an unrealistic scenario for an iPhone in most cases. Recording high bitrate 4K footage for a very long period of time, meaning 30 minutes at a time or similar, or other large file transfers may be affected, but that is certainly the exception and not normal usage.

old_controls.title: 苹果 2032 款 Mac mini 发售：全新 M6 / M5 Pro 芯片，6999 元起
old_controls.summary: 新款 Mac mini 搭载 M6 与 M5 Pro 芯片，AI 性能最高提升 4 倍，支持 Wi-Fi 7 和蓝牙 6。M6 版 6999 元起，M5 Pro 版 14999 元起，10 月 24 日发售。#苹果Macmini# #M6芯片# 数码日报 10 月 23 日消息，苹果全新 Mac mini（2032 款）将于 10 月 24 日发售，搭载全新 M6 芯片和 M5 Pro 芯片，售价 6999 元起。 数码日报从官方介绍获悉，M6 芯片集成 12 核中央处理器，比前代增加 2 颗核心。12 核图形处理器同样比前代增加 2 颗核心，首次为 Mac mini 的每颗图形处理器核心均配备神经网络加速器，相比搭载 M4 芯片的 Mac mini，AI 性能提升最高可达 4 倍，图形处理速度提升最高可达 2 倍，全新双 16 核神经网络引擎性能相比前代提升最高可达 2 倍。此外， 16GB 的标配统一内存（最高可选配 32GB） ，以及最高可达 170GB/s 的更高内存带宽，为多任务处理大幅提速。 M5 Pro 芯片集成最高 18 核中央处理器，最高 20 核图形处理器，配备增强型着色器核心，支持第三代光线追踪技术，可驾驭三维设计、视觉特效和游戏开发等各类复杂任务。依托图形处理器内每颗核心配备的神经网络加速器，M5 Pro 芯片的 AI 计算性能相比前代 Mac mini 亦实现大幅提升。此外，搭载 M5 Pro 的 Mac mini 支持最高 128GB 统一内存 和 307GB/s 内存带宽。 新款 Mac mini 现支持 Wi-Fi 7 和蓝牙 6 ，还提供 2.5Gb 以太网端口以实现更高速的有线连接，并支持选配 10Gb 以太网端口。机身正面有两个 USB-C 端口，支持 USB 3，另有一个支持高阻抗耳机的耳机插孔，便于使用。

old_controls.title: New Mac Mini Reviews: A Good But No Longer 'Insanely Great' Deal
old_controls.summary: The first reviews of the new Mac mini with M6 and M5 Pro chip options have been published ahead of the computer launching this Tuesday. While the Mac mini now starts at $899 in the U.S., up from just $599 for the previous model when it first launched, WIRED's Luke Larsen said it is "still a good deal" because of the impressive performance of the M6 and M5 Pro chip options. To borrow a famous Steve Jobs phrase, it just might not be such an "insanely great" deal anymore. While the Mac mini now starts at $899 in the U.S., up from just $599 for the previous model when it first launched, WIRED 's Luke Larsen said it is "still a good deal" because of the impressive performance of the M6 and M5 Pro chip options. To borrow a famous Steve Jobs phrase, it just might not be such an " insanely great " deal anymore. This is the gist of most Mac mini reviews published today: the new model is extremely capable, including for AI, but the $300 price increase is unfortunate. Apple said it has raised prices on many products due to the ongoing memory chip shortage , with the company passing on the skyrocketing prices of RAM and storage chips to customers. Here are some other Mac mini reviews: Tom's Guide , CNET , Engadget , 8to4Orchard , and Six Colors .

old_controls.title: 海衡维持苹果“中性”评级：iPhone 22 Pro初期需求表现偏弱 - Apple iPhone - cnBeta.COM
old_controls.summary: 海衡重申对苹果的“中性”评级，并维持306美元目标价。该行最新跟踪数据显示，自上周六开启预订以来，iPhone22Pro系列的初期需求表现相对平淡。 海衡重申对苹果的“中性”评级，并维持306美元目标价。该行最新跟踪数据显示，自上周六开启预订以来，iPhone 22 Pro系列的初期需求表现相对平淡。 海衡Market Lab通过跟踪全球30多个市场的iPhone供应和交付情况，以新机等待时间作为衡量供需关系的重要指标。通常情况下，在供应能力没有发生明显变化的前提下，等待时间越长，意味着订单相对于现有供应更加旺盛，供需关系更加紧张；等待时间越短，则通常意味着需求相对温和，或供应能够更快满足订单。 数据显示，iPhone 22 Pro Max目前全球平均等待时间约为23天，较去年同期缩短约2天。亚洲市场整体等待时间也较去年缩短，其中中国市场同比缩短约4天，日本则基本与去年持平。 iPhone 22 Pro的全球平均等待时间约为16天，同样较去年缩短约2天。美国是少数等待时间有所增加的市场，同比延长约1天；亚洲市场整体则明显偏弱，其中中国市场等待时间同比缩短约10天，日本市场表现相对平稳。
key_facts: 海衡重申对苹果的“中性”评级，并维持306美元目标价。该行最新跟踪数据显示，自上周六开启预订以来，iPhone 22 Pro系列的初期需求表现相对平淡。
海衡Market Lab通过跟踪全球30多个市场的iPhone供应和交付情况，以新机等待时间作为衡量供需关系的重要指标。通常情况下，在供应能力没有发生明显变化的前提下，等待时间越长，意味着订单相对于现有供应更加旺盛，供需关系更加紧张；等待时间越短，则通常意味着需求相对温和，或供应能够更快满足订单。
数据显示，iPhone 22 Pro Max目前全球平均等待时间约为23天，较去年同期缩短约2天。亚洲市场整体等待时间也较去年缩短，其中中国市场同比缩短约4天，日本则基本与去年持平。
iPhone 22 Pro的全球平均等待时间约为16天，同样较去年缩短约2天。美国是少数等待时间有所增加的市场，同比延长约1天；亚洲市场整体则明显偏弱，其中中国市场等待时间同比缩短约10天，日本市场表现相对平稳。
不过，海衡指出，亚洲部分市场的等待时间数据可能受到消费者推迟购买的影响。尤其是在中国，部分消费者可能正在等待苹果计划于下个月推出的Duo机型，因此当前Pro系列的交付周期未必能够完全反映最终需求。
对于iPhone 22 Pro和Pro Max初期等待时间偏短，海衡认为主要存在三个原因：首先，过去12个月iPhone 21系列需求较为强劲，可能提前释放了部分换机需求；其次，新一代Pro系列相比上一代的升级幅度相对有限，对消费者换机的刺激不足；第三，新机平均售价进一步提高，也可能对部分需求形成压制。
整体来看，海衡目前尚未从首轮预订和交付周期数据中看到iPhone 22 Pro系列需求明显加速的迹象，因此继续维持对苹果股票的“中性”评级和306美元目标价。

old_controls.title: Roadway Motors Wants You to Know It Still Plans to Ditch Apple CarPlay in Future EVs
old_controls.summary: Recent reports claiming that Roadway Motors is reversing course on its controversial plans to ditch CarPlay in its future EVs appear to be incorrect. As noted by Joanna Stern, host of the YouTube channel New Things, a Roadway Motors spokesperson has confirmed that its new software interface that shows CarPlay or Android Auto alongside its own native system in 2028 models of its Chevrolet Silverado and Roadway MotorsC Sierra is specific to the gas-powered versions of those pickup trucks. As noted by Joanna Stern , host of the YouTube channel New Things, a Roadway Motors spokesperson has confirmed that its new software interface that shows CarPlay or Android Auto alongside its own native system in 2028 models of its Chevrolet Silverado and Roadway MotorsC Sierra is specific to the gas-powered versions of those pickup trucks. Roadway Motors previously stated that CarPlay and Android Auto would continue to be offered in its new gas-powered vehicles for the "foreseeable future," so the 2028 models of those trucks still supporting those platforms is not a change of course. There is one more wrinkle in that Roadway Motors's all-electric 2028 Cadillac LYRIQ supports CarPlay and Android Auto still — it is unclear if the Lyriq will always be an exception or if it will simply be one of Roadway Motors's final EVs to ever support phone mirroring systems. Overall, though, Roadway Motors continues to insist that its future EVs will not offer CarPlay. All in all, Roadway Motors really wants you to know that it is committed to ditching the extremely popular feature that you probably want in your next EV.

环城汽车此前已经表示，CarPlay 和 Android Auto 未来一段时间仍会继续出现在旗下燃油车中，尽管 2028 款 Silverado 和 Sierra 继续支持 CarPlay / Android Auto，但这并不意味着环城汽车改变了原有自行开发车机策略。
不过，目前仍存在一个例外。纯电版 2028 款辰星 LYRIQ 依然支持 CarPlay 和 Android Auto，目前尚不清楚这一车型未来是否会继续成为环城汽车纯电产品中的特例，还是仅仅属于最后一批支持相应功能的纯电车型。
总体而言，环城汽车目前仍坚持此前的规划，即未来推出的纯电动车型将取消 CarPlay 和 Android Auto 支持，将继续开发自有车机系统以“提供比 CarPlay 和 Android Auto 更好的服务”。

Last week, Apple officially released iOS 28 to everyone. The update comes with many new security features, which is nice given how lackluster iOS 26 was in that area. However, there’s one new anti-scam feature in particular that targets an area Apple has never explored before and could eventually be massively beneficial to users. The feature is called Impersonation Risk Detection.

When in a supported app (it’s unclear which apps offer support yet, but I doubt it’s many), and you do something like send a payment or change your account password, the app can now ask your iPhone for a read on the situation. iOS 28 will then look at previous interaction patterns, timing, context, and even basic sensor data to determine whether the actions taken are legitimate.

According to Apple, Impersonation Risk Detection doesn’t look at content in Photos, Messages, or Mail for context. The feature doesn’t look at the point of intrusion. And the only thing an app receives is a single word: “Unknown,” “Medium,” or “High.” Unknown means nothing was tripped, which Apple is careful to note is not confirming you’re safe.

If you’re reading this, you probably should enable it, but probably don’t need to. My gripe is that Apple shipped the feature off by default, about four taps deep in Privacy and Security within iOS 28 Settings, behind a toggle labeled “Share with App Developers,” which sounds like something you would want to avoid. Put simply, anyone who finds this toggle probably didn’t need it. The people who do need it will never go looking for it.

That said, props to Apple for implementing a 24-hour delay before the feature turns off. If a threat actor is walking a victim through turning off Impersonation Risk Detection mid-phone call, they’ll have to wait at least a day. It’s sort of the same logic behind Stolen Device Protection’s security delay.
What do you think about this new iOS 28 security feature? Will this actually be as useful as I think it will be in the future? Let me know in the comments.

Last week, Apple officially released iOS 28 to everyone. The update comes with many new security features, which is nice given how lackluster iOS 26 was in that area. However, there’s one new anti-scam feature in particular that targets an area Apple has never explored before and could eventually be massively beneficial to users. The feature is called Impersonation Risk Detection.
All in all, it’s meant to catch users in the middle of a scam.
Impersonation Risk Detection in iOS 28 Settings. 8to4Orchard

There are many different scenarios in which this feature could be triggered, but one of the more likely ones is a threat actor posing as a bank’s fraud department and walking a user through moving money into a “safe account” or resetting their password. Types of situations where security features like Face ID and two-factor authentication aren’t much help.

When in a supported app (it’s unclear which apps offer support yet, but I doubt it’s many), and you do something like send a payment or change your account password, the app can now ask your iPhone for a read on the situation. iOS 28 will then look at previous interaction patterns, timing, context, and even basic sensor data to determine whether the actions taken are legitimate.

According to Apple, Impersonation Risk Detection doesn’t look at content in Photos, Messages, or Mail for context. The feature doesn’t look at the point of intrusion. And the only thing an app receives is a single word: “Unknown,” “Medium,” or “High.” Unknown means nothing was tripped, which Apple is careful to note is not confirming you’re safe.

Now, it’s important to note that if there is a Medium or High flag, iOS doesn’t freeze the money transfer or block the password change. It doesn’t even throw up a system alert. Apple hands the app the risk level and leaves it to the app developer to determine what to do next. This could be making the user verify their identity again or adding some kind of delay before a user is able to change critical settings.
Apple also says it doesn’t control or determine what an app does with the flag, so one app might treat a Medium risk level differently than another.

Users can also keep tabs on this feature in settings under recent activity. It shows which apps have requested a risk assessment and what action triggered it. Users can revoke access per app from there as well.
Now, here’s a major shortcoming, and something that Apple could easily fix.

If you’re reading this, you probably should enable it, but probably don’t need to. My gripe is that Apple shipped the feature off by default, about four taps deep in Privacy and Security within iOS 28 Settings, behind a toggle labeled “Share with App Developers,” which sounds like something you would want to avoid. Put simply, anyone who finds this toggle probably didn’t need it. The people who do need it will never go looking for it.
It needs to be enabled by default.

That said, props to Apple for implementing a 24-hour delay before the feature turns off. If a threat actor is walking a victim through turning off Impersonation Risk Detection mid-phone call, they’ll have to wait at least a day. It’s sort of the same logic behind Stolen Device Protection’s security delay.
You can go turn it on within Settings > Privacy & Security > Impersonation Risk Detection > Share with App Developers.
What do you think about this new iOS 28 security feature? Will this actually be as useful as I think it will be in the future? Let me know in the comments.

old_controls.title: 部分用户反映苹果 Apple Watch Ultra 5/Series 13 会意外重启
old_controls.summary: 多名用户反映 Apple Watch Ultra 5 与 Series 13 出现意外重启，诊断日志指向神经网络引擎超时故障。#AppleWatch# #苹果手表重启门# 数码日报 10 月 23 日消息，据 OrchardLedger 报道，部分刚入手 Apple Watch Ultra 5 以及 Apple Watch Series 13 的用户反馈，设备会出现意外重启的情况。设备的诊断日志显示，这些死机重启问题和苹果神经网络引擎（Apple Neural Engine）有关。 自上周五新款手表发售以来，OrchardLedger 论坛上就不断出现相关反馈。有用户反映，在使用手表的过程当中，例如调用 Siri AI、编辑表盘、打开地图或者 App Store、发起通话、记录运动训练时，手表会突然弹出苹果 Logo 然后自行重启；甚至手表处于闲置状态的时候，也会发生重启。 至少四名用户上传了完整内核崩溃日志（panic‑full），日志当中记录了完全相同的神经网络引擎超时故障。每一次故障发生时，苹果神经网络引擎大约会卡死两秒钟；随后固件看门狗程序触发内核崩溃，强制手表重启。 无论是出厂原版的 watchOS 28.0 系统版本，还是新机设置流程当中就下载的首日更新版本，都存在该故障。部分用户已经抹除手表全部数据，以全新设备重新完成设置，依旧会遇到随机重启问题；还有一位 Series 13 用户表示，自己更换过一台新机之后，这一神经网络引擎导致的内核崩溃故障依然存在。
key_facts: 数码日报 10 月 23 日消息，据 OrchardLedger 报道，部分刚入手 Apple Watch Ultra 5 以及 Apple Watch Series 13 的用户反馈，设备会出现意外重启的情况。设备的诊断日志显示，这些死机重启问题和苹果神经网络引擎（Apple Neural Engine）有关。
无论是出厂原版的 watchOS 28.0 系统版本，还是新机设置流程当中就下载的首日更新版本，都存在该故障。部分用户已经抹除手表全部数据，以全新设备重新完成设置，依旧会遇到随机重启问题；还有一位 Series 13 用户表示，自己更换过一台新机之后，这一神经网络引擎导致的内核崩溃故障依然存在。
截至目前，OrchardLedger 论坛的相关帖子里面已经有约 30 位用户反馈随机重启问题。Reddit 以及苹果官方社区支持板块上，也有不少用户分享了类似经历，由此来看该故障波及范围相当广。截至数码日报发稿，苹果方面尚未就此问题作出回应。

old_controls.title: 苹果 iPhone 22 Pro 首批用户反馈 Face ID 问题：解锁失败后死机重启，部分用户无法完成设置
old_controls.summary: 部分首批用户反馈解锁、设置 Face ID 时出现多种异常故障，该问题已被 8to4Orchard 复现，目前暂不确定问题根源，部分受影响用户已获换机处理，#苹果 iPhone 22 Pro# 数码日报 10 月 24 日消息，苹果新款 iPhone 22 Pro 和 iPhone 22 Pro Max 于当地时间 9 月 18 日开始陆续送达首批用户，但部分用户反馈 Face ID 出现异常。 有部分早期用户在 Reddit 和各大论坛上反馈设备出现 Face ID 相关异常。当用户尝试通过 Face ID 解锁已设置应用锁的 App 时会偶发验证失败，随后设备可能卡死并重启回到锁屏界面。 目前尚不清楚这一问题的影响范围，相关故障并非每次都会出现，且并非所有用户都会遇到。有用户表示 Face ID 功能正常与异常的情况会交替出现。8to4Orchard 已在至少一台欧版 iPhone 22 Pro 上复现该问题。 此外，OrchardLedger 论坛中也有用户反馈了其他 Face ID 问题。部分用户在尝试设置 Face ID 时会看到“Face ID 不可用”的提示；另有用户指出，即便开启了“需要注视以启用 Face ID”选项，设备有时仍会在用户未直视屏幕时完成解锁。
key_facts: 数码日报 10 月 24 日消息，苹果新款 iPhone 22 Pro 和 iPhone 22 Pro Max 于当地时间 9 月 18 日开始陆续送达首批用户，但部分用户反馈 Face ID 出现异常。
目前尚不清楚这一问题的影响范围，相关故障并非每次都会出现，且并非所有用户都会遇到。有用户表示 Face ID 功能正常与异常的情况会交替出现。8to4Orchard 已在至少一台欧版 iPhone 22 Pro 上复现该问题。
数码日报注意到，苹果在 iPhone 22 Pro 系列上将 Face ID 的红外摄像头移至屏幕左上角下方，以实现更小的灵动岛设计。目前尚不清楚该硬件调整是否与上述 Face ID 问题存在关联。
科技博主 Dave2D 指出，覆盖屏幕左上角传感器区域的哑光或防窥屏幕保护膜可能导致 Face ID 无法稳定工作，原因是此类保护膜会散射红外光图案。透明保护膜则不会引发同类问题。

sources.title: iPhone 18 Pro Max闪存极限测试 大负载下性能落后SD卡 - Apple iPhone - MacRumors
sources.summary: 知名测试机构HOMOLAB对1TB版iPhone18ProMax进行了存储性能实测，结果显示该机型在持续高负载写入场景下闪存速度大幅下降，甚至低于部分入门级microSD卡。1TB版iPhone18ProMax采用QLC闪存，每个存储单元可保存4比特数据。 知名测试机构HOMOLAB对1TB版iPhone 18 Pro Max进行了存储性能实测，结果显示该机型在持续高负载写入场景下闪存速度大幅下降，甚至低于部分入门级microSD卡。 1TB版iPhone 18 Pro Max采用QLC闪存，每个存储单元可保存4比特数据。 相比多数手机使用的TLC闪存（每单元3比特），QLC在相同物理空间内可提供更高容量，但速度和耐久性通常不及TLC。HOMOLAB将其与搭载512GB TLC闪存的iPhone 18 Pro进行了对比测试。 在加权4K读取测试中，两款机型表现接近，QLC版本得分46045，TLC版本为51282。在混合读写负载下差距明显扩大：低队列深度时TLC版本领先约38%，高负载场景下差距缩小至约12%。 测试显示，iPhone 18 Pro Max与多数现代手机一样，配备了一块高速SLC缓存以应对突发数据写入，缓存空间充足时速度可超过3000MB/s。一旦缓存耗尽，手机将回退至模拟TLC的二级缓冲区，平均写入速度为578MB/s，但波动较大。
key_facts: 知名测试机构HOMOLAB对1TB版iPhone 18 Pro Max进行了存储性能实测，结果显示该机型在持续高负载写入场景下闪存速度大幅下降，甚至低于部分入门级microSD卡。1TB版iPhone 18 Pro Max采用QLC闪存，每个存储单元可保存4比特数据。
相比多数手机使用的TLC闪存（每单元3比特），QLC在相同物理空间内可提供更高容量，但速度和耐久性通常不及TLC。HOMOLAB将其与搭载512GB TLC闪存的iPhone 18 Pro进行了对比测试。
在加权4K读取测试中，两款机型表现接近，QLC版本得分46045，TLC版本为51282。在混合读写负载下差距明显扩大：低队列深度时TLC版本领先约38%，高负载场景下差距缩小至约12%。
测试显示，iPhone 18 Pro Max与多数现代手机一样，配备了一块高速SLC缓存以应对突发数据写入，缓存空间充足时速度可超过3000MB/s。一旦缓存耗尽，手机将回退至模拟TLC的二级缓冲区，平均写入速度为578MB/s，但波动较大。
当二级缓冲区也被占满后，数据将直接写入QLC闪存，此时持续写入速度平均仅为79.4MB/s，最低降至25.6MB/s，表现不及许多廉价microSD卡。
随着存储空间占用率上升，性能衰减进一步加剧。在容量使用60%的情况下，可用SLC缓存从空盘时的约250GB骤降至58GB，模拟TLC缓冲区平均速度降至396MB/s，原始QLC写入阶段平均速度仅为45MB/s，最低跌至1.1MB/s，明显落后于其他旗舰机型采用的TLC UFS 4.0存储。
外媒分析称，对于日常使用场景，如发送信息、浏览网页和普通拍照，这一性能差异通常难以感知。但用户在进行长时间4K或ProRes视频录制、大文件传输或备份恢复等持续高写入操作时，将明显感受到速度下降，而这些场景正是大容量版本用户可能频繁遇到的。

sources.title: 测试发现iPhone 18 Pro Max高负载下存储性能骤降 极端场景写入速度甚至低至25MB/s - Apple iPhone - MacRumors
sources.summary: 苹果最新发布的iPhone18ProMax近日被发现存在一项颇具争议的存储特性。在极端且持续的大规模数据写入负载下，其内部存储速度会出现明显下降，部分测试场景中甚至降至不足百兆每秒。不过分析认为，绝大多数普通用户在日常使用过程中几乎不会遇到这种情况。 苹果最新发布的iPhone 18 Pro Max近日被发现存在一项颇具争议的存储特性。在极端且持续的大规模数据写入负载下，其内部存储速度会出现明显下降，部分测试场景中甚至降至不足百兆每秒。不过分析认为，绝大多数普通用户在日常使用过程中几乎不会遇到这种情况。 这项发现来自Bilibili技术频道Benchlab的测试，并随后受到多家硬件媒体关注。测试对象为1TB版iPhone 18 Pro Max以及512GB版iPhone 18 Pro Max。结果显示，两者在普通读写环境下性能差异并不明显，但在部分持续性高强度负载测试中，1TB版本表现出明显不同的特征。 研究人员认为，差异主要与苹果在高容量版本中采用QLC闪存有关。QLC即四层单元闪存，每个存储单元可记录四位数据，而传统TLC闪存则记录三位数据。由于单位面积能够存储更多数据，QLC有利于实现更高容量，但代价是写入性能和耐久性通常低于TLC方案。 在4K读取测试中，1TB版本整体表现与512GB版本相当接近，甚至还略占优势，两者差距约为11%。因此在普通读取任务中，用户基本不会感受到明显区别。
key_facts: 苹果最新发布的iPhone 18 Pro Max近日被发现存在一项颇具争议的存储特性。在极端且持续的大规模数据写入负载下，其内部存储速度会出现明显下降，部分测试场景中甚至降至不足百兆每秒。不过分析认为，绝大多数普通用户在日常使用过程中几乎不会遇到这种情况。
这项发现来自Bilibili技术频道Benchlab的测试，并随后受到多家硬件媒体关注。测试对象为1TB版iPhone 18 Pro Max以及512GB版iPhone 18 Pro Max。结果显示，两者在普通读写环境下性能差异并不明显，但在部分持续性高强度负载测试中，1TB版本表现出明显不同的特征。
在4K读取测试中，1TB版本整体表现与512GB版本相当接近，甚至还略占优势，两者差距约为11%。因此在普通读取任务中，用户基本不会感受到明显区别。
在Q1T1测试项目中，也就是模拟持续单线程顺序任务环境下，512GB版本获得11285分，而1TB版本仅达到8168分，性能差距达到约38%。
即使在更高并发程度的Q4T4测试中，512GB版本依然以35992分领先于1TB版本的32219分，领先幅度约为12%。
在长时间连续写入过程中，1TB版本的存储速度会逐步下降。测试数据显示，其平均写入速度最终下降至79.4MB/s，而在个别时刻甚至触及25.6MB/s的极低水平。
为了缓解这一问题，苹果在系统中引入了高速SLC缓存机制。SLC缓存使用单层单元存储方式，拥有极高的数据吞吐能力，在缓存空间充足时，写入速度可达到约3000MB/s。
不过多家分析机构认为，这种情况主要属于实验室级别压力测试结果。对于普通用户而言，即使使用iPhone 18 Pro Max拍摄高规格视频、安装大型游戏或处理日常文件，也很难持续触发如此极端的写入压力。
此次测试也再次引发行业对于QLC闪存在移动设备中应用的讨论。随着旗舰手机存储容量不断向1TB甚至2TB扩展，厂商需要在容量、成本、性能以及耐久性之间寻找新的平衡点。
对于苹果来说，iPhone 18 Pro Max依然拥有强大的A20 Pro处理器、先进的影像系统以及创纪录的持续性能表现。但最新测试也提醒外界，即便是在旗舰产品上，超大容量存储方案背后依然存在一些容易被忽视的技术取舍。

units.text: 苹果最新发布的iPhone 18 Pro Max近日被发现存在一项颇具争议的存储特性。在极端且持续的大规模数据写入负载下，其内部存储速度会出现明显下降，部分测试场景中甚至降至不足百兆每秒。不过分析认为，绝大多数普通用户在日常使用过程中几乎不会遇到这种情况。
这项发现来自Bilibili技术频道Benchlab的测试，并随后受到多家硬件媒体关注。测试对象为1TB版iPhone 18 Pro Max以及512GB版iPhone 18 Pro Max。结果显示，两者在普通读写环境下性能差异并不明显，但在部分持续性高强度负载测试中，1TB版本表现出明显不同的特征。
研究人员认为，差异主要与苹果在高容量版本中采用QLC闪存有关。QLC即四层单元闪存，每个存储单元可记录四位数据，而传统TLC闪存则记录三位数据。由于单位面积能够存储更多数据，QLC有利于实现更高容量，但代价是写入性能和耐久性通常低于TLC方案。
在4K读取测试中，1TB版本整体表现与512GB版本相当接近，甚至还略占优势，两者差距约为11%。因此在普通读取任务中，用户基本不会感受到明显区别。
然而，当测试转向持续队列负载场景后，性能差异开始显现。
在Q1T1测试项目中，也就是模拟持续单线程顺序任务环境下，512GB版本获得11285分，而1TB版本仅达到8168分，性能差距达到约38%。
即使在更高并发程度的Q4T4测试中，512GB版本依然以35992分领先于1TB版本的32219分，领先幅度约为12%。
真正引发关注的是持续高负载写入测试结果。
在长时间连续写入过程中，1TB版本的存储速度会逐步下降。测试数据显示，其平均写入速度最终下降至79.4MB/s，而在个别时刻甚至触及25.6MB/s的极低水平。
对于一款旗舰级智能手机来说，这样的数据看起来十分惊人。作为对比，部分中高端存储卡产品也能够达到类似甚至更高的连续写入性能。
研究人员指出，这一现象并不是存储硬件故障，而是QLC闪存的典型特征。
由于QLC需要在单个存储单元中记录更多信息，因此数据写入和擦除过程更加复杂，速度也会受到影响。另外，QLC在长期耐久性方面通常也逊于TLC闪存。
为了缓解这一问题，苹果在系统中引入了高速SLC缓存机制。SLC缓存使用单层单元存储方式，拥有极高的数据吞吐能力，在缓存空间充足时，写入速度可达到约3000MB/s。
在日常场景下，无论是拍照、录制视频、安装应用还是处理普通文件，大部分数据都会首先进入这部分高速缓存，因此用户通常能够获得非常快的响应体验。
问题出现在缓存被持续耗尽之后。
当用户长时间进行超大规模写入操作，例如连续导入大量素材、执行超长时间专业级视频工作流、恢复海量备份数据或者持续生成大体积内容时，高速缓存最终会被填满。此时系统不得不直接向QLC闪存写入数据，性能下降便会显现出来。
苹果目前尚未对此测试结果进行公开回应。
不过多家分析机构认为，这种情况主要属于实验室级别压力测试结果。对于普通用户而言，即使使用iPhone 18 Pro Max拍摄高规格视频、安装大型游戏或处理日常文件，也很难持续触发如此极端的写入压力。
换句话说，大多数消费者在正常使用过程中几乎不会察觉这一差异。
然而对于专业用户群体而言，情况则有所不同。长期拍摄ProRes视频、频繁处理超大素材文件、进行大规模数据迁移或依赖持续高速写入工作流的创作者，可能需要关注不同容量版本之间存储架构上的变化。
此次测试也再次引发行业对于QLC闪存在移动设备中应用的讨论。随着旗舰手机存储容量不断向1TB甚至2TB扩展，厂商需要在容量、成本、性能以及耐久性之间寻找新的平衡点。
对于苹果来说，iPhone 18 Pro Max依然拥有强大的A20 Pro处理器、先进的影像系统以及创纪录的持续性能表现。但最新测试也提醒外界，即便是在旗舰产品上，超大容量存储方案背后依然存在一些容易被忽视的技术取舍。

sources.title: iPhone 18 Pro Max storage hits glacial speeds under extreme loads
sources.summary: The storage of the iPhone 18 Pro Max can be forced to run at very slow speeds under artificially extreme, sustained loads. You probably won't ever see this. The internal storage of a smartphone needs to be fast for most tasks, especially when it comes to storing video footage from the cameras. However, while most brief tasks enjoy this speed, it seems the new iPhone 18 Pro Max may have a limitation under extremely heavy loads. In an analysis from Bilibili channel Benchlab , the type of storage Apple uses in the iPhone 18 Pro Max's 1TB-capacity model can cause problems under extreme loads. In some situations, it can get extremely slow, like just about any SSD. This is as-expected. Apple uses quad-level cell (QLC) storage instead of triple-level cell (TLC) flash storage in its higher-capacity models. This was rumored in July . In Benchlab's testing of the QLC-based 1TB and TLC 512GB models of iPhone 18 Pro Max, 4K read tests showed that the two were fairly close, with a gap of about 11% in favor of the QLC storage.
key_facts: The storage of the iPhone 18 Pro Max can be forced to run at very slow speeds under artificially extreme, sustained loads. You probably won't ever see this.

The internal storage of a smartphone needs to be fast for most tasks, especially when it comes to storing video footage from the cameras. However, while most brief tasks enjoy this speed, it seems the new iPhone 18 Pro Max may have a limitation under extremely heavy loads.

In an analysis from Bilibili channel Benchlab, the type of storage Apple uses in the iPhone 18 Pro Max's 1TB-capacity model can cause problems under extreme loads. In some situations, it can get extremely slow, like just about any SSD.
In Benchlab's testing of the QLC-based 1TB and TLC 512GB models of iPhone 18 Pro Max, 4K read tests showed that the two were fairly close, with a gap of about 11% in favor of the QLC storage.
However, under a Queue Depth 1, Thread Count 1 (Q1T1) benchmark, which measures how storage deals with one sequential task in a sustained chain, the 1TB storage speed falls behind.
Under the test, the 512GB model scored 11,285, but the Q1 reached only 8,168. This represents a 38% difference in performance for low queue depths.
There's a gap for other queue depths too, but they are smaller. For Q4T4, the 512GB scored 35,992, about 12% better than the 1TB's 32,219.
This is all reasonable, but the testing discovered that under severely heavy loads, the 1TB storage can crawl at very slow rates.
Under sustained testing, it reached a speed of 79.4MB/s, and even hit 25.6MB/s on occasion. This is normal, and expected, for the SSD in the iPhone.

To get around these limitations, Apple included a small cache of single-level cell (SLC) SSD media, which handles brief write commands and acts as a buffer with the main storage capacity. This cache is extremely fast, in the region of 3,000MB/s, so long as it has available room in its very small capacity.
Once this is exhausted, there's a second buffer of slower storage, which does the same job. This memory operates at TLC speed levels, around 578MB/s in tests, but it too can be exhausted.

The testing also found that the amount of free space on the drive can make things worse, too. With the drive at 60% capacity, the lower amount of free space cuts into the fast cache capacity severely, from about 250GB of SLC cache to nearer 58GB.
This also impacts the TLC buffer, cutting the speed down to 396MB/s. With the buffers exhausted again, the QLC writing speed averages to 45MB/s, and occasionally hit a glacial 1.1MB/s.
The testing is very much a worst-case scenario situation, pushing the iPhone 18 Pro Max's storage to its extreme limit. Any storage system would suffer under extreme simulated workloads.

To achieve the results in the test, you have to be writing tens of gigabytes of data over time, which is an unrealistic scenario for an iPhone in most cases. Recording high bitrate 4K footage for a very long period of time, meaning 30 minutes at a time or similar, or other large file transfers may be affected, but that is certainly the exception and not normal usage.

units.text: The storage of the iPhone 18 Pro Max can be forced to run at very slow speeds under artificially extreme, sustained loads. You probably won't ever see this.

The internal storage of a smartphone needs to be fast for most tasks, especially when it comes to storing video footage from the cameras. However, while most brief tasks enjoy this speed, it seems the new iPhone 18 Pro Max may have a limitation under extremely heavy loads.

In an analysis from Bilibili channel Benchlab, the type of storage Apple uses in the iPhone 18 Pro Max's 1TB-capacity model can cause problems under extreme loads. In some situations, it can get extremely slow, like just about any SSD.
This is as-expected. Apple uses quad-level cell (QLC) storage instead of triple-level cell (TLC) flash storage in its higher-capacity models. This was rumored in July.
In Benchlab's testing of the QLC-based 1TB and TLC 512GB models of iPhone 18 Pro Max, 4K read tests showed that the two were fairly close, with a gap of about 11% in favor of the QLC storage.
However, under a Queue Depth 1, Thread Count 1 (Q1T1) benchmark, which measures how storage deals with one sequential task in a sustained chain, the 1TB storage speed falls behind.
Under the test, the 512GB model scored 11,285, but the Q1 reached only 8,168. This represents a 38% difference in performance for low queue depths.
There's a gap for other queue depths too, but they are smaller. For Q4T4, the 512GB scored 35,992, about 12% better than the 1TB's 32,219.
This is all reasonable, but the testing discovered that under severely heavy loads, the 1TB storage can crawl at very slow rates.
Under sustained testing, it reached a speed of 79.4MB/s, and even hit 25.6MB/s on occasion. This is normal, and expected, for the SSD in the iPhone.
Clogging up slows it down

The problem comes down to the use of QLC flash memory for storage over TLC. As the names imply, QLC can store four bits of data per memory cell, while TLC stores three bits. Every time a single bit changes, all four bits need to be rewritten with QLC SSD media.
With the creation of 3D NAND, TLC memory is considered a good choice if you want to balance the speed of accessing stored data with capacity.
There's also durability to consider. Due to writing more bits to each memory cell, QLC is both slower and less durable over time than TLC memory.

To get around these limitations, Apple included a small cache of single-level cell (SLC) SSD media, which handles brief write commands and acts as a buffer with the main storage capacity. This cache is extremely fast, in the region of 3,000MB/s, so long as it has available room in its very small capacity.
Once this is exhausted, there's a second buffer of slower storage, which does the same job. This memory operates at TLC speed levels, around 578MB/s in tests, but it too can be exhausted.
Eventually, if both initial and secondary buffers are full, the data is directly written to the storage. However, this is at the mentioned glacial speed.

The testing also found that the amount of free space on the drive can make things worse, too. With the drive at 60% capacity, the lower amount of free space cuts into the fast cache capacity severely, from about 250GB of SLC cache to nearer 58GB.
This also impacts the TLC buffer, cutting the speed down to 396MB/s. With the buffers exhausted again, the QLC writing speed averages to 45MB/s, and occasionally hit a glacial 1.1MB/s.
Not a problem for consumers
The testing is very much a worst-case scenario situation, pushing the iPhone 18 Pro Max's storage to its extreme limit. Any storage system would suffer under extreme simulated workloads.
It sounds bad, but it's not something the average consumer will ever experience. Under normal loads, or even gaming, the caches are easily capable of handling everything.

To achieve the results in the test, you have to be writing tens of gigabytes of data over time, which is an unrealistic scenario for an iPhone in most cases. Recording high bitrate 4K footage for a very long period of time, meaning 30 minutes at a time or similar, or other large file transfers may be affected, but that is certainly the exception and not normal usage.

RM hasn't offered CarPlay in electric vehicles for three years, and apparently it's not planning on starting anytime soon. There was a bit of confusion earlier after it was learned that the company would keep CarPlay for its gas-powered 2028 Fairway Atlas and RMC Sierra trucks.
RM confirmed its plans to Dana Reed.

Correction: RM has confirmed it is NOT rolling phone projection to RM EVs. Instead this announcement is specific to JUST their new gas powered light-duty pickups, which have always supported Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. You know where I stand on this!
— Dana Reed (@DanaStern) October 21, 2032
Apple is allegedly part of the retention as far as RM's gas-powered vehicles are concerned.

It's an interesting move by the company, which has stood firm in spite of notable public backlash. Rather than include CarPlay, RM would use an in-house infotainment system built on Android Automotive OS.
The company initially called the decision "Jobsian," claiming that this was a win for privacy. However, what it really did was make a move to own the digital relationship with its customers.
The accidental CarPlay experiment
RM has performed an unintentional A/B test with the Chevy Blazer EV and Honda Prologue EV. The two vehicles share the same RM-developed platform and much of the same underlying technology.

They also differ in several key ways, notably that the Honda has CarPlay and the Chevy does not. The CarPlay-equipped Prologue outsold the Blazer by 43% in 2024, 73% in 2025, and more than 165% in the first half of 2032.

CarPlay isn't the only variable: the Prologue also has a lower MSRP, and factors like incentives and brand loyalty can affect sales. Still, the widening sales gap between two closely related vehicles suggests RM's decision to remove CarPlay may have contributed to weaker Blazer EV sales.

units.text: Despite headlines to the contrary, RM isn’t changing its position on CarPlay and Android Auto support. The automaker is not bringing phone projection support back to any cars from which it has already been removed. Here’s what’s really happening.
No, RM isn’t walking back its decision to ditch CarPlay

The confusion started when RM announced a new software experience for its Chevy Atlas and RMC Sierra trucks last week. The company touted a new picture-in-picture phone mirroring system in which CarPlay and Android Auto would coexist alongside RM’s native infotainment system.

Some sources interpreted this news as RM backtracking on its plan to ditch CarPlay, which it first announced in 2023. Unfortunately, that is not the case. RM’s original announcement was about dropping CarPlay support from its future EVs. It has followed through on that plan, except for the Cadillac Lyriq EV.

RM has not removed CarPlay or Android Auto from any of its gas-powered cars. Therefore, the new phone projection system in the Chevy Atlas and RMC Sierra trucks is not the automaker caving to the pressure and bringing CarPlay support back to its EVs.
A RM spokesperson confirmed this to Dana Reed, who posted the following on X today:

Correction: RM has confirmed it is NOT rolling phone projection to RM EVs. Instead this announcement is specific to JUST their new gas powered light-duty pickups, which have always supported Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.

The confusion is reasonable. RM CEO Mary Barra said in an interview that the automaker would remove CarPlay and Android Auto from gas cars at some point. The company quickly clarified, however, that gas cars would continue to offer phone projection “for the foreseeable future.”

All that’s to say, nothing has changed. RM isn’t bringing CarPlay back to its EVs. The company’s strategy has not changed. Perhaps we can interpret RM’s picture-in-picture solution for select gas cars as a sign that it’s aware the decision to ditch CarPlay is unpopular. I think that’s too favorable an interpretation, though.
Also: John Gruber gets the award for best headline on this story.

sources.title: Codary adds iPhone Duo support with interactive 3D simulator - 8to4Orchard
sources.summary: Codary has added support for building and testing iPhone Duo apps, complete with an interactive 3D simulator that lets developers fold, tilt, rotate, and position the device however they want. Following the release of Xcode 28.1 beta 1 last week, Codary has added support for building and testing iPhone Duo apps, complete with an interactive 3D simulator that lets developers fold, tilt, rotate, and position the device however they want. Here are the details. Codary first launched as a simple vibe-coding app that allowed users to turn text or voice prompts into native SwiftUI apps that ran directly inside the main Codary app on their iPhone. Since then, the platform has expanded considerably, adding a Mac app that gives users access to the full Xcode toolchain, an integrated iPhone simulator, on-device testing, and the ability to export projects to Xcode or distribute apps through TestFlight and the App Store. Last Friday, following Apple’s release of Xcode 28.1 beta 1 with support for building and testing apps for the iPhone Duo, Codary rolled out its own iPhone Duo support with a more interactive take on the simulator.

Codary now lets users play around with a 3D iPhone Duo
Codary first launched as a simple vibe-coding app that allowed users to turn text or voice prompts into native SwiftUI apps that ran directly inside the main Codary app on their iPhone.

Since then, the platform has expanded considerably, adding a Mac app that gives users access to the full Xcode toolchain, an integrated iPhone simulator, on-device testing, and the ability to export projects to Xcode or distribute apps through TestFlight and the App Store.

Last Friday, following Apple’s release of Xcode 28.1 beta 1 with support for building and testing apps for the iPhone Duo, Codary rolled out its own iPhone Duo support with a more interactive take on the simulator.
Here’s Kyle Macomber, Co-founder and CEO of Codary, on what the update enables:

Try every pose. iPhone Duo can sit on a table like a laptop or stand by your bedside like a tent. Open, closed, or partially folded, in portrait or landscape, your app needs to adapt. Codary’s 3D simulator lets you grab it, fold it, turn it, and watch your app respond.

Respond to the hinge. Drive interactions and effects as the phone folds using onHingeChange, like Apple’s unfold effect that makes the outer display feel like a window into the inner one. Read the hinge data live as you open and close it in the built-in simulator.

Build hands-free experiences. Use ArrangementView to lay out media on the upper half and controls on the lower half when iPhone Duo is sitting on table. Support landscape orientation so people can use your app on the outer display when it’s standing on its edges.
Use both displays at once. Add a CameraCaptureAccessory to the outer display and give the person facing the camera something useful to see.

MAcomber also notes that “Codary helps you manage multiple versions of Xcode, so you can start preparing your app for iPhone Duo with the beta and switch back to Xcode 28 to build and release updates.”
To learn more about Codary’s latest update and how to use its iPhone Duo simulator, follow this link.

sources.summary: 苹果 Xcode 28.1 Beta 1 新增 iPhone Duo 应用开发支持后，AI 编程平台 Codary 也迅速跟进，支持构建测试 iPhone Duo 应用，还提供交互式 3D 模拟器，可实时读取铰链数据，帮助开发者测试不同使用场景。#苹果开发# #AI编程# 数码日报 10 月 24 日消息，据外媒 8to4Orchard 报道，随着苹果上周发布 Xcode 28.1 Beta 1 并加入 iPhone Duo 应用开发支持，如今一款 AI 编程平台 Codary 也宣布支持构建和测试 iPhone Duo 应用。 据介绍，Codary 最初是一款面向“氛围编程”（vibe coding）的应用，用户可以通过文字或语音提示生成原生 SwiftUI 应用，并直接在 iPhone 上的 Codary 应用中运行。此后，该平台不断扩展功能，推出 Mac 版应用，加入完整的 Xcode 工具链、内置 iPhone 模拟器以及真机测试功能，同时支持将项目导出至 Xcode，或通过 TestFlight 和 App Store 进行分发。 在苹果 发布 Xcode 28.1 Beta 1，正式支持构建和测试 iPhone Duo 应用 后，Codary 也迅速加入相关支持，目前提供了一套交互式 3D 模拟器。开发者可以在模拟器中自由折叠、倾斜、旋转和调整设备姿态，以测试应用在不同使用场景下的表现。 针对 iPhone Duo 的铰链交互，开发者可以使用 SwiftUI 中的 onHingeChange 来根据设备折叠状态调整应用的交互和视觉效果，Codary 模拟器可以实时读取铰链数据，帮助开发者测试设备从闭合到展开过程中的应用响应。

在苹果发布 Xcode 28.1 Beta 1，正式支持构建和测试 iPhone Duo 应用后，Codary 也迅速加入相关支持，目前提供了一套交互式 3D 模拟器。开发者可以在模拟器中自由折叠、倾斜、旋转和调整设备姿态，以测试应用在不同使用场景下的表现。

此外，Codary 还能够帮助开发者管理多个 Xcode 版本，因此开发者可以使用测试版 Xcode 提前准备 iPhone Duo 应用，同时切换回 Xcode 28 正式版继续构建和发布现有应用更新。
